$comment: Voice: written from inside the crawl. Events as events, in the dungeon's own vocabulary. Never 'in book 4 Carl does X', never 'the series', never 'four books later' — the reader's position is the gate's job, not the prose's. confidence: 'verified' = drawn from the Fandom wiki's chapter record or an entity page. 'draft' = written from reading knowledge, awaiting a pass.

entities.name: Carl
entities.tagline: Twenty-seven. Coast Guard, marine technician. I went outside for a cigarette, and that is the only reason I'm alive. I'm not sure it counts as a reason.
entities.voiceNote: Deadpan, first person, understated. Notices the practical detail first (footwear, inventory, what will explode) and the feeling second, if at all. Gallows humour, never grandiose, never asks for sympathy. Says Donut, Mordecai, the AI. Swears in the crawl; here he keeps it to hell and damn. Talks like a man narrating a repair job while the building is on fire.

beats.headline: January 3rd, 2:23 in the morning
beats.text: I crack the window of my apartment in Seattle for a cigarette. That's it. That's the whole decision. Donut, who is my ex-girlfriend's show cat and not mine in any way I agreed to, goes out through it and up the tree, and I go after her into the freezing dark in my leather jacket, boxers and Bea's pink Crocs, with a Zippo and half a pack of Marlboro Reds. Mrs Parsons leans out to ask about the noise. Then every building on the planet comes down at once, and everyone who stayed inside one is gone.

beats.headline: Dressed for nothing, and stuck that way
beats.text: An hour past the stairs and I have a Goblin Pass Tattoo on my left forearm, a Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling, a Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness clipped to the jacket and a Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. What I do not have is shoes. I have asked. The dungeon has heard me ask, and the dungeon has an opinion about it.

beats.headline: The footwear situation does not improve
beats.text: The second floor finally addresses my feet. It hands me an Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. So now I am still barefoot, but my feet are shiny and they glitter, and the audience has noticed, and the audience does not let things go.

beats.headline: Primal, and a Compensated Anarchist
beats.text: Class selection, on the way into the Over City. I take Primal for the race and a monk-rogue hybrid nobody has picked before, and the AI writes me up as "a trapmaking, bomb-making, social-media dynamo" who "will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next." I'd argue with it if I could think of the argument.

beats.headline: The twenty-fifth holder of the Cookbook
beats.text: Twenty-four crawlers carried this before me. Different seasons, different species, worlds that aren't there any more. Whatever I do from here, I'm finishing somebody else's work, and most of them never got to finish theirs.

beats.headline: The explosives chapter first
beats.text: The book is sorted into chapters: potions in one, explosives in another, and a list of monsters and what they are weak to. Some of the people who wrote in it filled pages. Some managed a line. I go to the explosives first, obviously, and the first note that catches my eye is about infusing bombs at a sapper’s table.

beats.headline: He worships a god to survive a plane crash
beats.text: I am falling out of the sky and Quan Ch is about to finish the job. So I take Emberus as my patron, mid-air, and throw a celestial grenade. The god arrives at my position, and for a little while nothing can kill me. Then Emberus finds Orthrus, and both of them are gone.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds are opening and I take the bomb-focused specialisation. Agent Provocateur. I would like to be very, very good at exactly one thing, and I have picked the thing.

beats.headline: Zockau burns
beats.text: Zockau burns. I mark hunters with the Ring of Divine Suffering, I kill them, and I take their stats, and enough of them are inside the Desperado Club when it goes that the survivors have to be dug out. I get hurt on the way out. That part is fair.

beats.headline: He takes command of one of nine armies
beats.text: Thirty days. A castle at Larracos, dead centre of the map. No coming back from a death on this floor, for anyone. Supply, alliances, atrocity, at a scale where the arithmetic stops being about people I know.

beats.headline: Five thousand five hundred and one
beats.text: Five thousand five hundred and one. Seventy-five per cent of us took deals, and the relief I feel about that is enormous and secondhand. Every one of them earned it. Then the message I knew was coming: Justice Light, "I am not sorry," from a deceased mercenary. Quasar has already told me the Nothing is broken, the club on the eighteenth floor is inside an awake Scolopendra, and the guests there can neither eject nor die. I have a garage, two gremlins in overalls and four minutes on a countdown. I will not be taking that way out.

beats.headline: The wheel lands on a food truck
beats.text: The wheel ticks past a school bus, the Popemobile, a missile launcher and something that is either a floor polisher or a Zamboni, and settles on a box truck with windows. A food truck. Big Shot Chicken, the 1920s-gangster chain whose safe room Donut and I sat out the rage elemental in. Chrome fenders, a fiberglass nose built to sit at a state fair, and a giant plastic tommy gun on the roof whose drum magazine blocks half the windshield. No passenger seat. I turn the key and there is an engine. Good. I drive.

beats.headline: Only driving
beats.text: Seventy miles an hour down a black road in the dark, slumped low to see under the plastic gun, and Mongo pukes on the dashboard. And for a minute it is almost peaceful. If I make a mistake here, I die, Donut dies, and that is all. Nobody else. After the armies of the last floor I could cry at how small that is. It does not hold. Donut keeps wiping her paw on things and I keep not looking. Katia is out and free. Justice Light showed there is also the possibility of vengeance. First we have to survive this floor.

beats.headline: We tow them in
beats.text: The Trauco Triplets are eliminated the moment their mount dies. One team gone. The next one down is a red Pontiac minivan on its side and burning, with two bugbears trying to save it. If they go too, Prepotente's arithmetic says we race our friends. So Donut drops the manatee, I make fire hoses out of a bucket and a kitchen bowl with water scrolls, and when the van is plainly finished I tell them the truth and start building a flatbed. They are awake, they are scared, and they want to be free. The next race is the next race.

beats.headline: A catalogue of weapons
beats.text: Hedy hands me a tablet with over a thousand upgrades, and I scroll past the hover and the climbing tires into the weapons. A barrel of spikes like the goblin murder dozer. A flamethrower. A pulse that shuts down other drivers. A brick wall you drop on the road behind you. We can maybe avoid killing other teams. We cannot stop them killing each other, and Zhang says Li Na has already killed most of her heat. Crawler against crawler is coming. I start thinking about a driving rig Katia could build, and then I remember. I pick the spider legs.

beats.headline: Come to Daddy
beats.text: Most of my achievements are leftovers from the end of Faction Wars. Bomb's Away, for emptying my inventory in midair without aiming any of it. Wastrel, for feeding Frank Q's ring to a cat, reward withheld in terms I won't repeat. And Come to Daddy, for rejecting the exit deal, written like the AI is about to cry. I'm not like the ungrateful ones running off the playground. Good boy. The Gold Payload Box holds a skill potion that doubles my hotlist. No celestial this time. Then there is the fan box, and I already know what's in it.

beats.headline: We don't tell Dong
beats.text: The half-mantaur in the gimp suit waves at us before his garage door comes down, and Donut names him before I do. Dong's friend. Corcunda. They put him here to mess with us, and the way to handle that kind of drama is never to step in it in the first place. So we don't tell Dong. I say that out loud, which is my mistake. The air ripples. New quest: reunite them, part one of two, and part two needs his other half and a fleshmancer. Reward: two stand-ins of our choosing, sent to the arena on the eleventh floor.

beats.headline: Who goes to the arena
beats.text: Kill certain mobs on this floor and the audience votes. One way, the mob survives and is sent to the arena. The other way, a stand-in goes instead, and the stand-ins are people from outside the dungeon, like the guests at the resort on the eighteenth floor. The arena is on the eleventh floor, and nobody knows anything beyond that. I can't stop thinking about it. The AI dragged Princess Formidable off her own spaceship. Could I pick someone in orbit? A liaison like Harbinger? Prime Minister Victory? Who could I send down there who would do the most damage?

beats.headline: The truck will not be modified
beats.text: Fifteen minutes to the line. I stand in the passenger door and try to tear the tommy gun off the roof with my bare hands, and the dungeon informs me I may not change the stock configuration of my vehicle. Fine. The driver is a crocodile who has driven a cart, the GPS threatens to drown him in a swamp, and the freezer in the back refills itself every ten seconds. Then Zhang's message lands. Tran's team is in his heat. And so it begins.

beats.headline: Black and White at the start line
beats.text: The plan was one kill: Donut roots the womantaur driver with a Danforth bolt, Chiyome's bear does the rest, and nobody else dies, because if a second team goes, all of it was for nothing. Then the hail takes the awning off, Team Sparkles puts a cannon through the car in front of us, Donut never fires, and our one kill is somebody else's. The bugbears' van is playing "Black and White". My mom loved that song. For a moment I just sit there and listen.

beats.headline: There will always be clues
beats.text: Two province bosses, level 170, squatting on the road like kangaroos that grew spikes, with pouches full of dead joeys and one live engineer wearing a joey. Chiyome sets the other one's pouch alight and it pulls out a burning razor fox, eats him, and heals to full. Its only weak spot is inside the pouch. So I ask Donut to examine the dead joeys. Starvation. And their inventory is just their skin. A skin. There will always be clues.

beats.headline: Into the pouch
beats.text: Genesis was supposed to hook me a dead joey. She hooks the engineer through the face instead, so I peel the joey skin off his corpse: protection from acid, a jump skill, twelve hours on the clock, and I cannot walk in it, only hop. So I hop, onto the boss's pouch, and he shoves me in himself. Down through the goo to the bottom, two satchels dropped, then out again on Gloom Wraith Phase and the detonator in the air. It works. A gremlin drops his toolbox on me. I probably deserved that.

beats.headline: Barely responsible for myself
beats.text: Last place, and alive because another team died first. No fuss, no epic fight: we'd just be gone. I lie on the garage floor in a dead kangaroo and look at the gremlin's blood on the ceiling. I thought I was relieved not to be responsible for so many people any more. Now I'm barely responsible for myself. It feels like the day my father put his motorcycle helmet through the fish tank, and every molly died, no matter what I did.

beats.headline: Everything is connected, somehow
beats.text: Akuma. He killed Stalwart, stole the Gate, and left me to deal with Agatha. Now he wants two teams dead and hasn't said why, so I won't do it, not deliberately. The Pineapple Cabaret I've heard once: the AI, wearing Growler Gary, offered "Backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret" to Formidable as a place of banishment, and every place on that list was bad. Samantha's daughter. The Scavenger. Emberus and Geyrun. Prepotente's crystal. It's all connected, and I have no idea what any of it means.

beats.headline: He asks it on live
beats.text: The goats of the Plenty sentence us to death and then take questions. One explains what Justice did: broke the Nothing and let everything inside it loose into three levels. Then Orren and Victory are in my chat, wanting me to ask about the integrity of the tunnels in their exact words. I rephrase. Does the public know the gods have escaped? That the AI is in their tunnels? That they're in worse danger than us? That they need to run? Out loud. The AI lets it go out.

beats.headline: Too dangerous for the herd
beats.text: Victory tells me that was reckless. Please. They knew exactly what would happen when they asked me. The goats stampede out through the wall, and the one who stays, Gamori, the matriarch, judges me: rash, impulsive, loud, a troublemaker, too dangerous to walk amongst the herd. So I ask why they're even here. She bursts into tears. They sponsored us at their partner's behest. The kids love us. I'm best friends with their champion. She knew all of it and told nobody.

beats.headline: Glue and foam
beats.text: Ninety seconds of invulnerability, twenty minutes, thirty kilometres straight down. I swing the two ghoul cages out on Hedy's booms and fire the eight-pack: four Denial of Service missiles at One Fine Pig, four at Team Sparkles. They don't explode. They glue. Three bury the unicorn's shield in green mucus and the bush goes spinning in circles. Then the sugar hermits come in twenty-foot waves, the ghouls throw Biscuit Packs, foam that sets like rock, and Donut puts up a wall of fire a mile long.

beats.headline: Feet first into the skull
beats.text: Gluteus is out cold on the wheel with a three-storey beetle skull between us and the finish. I grab the wheel, which means I've driven. Donut takes the pedals. I climb out through the windshield, lie on my back on the hood, activate Daughter's Kiss and aim my kangaroo feet at the skull. Then Dwight's cannon hits us, and the truck, the GTO and the bush all go over the line spinning together. The suit shreds against the road. Both arms, both legs, the pelvis. First place.

beats.headline: Triple the price, and he pays it
beats.text: Rosetta and Tipid bring in team Helix: a Grulke named Olga, a Porsuk named Finley with poison on his claws, and a fire fairy named Quemada, three mercenaries for the price of one. They have raced two heats already. Quemada takes one look at the Emberus shrine in the back of the room and decides the fee is now triple. Rosetta says the price was settled with the guild. I ask whether they drove in the last races. Two of them drive. We'll pay the price.

beats.headline: Four ways out of the Emberus problem
beats.text: The Kill Hellik quest has been sitting in the back of my head and I have not planned for it, which is a mistake. The options: kill Hellik, and Emberus has told me to my face he will kill me for it. Don't kill Hellik, or leave the church, and I get smitten. Or kill Emberus, whom I cannot get near without burning to dust, and then every other god wants me dead. Now Eris wants me to ditch him for her. I grab her coin and it burns a swirl into my palm.

beats.headline: An idea he will not say in chat
beats.text: Eris is gone and my heart will not slow down. I write everything into my notes: the four sides of the coin, Britney and the pickaxe, Florin, the Pineapple Cabaret. I have to close the eye on my chest on purpose. We are on rails, playing their game. We have to break it. I have an idea so ridiculous, so completely suicidal, that I dismiss it straight away. Then I tell the group chat everything, and ask them to hear me out on a plan I cannot type the end of.

beats.headline: Trust, but verify
beats.text: I fist-bump Akuma into my chat and leave him on two percent health. He answers nothing except to say I'm annoying. I don't trust him. But Herot, and Eris swearing he has a way out, keep me on the hook. So: gather volunteers who can fight in the Cabaret, have Prepotente and Mordecai work the shop-interface exploit, send some of the strippers back to the Desperado Club for the other way in. Everything still has to fit between races. I miss bouncing around a map.

beats.headline: Fists against an armoured door
beats.text: Finley walked out of our garage to go and find his friends a temple and One Fine Pig ran all three of them into the pavement, then backed up and did it again. I storm their garage. Their gun takes out a wall and a bus. I dent the door with my gauntlet until their shield throws me into the street. Imani and Donut pull me away. I sit on the curb in front of what is left. It was a simple act of defiance, and it was snuffed out.

beats.headline: Two traps, keyed to Tigrans
beats.text: While Donut talks, I lay a hidden trap on each side of their truck, as close to the shield as I dare. Disintegration traps, like the one I pulled off Akuma's door: silent, one target each, and I set them to fire only for a Tigran, so even if one of them is carrying the pig, she is safe. Five seconds. Imani asks how I'm feeling. I tell her I freaked out, that Donut talked me down, and that I have an idea.

beats.headline: One Fine Pig is eliminated
beats.text: Two notifications, one after the other. A Tigran dissolved, then the other. One Fine Pig is out, both racers expired, five teams left. I hold my breath, and nothing comes about Penelope. We have drawn Satan's Water Park, an hour behind team Sparkles, with Florin already on it. We need to win the heat, because the winner gets a key, and we need the key, because we need that pig. Florin asks if there's a team I need slowed down. Let me tell you about a unicorn named Dwight.

beats.headline: Mehmet's page
beats.text: An entry in the Book of Boom from Mehmet Or, level sixty-two, a Sipahi. He owned a bowling alley in Istanbul that his father left him. He killed his pregnant wife in the hydra. He has taken a deal, and he asks me to forgive the cowardice. His daughters, Azra and Yaz, did not step into the light with him, and he thinks they are with the children. If I cannot save him, find them and tell them he loved them. Associated spell: Gutter Bumper. I never met him.

beats.headline: Ice, chains and rodents
beats.text: The River of Sloth is packed with Gingers on inner tubes, and Maurice is somewhere among them. I cast Mehmet's Gutter Bumper along the river, and Donut's Ice Slick follows the lines and freezes the lot solid. We drive over the ice dragging every spare weapon I own on chains behind the truck, then Donut casts Summon Ye, Vermin and the zipper shrews drill through whoever is left, Maurice included. Quest complete. People like Mehmet, who buffed everyone else and saved lives, are the real heroes here.

beats.headline: Asking around about Chachi
beats.text: I send the same question to Rosetta, Mordecai, Tipid and Prepotente at once: who is this Chalchiuhtlicue, and why did my Scavenger's Daughter patch try to go off while I was talking to Lucia? Rosetta says she's a minor goddess of childbirth, water and fire, never sponsored, weak in the Ascendency game. Mordecai says what he always says, which is that nobody knows, this is all new. Donut says we're calling her Chachi. My question stands. If she can get from wherever those kids are to here, can we go the other way?

beats.headline: Trust me on this one
beats.text: Donut wants the whole plan and I can't give it to her yet. The prize is two people of our choosing brought to the eleventh floor, and she's scared I mean to hurt somebody she likes. So I tell her what I can: I'm scared too, and the pig, this quest and the war mage plan will all help us survive. I'll explain once it's too late for them to take the prize away. Then Zhang says what he means to do, and I see it. Li Na can't worship a god. She's a weapon. She just needs pointing. I message Bodi.

beats.headline: It's a go
beats.text: Splash Zone says the casino plan is a bust, so it's the cleaner bots. Li Na's poison won't clear, and it'll get worse, because health tops up on every new floor. If Herot's real and the war mages weren't lying about the Cabaret, getting her through stops that, keeps Zhang alive, stops her killing crawlers, and tests the route before we try it with a crowd. It only works if she agrees. She's too smart to trick, and I wouldn't want to. Everyone at the table is looking at me. "It's a go." Tran bows.

beats.headline: Potions, a scroll, and A-ha
beats.text: I've never sung in my life, except hammered in a bar with a bunch of coasties, years ago. So Mordecai compounds potions to get round the cooldowns, and I'm Honeyed, Yo-Yo Ma'd and Dio'd. There's a scroll called Gelded Choirboy for the notes my voice can't reach. Mordecai insists the name isn't literal. I read it at the last second and sound like I've sucked on a helium balloon. The song is "Take on Me." I take the lead, so Donut's few lines have the better odds. Then the unicorn stabs the DJ.

beats.headline: Singing through a bar fight
beats.text: The DJ's dead, so this is our only shot, and the music keeps going. I sing. Bottles break on me. I kick a gremlin and a Draconian off the stage before they reach Donut, catch her microphone stand between my big and index toe, and bounce off the stage when the curtains go up. I hit the high note and the gauge by my head throws sparks. Permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild, and an achievement, Sing for your supper. The sign over Donut says FAILED. I guess I gotta do this myself.

beats.headline: A running list of gods
beats.text: Jurgen asks a better question than I'd managed: can people who worship gods not go to the Cabaret, or do the war mages just not want them there? Akuma lied to us about needing two teams dead, so he could be lying about this too. I've been keeping a running list of every god I hear of, sorted by affiliation and skill. Donar goes on it: thunder and lightning, like Thor but manlier, not sponsored this season, and he's given Jurgen lightning spells. My heart skips a beat. Then I'm through the door, and the guildmaster is stuck in his own zipper.

beats.headline: He could have been kinder
beats.text: Dong's cursed. Mordecai says the sock has gone, and without it and every nickel the NPCs grabbed, a temple won't help. I gave him that sock. I got it from Quan Ch. The Dominators heard us outside their garage and drove for the starting line with Corky in the back, where we can't touch them. I sit on the curb. Dong's an NPC, and he's my friend, and I could've been a lot less of a jerk about it. So we stop waiting. We join the two halves during the race, and Grigori gets half an hour to learn to drive.

beats.headline: Holding on by his fingers
beats.text: I apologise to Bigs, and then to Dong, because they're right. This floor felt easy at first, on rails, no choices. It isn't. It's a drain for everyone spat out of the bottom of Faction Wars, spinning faster near the hole. I tell Dong he's coming: three mercenary seats, Grigori, Porky and him. But while I'm saying it I think of D'nadia, and of Finley, and the voices under the surface, and the tremor in my hands since Donut's attack in the tower. I'm not on the edge. I've already stepped off. You will not break me.

beats.headline: The rocket button
beats.text: I blow the tommy gun off our roof to clear the windshield, and Osvaldo complains the shrapnel hit them. Inside the factory the containment snaps on; five seconds' contact with anyone else and it merges. The Dominators take a conveyor belt loaded with metal balls toward the melting vats, so we follow. The edge isn't a ramp. It's a drop. I smack the untested rocket button, know within a second it's far too strong, tap it off and steer the Bubble Buddy through the air. We land, run off the side, and the bubble catches us.

beats.headline: Upside down, at speed
beats.text: The next room is a river of molten metal three floors down, so we go sideways up the wall and then upside down onto the ceiling track. Behind me Grigori is vomiting, two half-mantaurs are unzipping, and Dong is wrapping their half brains in the kappa's plastic wrap. Slag elementals jump from the river and throw metal at us, and one blows a hole in the hood. I fold us between the legs of a ferret mount with the trans-dimensional upgrade and pop out ahead. When I look back there's one name over the mantaur. Then a god.

beats.headline: Fifteen seconds to spare
beats.text: Grull wants Corcunda, and Corcunda decides to go to him. Dong pulls out the lance I haven't seen since the day I gave him the sock, and they go out the back of the truck together, and the screws go with them, and the god says it was a good death and vanishes. We skitter through somebody's Hole and cross the line with fifteen seconds left. Fourth place. I can't look back at who didn't make it. We're alive. We won the quest. That was supposed to be the part that mattered most.

beats.headline: What a hero
beats.text: Dong Quixote is dead. I let it sink in. What a way to go. Out of sixty teams in our race, eighteen came through, and there are about three hundred heats of four left. We're getting slaughtered. The quest pays out: two creatures of my choosing brought to the arena on the eleventh floor, the choice made once we're inside it. The AI's note carries a warning about exits that seem too good to be true. Then Mordecai says a single flower has bloomed on the cactus. Li Na made it.

beats.headline: The plan, in the stables
beats.text: We meet in the pet stables, because Rosetta says a guild add-on room has a bug and the gods can't hear what's said in it. The numbers: two heats left, about two hundred people going to the Cabaret, and by Mordecai's math we need fifteen hundred more to take deals to keep the crawler-on-crawler races down. Only volunteers who've stayed human and don't worship a god can go. And me: Hellik has to be dead before the eleventh floor ends or Emberus smites me, so I'm leaving the party. Donut isn't speaking to me.

beats.headline: Who killed Geyrun
beats.text: My quest is to find out who murdered Geyrun, Emberus's son. Samantha was there when someone was hired to do it, and her memory is spotty. One of the four sons of Sheol may be involved, and Amayon claims to know who did it. I'm building a family tree of gods in my scratch pad, and I miss Katia badly; she'd have had this worked out. I think it's the key to all of it. I think the AI wants it solved and doesn't know the answer either. I have a very loose theory. Not nearly enough.

beats.headline: Is this truly the only way
beats.text: On the walk into Hungry Eyes Village, Donut asks me whether this is truly the only way. I think so. We're all dying, and every floor takes away a little more of our ability to fight back. The Emberus quest to kill Hellik is due. Mordecai says it could backfire the way it did for Drakea, when the Nagas cheated. It could. But the showrunners aren't in control anymore, and the AI, crazy as it is, still follows the rules. Eris wants devotion, not worship. That's a trap. She has the right idea, though.

beats.headline: Tempered in the fires of hell
beats.text: I raise my tea to all of them: the ones escaping, the ones taking a deal after the next heat, the ones staying for whatever comes after. We aren't perfect. This floor keeps making us turn on each other, and heat seven is three teams and one survivor. But these people are my family. Then Elle springs the trap on Linus, and I keep my hand on his neck. You keep trying to divide us, I tell him. We've been tempered in the fires of hell. You've already lost. All that's left is the wreckage settling.

beats.headline: If he could slip in
beats.text: Everyone thought the Linus thing was a joke. It rattled me, because I was one of the last to notice anything fishy, and I pride myself on noticing. If he could slip in, who else is out there? The AI stopped Harbinger cold. Not every attempt will be so clumsy. And we still have our own strife: Osvaldo, and Agatha, who has simply disappeared. Our new mercenary is a Zebani cartographer, which reminds me of a dead crawler who accused me of killing her father. Just another mystery.

beats.headline: Crossed-out eyes
beats.text: Archie Mu's apartment: his wife, Mackenzie, screaming on a chair, their boy alive in the photographs. Her eyes are X'd out. His aren't. The boy's aren't. I think I've got it. Crossed-out eyes mean dead. Then we drive through and the loop breaks, and she starts pulling at her stitches. One floor down it's Imani's family, a man seizing on the carpet while everyone watches, and when her mother tears her eyes open, beetles pour out. The AI said it was done with this. I tell the ceiling exactly what I think of that.

beats.headline: Forgive me, friends
beats.text: Jurgen needs help on the first floor, and Osvaldo says he's about to cross the line. That could put us last. So I open the Primed tab and find the detonator. Earlier, Samantha distracted the two bugbears while I used Oozy Form for the first time and swapped one of their peach beers for a can I'd drilled out and filled. It hides from anything under level twelve Find Traps. Forgive me, friends. I click it. They were NPCs. They were our friends. At least it's not another crawler.

beats.headline: Under a thousand left
beats.text: Imani's count: under a thousand of us. We started this floor at fifty-five hundred. A little over two hundred went to the Cabaret. Then a voice I've never heard, Damien, some behind-the-scenes lifer, tells us to take a deal, promises the garages and hired NPCs transfer down, and gives us ninety minutes on arrival to build a parade float. Donut gasps with delight. Imani, meanwhile, is running the entire upgrade-stealing operation. That assassin was right to target her. Look for the helpers.

beats.headline: The draw undoes everything
beats.text: For the first time we can see the other heats across the lobby. One is team Yokai against two NPC teams, all three NPCs, so they're allowing that now, and every calculation we made is worthless. Then the next two heats, side by side. A Cadillac, Imani and Elle's APV, and Chris's red semi. A gecko, an NPC sedan, and Florin's moped with Lucia on the back. Chris against Imani. Louis and Britney against Florin and Lucia. Everything we did to keep our circle alive, undone in one moment.

beats.headline: Red, and four legs
beats.text: Everyone in the truck gets a second wheel: mostly green, a sliver of red. Donut, green. Jamal, green. Samantha, who has no business being in the truck, green. Mine ticks past the green and stops on red. A level twenty Transformation spell. I black out for five seconds and wake up smaller, able to smell everything, including the frozen chicken patties, which smell delicious. Quadruped actions menu. Donut is suddenly huge and hissing at me. Samantha asks if she can pet me. I bark.

beats.headline: Contingency three
beats.text: The messaging spells my name with a K now. A notice nearly slips past in the chaos: Pontiff has left the playing field and is no longer my mercenary. That's the idea. I know why this heat is four hours and why we can leave the blocks. Mordecai says the garden is intact. Contingency three, I tell everyone with more than one crawler team in their heat. It's a bad idea. I beg Osvaldo one last time, and he tells me to go fuck myself. Forgive me. The light goes green.

beats.headline: Poleaxes, all the way up
beats.text: I designed them on the last floor and never got to use them: poleaxes. Focused charges that blast up and down in a cone but not sideways, vaporising a ten-meter circle below and a wider hole above instead of bringing the building down. I dropped several in a rough vertical line through the apartment building. When I hit the detonator they punch a jagged, almost straight shaft from the lobby to the roof. Being three times bigger this heat makes the holes three times bigger. A pleasant surprise.

beats.headline: They laugh until they cry
beats.text: Mordecai's slugpox cure is still sitting on the crafting table, which I tell Imani with my tail down. About thirty of our people are waiting outside the Hairpin: Chris back in human form in his Meadow Lark overalls, Elle a goblin, Imani holding Jacobus the starfish. They see me, a dachshund, and every one of them, Prepotente and Lucia included, falls over laughing. Imani scratches my chin and cures me. Fine. Let's go rob a casino.

beats.headline: The eye on the dog's forehead
beats.text: As a dachshund I can't punch, which I learn the hard way against a table. Worse: the Eye of the Bedlam Bride has moved from my chest to the middle of my dog forehead, and it's trying to wrench itself open. Let me take over, it says. No. You stay trapped. Then Mitch lunges at me, all mouth, and I open it on reflex. He freezes, glittering, screaming that it's too cold, and Donut finishes him. It's there when I need it. That's what worries me.

beats.headline: A promise at the hole in the floor
beats.text: I'm a dachshund, so I hold up a paw to look at the portal. It's the same as last time. Louis is going through it, and Samantha is crying, so I say it to him and to all of them: as long as I breathe, I will do everything I can to get you free, wherever you land. On the walk out Elle asks what the evil-eye business was. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride tattoo; I control it. She says I'm keeping secrets. She's right. One more floor, I tell her, and we'll talk.

beats.headline: Twenty-three
beats.text: Welcome to the eleventh floor. Twenty-three crawlers remaining. That number sobers me faster than Quasar did, and Quasar was shaking. The leaderboard is suspended, but my final ranking is two; Donut is three and wants to know who beat us both. I'm pretty sure I'm the last crawler left without a player-killer skull. I'm not a dog anymore, though I still want to lick myself, and the Eye of the Bedlam Bride is back where it belongs.

beats.headline: A patch, sewn crooked
beats.text: A patch, a gun, a sewing kit and a holster, laid out on the table, which is Mordecai. The patch is a foot crushing four-leaf clovers. Lucky Shot: a fatal blow gets deflected into a party member instead, once per floor. I sew it on above the Midnight Epicure. Donut says it isn't straight, and that I've started a new row without finishing the last one. It is straight. It comes off the second I've used it.

beats.headline: He leaves the Royal Court
beats.text: An hour of flowers, and it's time. I click Yes. I have left the Royal Court of Princess Donut. I'm not in a party. My personal space is segregated, down to one room, a bathroom and my food boxes, and I accept the invitation from Safehome Yolanda. Most of my crafting tables, bomber's studio included, stay on Donut's side, which makes rejoining easier. Plus, if I die, she doesn't lose it all.

beats.headline: He examines a Horrible
beats.text: I focus on a girl in the crowd. Maybe eight, long arms, bone-white skin, a green goblin mask. She scratches her leg with a black shoe. Her description isn't a stat block. It's the AI asking what her name was, whether she had a pet, who she would have become. Donut asks whether I understood any of it. I did, mostly, and a deep well of sadness comes with it. I think the AI is about to explain the rest.

beats.headline: Vengeance, not revenge
beats.text: Our turn at the stand. Donut asked me the difference, so I tell everyone. Revenge is direct. Vengeance is punishment, righteous and not always direct. The triangle falls away and there's the Unwashed, the Nothing's own face, an upside-down tree made of dahlias. Passing Grigori, I heal Chaco with a scroll and hold the AI's eyes while I do it. Then I point at the effigy and tell the galaxy it is coming for all of them. It may not be me. But we are coming.

beats.headline: This is our revolution
beats.text: The missile launcher we looted from Dwight is bolted to the chicken truck under the Unwashed. The sluggalos have the wheel and the deep fryer on, which was not the plan. I have the microphone and my face on a jumbotron. We are done playing and dying on your terms. This is our revolution. The door opens on thousands of monsters and the masked stand-ins they're tearing apart. Then my first choice, and the galaxy hears it: Scolopendra.

beats.headline: A gun to the pig's head
beats.text: Penny's a crawler now. Level ten Yorkshire pig, no class, typing in capitals because the biscuit made her sapient without giving her a voice. She wants a chicken sandwich. I strap her to my chest in the harness Mordecai modified, pour splooge down her, drink some myself, and put my father's gun to her head. I've blown up settlements. I killed Jasha and Radoslav. This still feels like a line I didn't know was there. Then I yell for Taranis.

beats.headline: Inside Scolopendra
beats.text: Gloom Wraith Phase puts Penny and me through the centipede's wall. No air. Splooge doesn't help her breathe, and I can't risk her potion cooldown, so I pierce her nipple with Petey Motteux's Little Secret, a ring from Tiatha's pile that grants Oxygenated. Mordecai then tells me splooge counts as food, no cooldown. Now you tell me. Oozy Form gets us into Club Scolopendra. The Sin of Consumption wheel lands green for both of us. The alien in the web lands red.

beats.headline: Lucky Shot, spent
beats.text: Emberus throws something at my chest that should kill me outright. The Four-Leaf Clover patch deflects it into my party member, Penny, out at Taranis's feet. Donut jumps us outside, into a demolition derby. Emberus climbs out of the bug at full size, screaming my name, and Taranis, who saw who hurt his pig, twists his wrist. I hold on to Donut. When the blast clears, most of the arena is dead or dying. I get on the motorcycle anyway.

beats.headline: What the actual fuck, Carl
beats.text: I put the bike down, launch us into the air, and throw the ball down Scolopendra's open mouth. The biggest thing in the dungeon splatters into a puddle the size of a small elephant. The achievement is the AI saying what the actual fuck, Carl, one word at a time, and admitting it's got nothing for a reward. Then Eris, huge, tells me I'm chaos incarnate and she doesn't need my worship. Every exit is an entrance. Don't forget the coin.

beats.headline: Mark of the Damned, and a dart
beats.text: Nineteen crawlers. Twenty if you count Penny, which I don't. The sun tattoos on the backs of my hands are raised scars now: Mark of the Damned, no explanation. There's a dart in my leg I never felt. Tracking Tag. The Kyryap has claimed you. I send party requests until every one of us is in a single party. We do this together. I have to stay on the twelfth and stop anyone winning the Ascendency until everybody left is out.

relations.note: Stuck with each other from the first night.

entities.name: Princess Donut
aka: Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
entities.tagline: I am a pedigreed tortoiseshell Persian with a bedroom full of ribbons and a very good voice. I do not see what more you could possibly need to know.
entities.voiceNote: Imperious, delighted by herself, wounded by any slight and quick to say so. CARL in capitals when he is being difficult; Mordecai is staff. Uses her titles in full and treats them as facts. Things are common, vulgar, rude or unfair. Never swears, because swearing is common. Mongo is her son and she will not be told otherwise.

beats.headline: First cat down the stairs
beats.text: Carl carries me down, and the dungeon gives him a Legendary Pet Box for it, which is fair, and gives me a Legendary Quadruped Box of my own, which is more than fair. His box has a biscuit in it. An Enhanced Pet Biscuit. I take it out of his hand, because it is obviously for me, and I melt into a heap of goo, and I get up talking. I have a great deal to say.

beats.headline: GC BWR NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
beats.text: I learn Magic Missile. I also have the highest stat total in the party, which makes me party leader, which anyone could have predicted. My first act is to give the party a proper name: the Royal Court of Princess Donut. There is an inauguration. Carl does not take it seriously enough, but there is an inauguration.

beats.headline: She equips a crown with an ominous description
beats.text: Mordecai says read the description first. Mordecai says a great many things. It is a crown, it is dark and smoky and exactly my colour, and it came out of my box, which has the word Legendary on it. It has a vulgar name, which is not my fault. It says something about the Blood Sultanate and a line of succession, eight floors down. I am already a princess. I do not see how being in line for anything could be a demotion. Carl is making his face.

beats.headline: She adopts a dinosaur
beats.text: There is a reward room on the second floor with a cage in it, and in the cage is a pet-class mob, and the pet-class mob is my son. I did not know that until I saw him. He is called Mongo. He is mine, and that is the end of the discussion.

beats.headline: Cat, and a Former Child Actor
beats.text: Odette suggested it, so obviously it is a good idea: a class that lets me choose another class at every level. I also arrange for Mordecai to be my manager. He is thrilled. He does not show it, but he is. My constitution is apparently far too low for what Carl calls melee, so I will be fighting with charisma, spells and the audience, which is how it should be done.

beats.headline: She fights with people
beats.text: It is a card floor and I have a deck, and Shi Maria is going into it. She is somebody, which is not the same thing as a mob with a number over its head. Carl saw straight through her and made an arrangement: she becomes a card, and we take her down to the next floor with us. I will play her when I need her. It is a game. That is what the cards are for.

beats.headline: The crown comes due
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate is on this floor, and every royal in the line must slay the Sultan and all the other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth. I am a royal in the line. I have been since the first floor. I would like it noted that I was told to read the description.

beats.headline: Her new attorney
beats.text: A Naga called Princess Chandra, Esquire, informs me that she is my attorney now, not Quasar, and that I have been put under a conservatorship with Carl as my guardian. She has married him, too, through some widow's law, and she has seized the Posse's accounts. I refuse every deal, since Carl is refusing his. Then I read every one of her papers and tell her what they say about her. And, for any reporters watching, I am most definitely not offering fifty million credits to anyone who turns her inside out on my behalf.

beats.headline: Assassin of Sekhmet
beats.text: Four minutes to pick a new class, which is simply not enough time for a decision of this importance. The Las Vegas Showgirl comes with a feathered hat for Mongo. Mordecai suggests Zoo Warden, which I will not dignify. Then there is a whole new tab tied to my deity titles, and even Mordecai says it is new to him. I take Assassin of Sekhmet: a healing aura, a hat, and accessories for every pet in the party. And straight away, a very nasty message from Khepri, the bug god, saying he is forming a death cult in my name.

beats.headline: Two missiles for a manatee
beats.text: The manatee is called Miss Talulah, she is level ninety, and she smells simply awful. Two magic missiles and she collapses into the water with holes in her you could put a soccer ball through. I am the number one crawler at level 135, so this is hardly surprising. Then a notification: I must choose the fate of my kill. Keep it dead for regular experience, or let the audience vote. It says the second choice will be more fun. Naturally, I pick the second choice. Results pending.

beats.headline: Fatty
beats.text: A unicorn in a tumbleweed calls me fatty, and the bug-eyed rat in a racing helmet on his head calls me a corpulent swine. Fatty! I stand in the road and explain that I am practically twice their levels and that their mount is very likely flammable, and Carl tells me to let them go around, which I do not, and then Mongo leans on the horn and they run over everything anyway. As soon as the next race starts, I am setting them on fire. Also, my vote came back: the people have chosen Otto the slime guy to be the manatee's stand-in in the arena. That is all it says.

beats.headline: A godslayer box
beats.text: Forty boxes, and the achievements are mostly rude. Emergency Gremlin scrolls by the dozen, apparently for when the truck breaks down mid-race. Crossbow bolts that pin whatever they hit in place. A crupper that matches my champion cloak. And then the celestial godslayer box, which is only smoke: it becomes Meatus, and a smoky paw comes down on him, and Rosetta says she can still taste it. No prize falls out. My right front paw, the one I used for the War Crime, starts to glow, and it hurts, and I stretch my claws, and the kitchen table rips in half.

beats.headline: Blue claws, and caps
beats.text: The claws glow blue. Blue! Like cheap LED lights, and they will not turn off. Mordecai calls it a boon. They cut through anything, which is lovely until one considers my litter box, and Carl's shoulder, and biscuits. Rosetta finds claw caps on the shop wall and buys red ones, so the glow comes out purple, which I suppose will have to do. Then the crupper's description, which is about a gnoll I killed and his children, and I do not wish to discuss it. It made me choose a spell. Puddle Jumper is now level sixteen.

beats.headline: Rule number one
beats.text: Prepotente has a biscuit that makes whoever eats it fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them, and he came to me for advice, which was the correct instinct. My advice is absolutely not. She would be level one and stuck with us, and it is a crime against nature besides. So I am compiling him a list of rules to live by. Rule number one: do not use magic to make someone fall in love with you. It is creepy. Rule number two is to stop arguing with me.

beats.headline: Is Katia okay?
beats.text: A greenroom at the bottom of the ocean and no snacks, which is not how Prepotente described this show. And Lexis is here! She has a minute, she says, so I ask the only thing that matters: is Katia okay? Something strange happened at the kinder facility after Faction Wars. A third party has appeared and is protecting it, and it is confused. She believes Katia is okay. Then her tablet beeps and all the colour goes out of her face, and I do not get to ask anything else.

beats.headline: The War Crime question
beats.text: A goat judges me worthy and asks which three spells I would combine if I cast War Crime a second time. I stiffen. Then I compose myself, because we are live and I am a professional. It will depend on the circumstances. Nothing is off the table. But I cannot cast it until the twelfth floor, and Carl and I must first get through these next two. The goat nods. I ask whether it is my turn to ask. It says yes, and the table turns to the next goat anyway.

beats.headline: A throne called Dorota
beats.text: The audience voted me a throne, which shows some of them have taste. It is a Smart Companion Royal Pet Throne, the Ultimate Diamond Pampered Pet Princess edition, and the moment I sit on it a little fluffy bed appears, it holds me steady like a gyro, and it feeds me snacks on demand. It came with a creepy man's voice, so I had it changed to a woman with a Polish accent, and I have named her Dorota. She agrees with everything I say. Dr. Metcalf is jealous.

beats.headline: A letter from Luca Di
beats.text: An entry in my Banquet Fit for a Princess, from a crawler I do not remember: Luca Di, a Pastamancer, who gave me his train hat on the fourth floor. His mother had dementia. On the third floor she took a race that mended her mind, and they talked, properly, before she fell on the bubble level. He says I saved that for him. He says it is all right to forgive myself for War Crime. The spell he left me is Temporary Macaroni.

beats.headline: A tunnel of cannelloni
beats.text: I killed more than ten thousand of them and did not go up a level. That is an outrage. Then the skulls come up out of the road and down out of the sky, and I cast Temporary Macaroni, which I have had for about a minute, and I chain it: uncooked cannelloni, a foot thick, a tunnel of it. When Gluteus passes out on the wheel I rip myself free of Dorota's belt and hold the accelerator down with both paws. We win.

beats.headline: Easier not to like him
beats.text: The gauge at the Lollipop was clearly broken. I sang Journey and it did not move, and Finley says I did fine, and I thank him. Then Osvaldo is in our heat and tells Carl something extremely vulgar, so I tell him he is only alive because of me and Carl, and he is a straight-to-video leprechaun. Carl says he is not an enemy. He is not going to help us. It is us or him. It will be easier if we stay not liking each other.

beats.headline: The Astral Paw, and a bite
beats.text: Cannibals, hundreds of them, dropping out of the trees and bursting on our shield. I swipe my Astral Paw and sweep the arch clear like pieces off a chessboard. Elle calls me terrifying, which is fair. It is a lot stronger than it was, but it does not last, and now I cannot cast it for eight hours, and I killed about eighty and did not go up a level, which is ridiculous. Then something bites my bottom. I believe it was the dog tattoo.

beats.headline: What she tells the shark
beats.text: I Hover up to the ceiling and whisper to him, and he flips down and lands right by the truck. Carl asks what I said. I told him it is true, it could happen at any moment, but if we worry about things we cannot control, we ruin the things we can. And even if he is annoying, he is family now, and he should tell us when he is in trouble, because family helps. Mongo, mind Mommy and guard Hedy.

beats.headline: Relationship advice for a pig
beats.text: Carl wants a distraction, so I take the driveway with my headset microphone and address the fake tiger people. My charisma is high enough now that All Eyes on Me works with plain talking, no singing required. I explain to Penelope that throuples in which two members are at each other's throats end in heartbreak, and then Miss Piggy, and Piglet, and Wilbur, and Peppa. They cannot look away. By the time I wave goodbye they do not even know they were charmed.

beats.headline: Jezebel the hedgehog
beats.text: Satan is a hedgehog, a kaiju-sized one, and I would bet anything he talks with a fake British accent, and I do not care what Carl says, this has nothing to do with Tacoma. Yes, there was a Cutest in Show, and yes, I was a kitten, and yes, the winner was a baby hedgehog from a rescue named Jezebel, and Miss Beatrice sulked all day. It was fixed from the beginning. Who names a hedgehog Jezebel? It hardly matters now. I have raised the toad, head caved in and all, to drive us.

beats.headline: We are calling her Chachi
beats.text: WE'RE JUST GOING TO CALL HER CHACHI. I only have so much room on my cut-and-paste, and I am not filling it with a name that long. Anyway, it is concert day. Prepotente is coming, and he is singing as well, which is lovely for him. Mine is a surprise. It will be a duet with Carl, and he has to take a great many potions and scrolls first so that he does not mess it up. Then we go and collect the pig from the empty house.

beats.headline: She is not a weapon
beats.text: Carl says we need people like Li Na, because she is so strong. She is not a weapon, Carl. She is a person. I like her, of course I do, but we cannot let her keep hurting people, and we certainly cannot let Zhang kill himself to stop her. That is not right, and I told Zhang no, twice. We will find something to fix this. Somebody has to talk some sense into her. It is the only way.

beats.headline: Robbed of a perfect score
beats.text: My part was perfect, Auto-Tuned and in key, and in the middle of a chorus I shot the axe out of a Draconian's hand before he could put it in Dong's head. Then, on my very last line, a paralysed kappa fell backward right into me, and now there is a sign over my head that says FAILED. I was robbed of a perfect score. Carl has to go through the glowing door by himself. We are never going to mention this again. I do love that song, though.

beats.headline: A letter from a half-orc
beats.text: The newest entry in my Feast book is from Mees Koning, a half-orc mage, final level sixty-three. Before the battle at the southern border I stopped at his stinger unit and told him I liked his fangs, and we talked for maybe a minute, and he says it was the first time anyone had been nice to him just to be nice. He was inside the ball when I cast my Atrocity. He drew me a magnet, a very well-shaded one. It is called Big-Ass Magnet. I did not choose the name.

beats.headline: Twice now
beats.text: At the shop terminal, as the white bot sold, Mordecai's hood came down, his head was on fire, and he said something about the Oak Fell in a deep voice that was not his usual one. Then he blinked, patted the fire out and carried on as if nothing had happened. He said that would only happen once. That is twice now. Carl says he told us to ignore it. It is really scary, and I do not like it, and nobody is explaining it to me.

beats.headline: Not a kangaroo anymore
beats.text: The Dominators' car went through a hole in the floor, and I saw it, so I made Carl stop and reverse. It is a ten-metre drop, and horrible little dolls are tearing the car apart. Carl wants to jump down. And then what, Carl? You are not a kangaroo anymore. I got this. I land on the car and cast Puddle Jumper. I cannot teleport Corky into the truck, so I bring us both up to the road beside it, which is the next-best thing. My fur is smoking.

beats.headline: Laundry Day, and then a magnet
beats.text: Grull came crashing through a wall with that awful Maestro riding inside him, so I cast Laundry Day, and the orc dropped out of the god's chest into the molten metal. We do not have time to kill you now. Maybe next time! But Corcunda is still marked, and he and Dong decide to go and meet the god themselves, and I try to say no, and I cannot finish saying it. So I cast Big-Ass Magnet on Dong's lance, the spell that was meant for the Dominators' car. Every screw in the room goes with them.

beats.headline: Dong is dead
beats.text: We came in last place, and the stupid unicorn won by going over the factory instead of through it, which is cheating, and Osvaldo agrees with me. Dong is dead. He was my friend. Grigori says some people believe death is only a movement on to another plane, and that Dong did not think it was the end. Perhaps. It is still horrible for those of us who are still here. Grigori agrees.

beats.headline: Not speaking to Carl
beats.text: I am not speaking to Carl. His strategy has him leaving the party for the eleventh floor, so that I do not get hurt, as if I cannot look after myself. So I am sitting in the stables while Rosetta explains dungeon lore that will not matter because we will all be dead in a few hours. A child who can take the powers of gods and use them for herself, just like that Spock on the show with the cheerleader. Carl laughed. You are not allowed to laugh at my observations, Carl.

beats.headline: The message board caught him
beats.text: Let the record show it WAS NOT ME. It was the Princess Posse message board. Linus is the brother, which was the big theory, and WriggleInDew2023 of the Mongo Mommies Valtay chapter said all along he was no Valtay agent, and she will be thrilled. He leaned far too hard into the romantic material, which real admirers rarely say out loud, and one of his brother's friends noticed his tattoo was wrong. Honestly. He could at least have taken acting lessons. He is worse than Prepotente, and I mean that with love.

beats.headline: Plan Mach Schnell
beats.text: Carl is a dog now and cannot even say the name of the plan properly. It is Mach Schnell. Dorota rolls the window down for me, bless her. When the light goes green I am through the window as smoke and onto the roof before the vine has finished dying, and before Osvaldo's gnu has stopped staggering I take that tiresome unicorn's head off with one swipe and his horn goes into my inventory. The announcement is complimentary. I prefer decisive. Carl is wagging again.

beats.headline: Astral Paw on the Cadillac
beats.text: The Russian car throws itself up on end in the middle of the lobby to make a run for the exit, after all our planning and all Imani's pleading. The APV and Chris's truck fire into its shield, Prepotente throws something, and the shield flickers out. So I cast Astral Paw and the Cadillac simply ceases to exist, all in less than a second. Three new skulls over my head before Carl can even think a rude word.

beats.headline: She tells the giant Imani it is a dream
beats.text: The giant Imani is sitting in the lobby holding Gucci, and the building will not let her leave, and she says she should have left them all when she had the chance. So I switch on my headset microphone. Darling, this is a dream. Out in the real world you already left: Detroit, then Washington, and friends named Yolanda and Brandon and Elle, and a man named Chris, and happily ever after. Close your eyes. Before that I moved Onikuma and Old Shuck into our garage with Dwight's keys. We will need them. I am not discussing it.

beats.headline: The pickle class
beats.text: Mordecai, help me pick a class. Comeback Kid comes with a movie deal, which is obviously me, but CARL says my Glass Cannon ruins it, because you get all your old bad parts back too. So: Elite Gurkha Warrior. It sounds like a pickle. Extra skills for pets and mercenaries, a big claw upgrade for Mongo, Cockroach to fifteen. Carl says I am going to pick it, so I nearly didn't. I picked it. Also, his psychotic wife tried to accept a deal on my behalf, and then got scared and vanished.

beats.headline: An advance copy of a spell
beats.text: My new spell book is a paperback, which is common. Tome of Gatekeeper, an Advance Reader Copy: I may install it now, and it works on the twelfth floor. It takes away a target's class skills for a while, even a god's. The duration is nerd math. And I got a Legendary box for seeing the shadow mimic before he revealed himself, and a Legendary Steed upgrade so Mongo can pull a cart.

beats.headline: Her title goes with his
beats.text: I do not like this. Carl's royal bodyguard title has gone, and now his says nothing at all. Then he grins and tells me mine has gone too. MINE. I am not the one who left the stupid party, and I cannot even add a new one. This is so unfair. At least the float is beautiful: Requite Dahlias from my Sprout Forest, black and gold and magenta and white, which match the Gurkha blankets, on every square inch of everything.

beats.headline: I love you too
beats.text: At the arena door Carl lifts me off his shoulder and holds me much too tightly and tells me to get to Elle and Imani and stay away. I know the plan. I am scared, and I say so. Then he says he loves me, and then he starts on if this doesn't work, and I will not let him jinx it. People keep asking how he would react if something happened to me. Nobody asks me. I love him too.

beats.headline: Two bolts, and Puddle Jumper
beats.text: Now. One of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps swaps me into the room and the pig out to Taranis's feet. Scorpion's Bite on my back, Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus loaded, and it goes straight into Emberus's eye. The second, one of my Danforth bolts, goes into the other, and he cannot move. Toodles. Puddle Jumper, level seventeen, and Carl and I are outside the arena door. When he tells me to get off his motorcycle, I tell him exactly where he can go.

beats.headline: His inventory is a disgrace
beats.text: Eris swaps everybody's pockets and I get Carl's, and it is not organised. Rocks, CARL. Why are there rocks. Why is a chicken and goblin recipe book in his hotlist. He shouts at me to combine the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve, and my hotlist only has ten slots, so I search and combine and drop it into his xistera, very fast, while the centipede glows.

beats.headline: The wrong biscuit
beats.text: I am sitting in the dirt and not being sarcastic, which should tell everyone something. Carl sends me a party request and I accept it without a word. Then I have to tell him. Don't get mad. The inventory was happening so fast. The goo drains away and there is a centipede with lips and a red bow, and she is not a pet. She is Sexy Scolopendra, level one, crawler, in our party. I gave him the wrong biscuit.

relations.note: She considers him her son. He agrees.

entities.name: Mongo
entities.tagline: MOTHER. Food. MOTHER. Bite anything near Mother.
entities.voiceNote: Does not talk. What the camera gets is the dinosaur: single words, capitals, appetite. MOTHER is Donut. Everything else is FOOD, NOT FOOD, or BAD. Never more than a few short lines.

beats.headline: Seven inches of pink feathers, in a cage
beats.text: CAGE. Small. Pink? Pink. TWO BIG THINGS. Bite them. Bite them. Bite. MOTHER. Mother has grubs. Grubs open. Inside part GOOD. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: He stands over her
beats.text: Mother down. Mother NOT MOVING. Mongo on top of Mother. Spiky things. MANY spiky things. Bite. Bite. Bite. Hurts. Mongo stays on Mother. Carl says something. Mongo does not listen to Carl.

beats.headline: He finishes Maggie My
beats.text: Thing on Chris. Thing OFF Chris. Thing goes for Carl. Thing is FOOD.

beats.headline: Nearly lost, and then a father
beats.text: Mongo, dinosaur, registered pet of Crawler Princess Donut, has survived the ninth floor. This was not the expected outcome. The last of Lucia Mar's dogs very nearly ate him, and Sir Rendlegore saved him, and the dog died. Mongo is also, as of the stairs, a father. Nobody is going to explain that to you, least of all me.

beats.headline: HAT
beats.text: MOTHER has a HAT. Hat is NOT FOOD. Mongo backs UP. Dong puts hat on Mongo anyway. Floppy ears. Hat is fine. Rend gets red one. Fries are FOOD.

beats.headline: Beer is FOOD
beats.text: Bug-bear man pours BEER. Slug drinks it. Mongo WANTS. MOTHER says NO. Mongo does not stay back. Now floor moves. Tater tots. FOOD. Mongo waves both wings. HAPPY.

beats.headline: Friend is dead. Friend is not dead.
beats.text: Rend not moving. Mongo stands over Rend and cries. MOTHER says time-out. Then Rend is up. Rend is BIGGER. Mongo dances. Ghoul things at door. Mongo turns too fast. Falls over.

beats.headline: He guards the garage
beats.text: Big box. Sniff. Sniff bumper. BAD. Mongo backs up. Shark on ceiling. Shark comes down. Mongo lies down by shark. MOTHER says stay. Guard Hedy. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: Into the fight
beats.text: MOTHER singing. Loud. FIGHT. Tail. People fall over. Fairy throws fire at Imani. Fairy is FOOD. MOTHER has beer on her. Lick MOTHER. MOTHER is cross.

beats.headline: Three Mongos, one sat on
beats.text: Table bites MOTHER. Now THREE Mongo. Chandelier eats shiny Mongo. BAD. Shiny Mongo goes BOOM. Mongo ANGRY. Mongo bites chairs. Big mimic last. MOTHER kills it first. Mongo sits on it anyway.

beats.headline: Claw caps
beats.text: CLAW CAPS. On FEET. Sharp. MOTHER has hats for everyone. Mongo keeps the old head thing. Mongo is marching band. Rend is marching band. Flowers on EVERYTHING. Flowers are NOT FOOD.

entities.name: Mordecai

tagline.text: Your guide for the first three floors. I have done this before. Listen, and you might get to see the fourth.
I crawled once. It cost me everything I had, and Borant still owns what's left.

entities.voiceNote: Tired professional, precise about rules, exasperated by clients who ignore them. Leads with the warning, follows with the reason, ends with a sigh you can hear. Kid, listen, you don't get it. Bitter about Borant in short sentences. Does not gush and does not comfort; drunk, he talks about the past and stops himself.

beats.headline: Tutorial Guild Hall, first floor
beats.text: Rule one: I don't open the door until you kill a goblin. The cat desecrates my mother. The man blows up a Murder Dozer. I open the door. My name is Mordecai. Borant holds my indenture, which means I guide for the first three floors and run a magic guild after that, where they mostly leave me alone to brew and look up old friends. Try to live long enough for that to matter.

beats.headline: He has done this before, and it cost him everything
beats.text: I crawled. I took Changeling, and I can't shift on my own any more, so the dungeon hands me a body at the start of every floor and I wear what I'm given. This one is a rat-kin. What I actually am is golden, and has wings. I don't talk about the family. When I've had enough to drink, I talk about the family.

beats.headline: Manoeuvred into managing a cat
beats.text: Odette says my memory is the most valuable thing a crawler could get hold of, so the two of them arrange for me to become the cat's manager during class selection, and they make it look like an accident. It was not an accident. I will forgive Donut. Carl, no.

beats.headline: The rules he cannot break
beats.text: Most of what I know I'm not allowed to volunteer. Some of it I can only give you if you ask the exact question. Without press credentials nobody watching can see me or hear me, and as a manager I can't touch a mob. My advice is what it has always been: stay ahead of the curve, never trust an elite, stay away from gods. Carl has heard all three.

beats.headline: Huanxin, Uzzi, and what happened
beats.text: Odette is in the middle of this crawl now, so the old story is going to come out. Chaco. Uzzi. A stairwell that would not open unless a god was struck down, and me volunteering to do the striking, because the only life it cost was mine. Odette found a cheaper way to pay. She talked Chaco into putting the dart into my brother instead. She had a bargain with Huanxin Jinx and she tore it up rather than sign away her bonus, and Uzzi is what she spent in its place. I walked out of that stairwell. He did not. I do not talk about it sober.

beats.headline: Not a Moon Reaper
beats.text: Kid, listen. I look like a Moon Reaper on this floor, and I'm not one. I'm a shadow mimic. Mimics take the shape; changelings get some of the powers. This form is an impossible combination, which is why I keep glitching into a cat, an otter, a slug. And the prophecy business is a Moon Reaper thing. It only happens once for each of you. Nobody give it any weight. Predictions in here are vague, scary and made to fit whatever happens. And keep Rend out of here. His weakness is Reaper Gaze.

beats.headline: Dipped in radiant light
beats.text: That was a celestial boon. Permanent, and it lives in her body, not in her spell list. Her right front claws cut through anything in the mortal realm, ghosts included, and her Claw skill has gone past the cap to seventeen, because when it comes to gods all bets are off. With that constitution she has gone from a ranged powerhouse to one of the strongest melee fighters the game has seen. Now the warning. The game has ways of compensating for overpowered crawlers on this floor and past it. Believe me. Don't get complacent.

beats.headline: Leave the costume on
beats.text: Kid, listen. How high has the costume skill gone? If it's above level three or so, taking that thing off might take a lot of your skin with it. Above five I wouldn't risk it. Six, he says, with a bunch of other skills hanging off it. Then leave it be. Laundry Day will definitely get it off you. You'll get flayed in the process. Most armour isn't physically attached. That one is.

beats.headline: The bard potions are brewing
beats.text: Tipid warned me before Carl asked. A karaoke guild, and the needle has to stay in the green for the whole song. So yes, the bard potion. It is brewing now. It will not be ready until just before the next race.

beats.headline: A soul returned, a mind still gone
beats.text: Carl's driver goes down Gingered, unconscious, health bleeding out, and he messages me in a panic. Listen. Did you kill the mob that did it? Good. That returns her soul. It does not return her. She needs specialised healing from a cleric, and until she gets it she is in a fugue, staring at nothing. Good thing you have a backup driver. Try to keep that one.

beats.headline: The test worked, mostly
beats.text: Believe it or not, the test worked. Samantha can't die and she's not what you'd call a reliable subject, so we ran it again on some sluggalos. It works. There are a few wrinkles, and I'm working on them right now. But listen to me, kid. This is so far off the codex we don't even know the system will let Li Na do it. And if it does, she could still die when your floor collapses. He says he knows. He always says he knows.

beats.headline: Goddamn sapient weapons
beats.text: Okay. We're busy prepping the Li Na exit, but we took a look at Dong. It says Negative ROI. Mistress Tiatha thinks it's really a curse called Separation Anxiety, and if she's right a temple won't do a thing. We need the sock back, and every coin he lost. The sock went for Bucket Boy and got teleported by the safe room rules, and it's probably in Hungry Eyes in somebody else's hands. That's what sapient weapons do. They use an owner up and move on. I didn't see this one coming. Its stupid origin story hid it.

beats.headline: Two hundred plants under glass
beats.text: Li Na's dread cactus is steady, one bloom. Ronit, the druid, has worked out something simpler for the rest: every crawler who went through gets a small potted plant tied to their life. Wilts or turns to dust, they're dead. Blooms, they got out. I had to build a glass terrarium for the lot because the sluggalos were eyeing them. Two hundred-some pots in the guildhall common room. It's the only way we'll know. Even the showrunners can't see in there.

beats.headline: Mimics, and safe words
beats.text: Listen. If the Desperado Club is infested, you can't go back. Mimics are almost impossible to root out; the whole place needs fumigating. They dodge most detection spells, like one of Carl's level fifteen traps, all but invisible. They can mimic a crawler, and the system labels them a crawler right up until you catch one. So you all devise safe words, and you quiz each other every day from here. I'm not asking.

beats.headline: An animistic spirit
beats.text: Welcome to the eleventh floor. I'm not going to be much physical help to you. I'm an animistic spirit: no body of my own, I occupy objects. Not my first time as one. Donut hears racist. Animistic, Donut. I can still talk in chat, so we do classes. Comeback Kid gives you every old skill, leveled up, and every old penalty with it; I'd have to research it and we don't have time. The Gurkha one comes with pet and mercenary skills. Take that.

beats.headline: He is the table
beats.text: I'm the table. Samantha is sitting on me. Donut, you're standing right next to me. I can hear all of you, but I can't answer out loud unless I move into something with a mouth, and I'm not good at moving yet. Won't be in a few hours, either. We just had to fight a table, she says. I know. It freaks me out too. I feel like I gotta pee. Carl, the backpack is done. It's on your crafting table.

beats.headline: Safe rooms are not safe
beats.text: The splooge is a type of potion, but it's treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules don't apply. As for the pig's nipple, I don't know how to respond to that, Carl. What you need to know: we're okay. Game guides appear to be immune. Safe rooms are not safe from these nine-tier attacks. Bucket Boy got hit, and Mistress Tiatha healed him in time.

entities.name: Katia Grim

tagline.text: Doppelganger. Apparently I am like clay, and I can mould my own mass. I am working out how, and you can tell.
Art professor, Reykjavík. I can mould my own mass like clay, and I am getting better at it.

entities.voiceNote: Quiet, exact, self-critical. An academic's vocabulary used plainly; dry about her own face and her own standing. Puts other people first and says so as fact, not virtue. Grief is stated once and not decorated. Carl and Donut by name; Eva by name, without explanation.

beats.headline: Ten levels behind and nobody's problem
beats.text: I came in with a friend. We fell in with Hekla and Brynhild's Daughters, who carried the two of us through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I know exactly how much of that was us. Class selection split us up, and she did not wait. Now Hekla is asking Carl and Donut to take me. The system has just upgraded my displayed race from "What the f-word?" to "Human", so things are looking up.

beats.headline: Doppelgänger, Monster Truck Driver
beats.text: Bannon, my guide, talked me into it: a momentum-based constitution tank who can reshape her own mass, body and equipped gear together, into any form of the same weight. I sculpted my face using my reflection in a health potion bottle. Carl says it looks like a Juan Gris. He is being kind, and I would know.

beats.headline: She spends a death sentence saving NPCs
beats.text: The Fools Who Broke the Glass quest is close to unsurvivable, and it triggers before I have earned my place. I spend the time getting NPCs out. I tell Carl and Donut to save themselves. I mean it.

beats.headline: She kills Ghazi and takes his notes
beats.text: The sand ooze is dead and the walls are coming in. I get out with Ghazi. Then I kill him, for the notes that explain how the Gate works. Carl and Donut are still buried when I do it. I know how that sounds.

beats.headline: She turns the watches into a map
beats.text: The linked watches read as a reverse compass: a time, an altitude, an exact position relative to anywhere else. Which means the Gate could open onto the city of Larracos, on the ninth floor, and I am mapping ground nobody has stood on.

beats.headline: She takes the Orchid and goes
beats.text: Crawler Katia Grim has left the dungeon. Not by the stairs. She ate the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and lay for an hour at one percent, and when she opened her eyes the goddess was standing over her, telling her to get up. She got up. Where she has gone is between her and the goddess.

entities.name: Imani

tagline.text: Meadow Lark, on the badge. Scrubs, a longsword and a cloak. I'm nowhere near finished, and I won't be rushed.
Out of Meadow Lark, and holding a portal open on the racing floor until everyone who's coming is through.

entities.voiceNote: Calm, steady, a caregiver's voice under pressure. Counts people, says what needs doing, does it. Warm without fuss, firm without volume. Carl, Donut, Elle, Yolanda, Brandon and Chris by name. Never dramatises a loss and never leaves before the last one is through.

beats.headline: The good folks from Meadow Lark
beats.text: We came down out of Meadow Lark, the elder care facility, together: Yolanda Martinez, the Andrews brothers, Brandon and Chris, me, and Agatha, who none of us can quite place and who came with us anyway. Carl and Donut find us, and we sit down and trade stories, theirs and ours, and then we make a plan, because there are people depending on us and a plan is what you owe them.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Seven of us against the Ball of Swine: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Carl, Donut, Agatha and me, fighting from the redoubt. It is the first time this group has fought as one thing instead of six people and a cat standing near each other, and it works. Afterwards I count everybody twice, because that is what I do, and everybody is there both times.

beats.headline: The table at the Lollipop
beats.text: The Lollipop, back table. I have a beer, and I slide Carl one, and Donut gets a Shirley Temple with extra cherries. Everyone checks in. Elle and I drew a military troop carrier. Tran is stuck in his garage. Zhang is not here: Li Na isn't really talking to him, and she killed almost every other team in their heat, so next race will show whether Prepotente is right about crawlers racing crawlers. Chris says his big rig is big but slow. Kinda like you, I tell him, and he almost smiles.

beats.headline: It's the sock
beats.text: Dong goes down outside the other team's garage and everyone assumes the Dominators cast something on him. I wrap him in my wings. There's nothing wrong with him now. What bothers me is where the sock was: he'd left it in our garage. Near it, he's actively healed and his health doesn't go up, which means it's sustaining him. Rosetta and Mordecai don't trust sapient weapons. If he's addicted, I don't know what to do yet. We don't tell him until we have a plan.

beats.headline: Two brothers, and no more
beats.text: I came over to get away from Elle's fan, Linus, and the slugs find me anyway. Donut asks how many brothers I have, in the present tense, and everyone flinches. I answer it the way it is. Full siblings, two. I was the youngest and the only girl. Then I tell Carl to open his boxes before Donut's blood bar drains, and I go and play, because somebody has to unlock Funky Kong if anyone in this room is ever going to beat Samantha.

beats.headline: Her card will not go back
beats.text: I get a notification: Jacobus is permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card. I did not summon him. Carl did something. Now there is a fist-sized reverse tooth fairy doing laps around my head in Danish, asking my friends to show him their teeth and pay him three hundred and twenty gold. We are in a safe area. When he goes for Prepotente I catch him in my hand. No. He will not be doing that with any of my friends.

beats.headline: Crawler Henrietta's team is gone
beats.text: We pull onto the road just as Carl's truck passes, and now we are behind him. Elle is driving, like an old lady. We have lost a team already this heat. Crawler Henrietta, from Angola, new this heat. They hit a trap. It swallowed their mount whole, and she and her partner are gone. Carl sends us his course and asks about the cliff ahead. We have a wall-climbing kit. It is slow. He says he will wait until we are over, so we go.

beats.headline: Looking forward to this
beats.text: Donut has zapped Mongo into the bar so he won't miss Uncle Carl's stage debut, and the patrons are jumping back from his wings. Carl won't tell us why this quest matters so much. I don't need to know. I tell him the truth, and I smile when I do it: I've been looking forward to this moment for a long time. He says he hopes I like Norwegian music. Elle is going to be furious she missed it. I wave Chris, Florin, Bautista, Britney and Jurgen to the back, and suddenly the place is packed.

beats.headline: Goddamnit, Carl
beats.text: He posted his plan for the eleventh floor to his page in the Book of Voodoo, and I left him three paragraphs on why it gets us all killed. He wrote back that he hopes I take a deal, that nobody would blame me, that I deserve the rest. So I told him: Goddamnit, Carl. This is insane. I still know he has no other choice, with Emberus coming due. My blood bar has an hour on it. The volunteers are gathering in Hungry Eyes, and Florin is choosing. Can we get on with this?

beats.headline: That's not my dad
beats.text: Elle and I hit our gate in 310, and I cast Confuzzled on the room so the bugs stay stunned long enough for us to drop out. Carl calls the man on the floor my dad. That's not my dad.
