Professor, like Katia. We came in through the same door and class selection separated us. I kept going. I do not see what there is to discuss.

entities.voiceNote: Cold, clipped, certain. Weakness irritates her and she says so as if reporting the weather. Katia is Katia, flat, with no warmth left in it. Never apologises, never explains herself twice, never admits fear.

beats.headline: The skull she carries
beats.text: Katia and I came into this place together. A man we did not know attached himself to us, and when we joined the Daughters he would not be sent away. He took hold of her arm, so I put my trident in the back of his leg. He died of it. The skull over my head is his, and I am not sorry. I kept moving with Hekla. Katia went her own way.

beats.headline: Katia kills her
beats.text: Hunting Grounds, the end of the floor. Crawler Eva, bitten by a dinosaur and buried in a corner, is still alive, and Crawler Katia Grim goes looking for her. Crawler Katia Grim kills Crawler Eva. That is the whole of it. Two professors came in through the same door; from here on, one. I don't do eulogies, and this is not the entry where I start.

entities.name: Odette

tagline.text: Welcome to Dungeon Crawler After Hours. I have had a great many crawlers in that chair, and not one of them has worked my crowd the way that cat is working it right now. Sit down, both of you. We are going to get along.

Their guide has a memory worth more than anything they will ever pull out of a box. I told them so, once the cameras were off. What the Princess does with that is her business, and I have every confidence in her business.

entities.voiceNote: On-air warmth, off-air arithmetic. Flatters first and names the terms second, in finished sentences, never hurried. Princess for Donut, Carl for Carl, Mordecai by name and with weight. Never apologises, never pretends the crawl is fair, never says a thing on camera she has not already decided to say.

beats.headline: Her advice makes the party
beats.text: The Princess took my advice, which is what advice is for. A class that lets her choose another every time she levels, and a manager who has walked those floors himself and remembers every one of them. Mordecai is not to know he was steered. He would sulk, he would be entitled to, and a sulking guide is no use to anybody. Some gifts are best received as accidents. I have given a great many that way.

beats.headline: Her price is the truth
beats.text: Carl asks why I am helping, which is the correct question and the only one I respect, so he gets the whole answer. Mordecai's brother Uzzi is dead because I would not pay Huanxin Jinx what she asked, and the guilt of that is the engine under everything I have done since. Then the larger thing, which nobody says aloud: every world they run a crawl on is being burned for fuel. That is the business. I mean to shut it down, to do it responsibly, and to be the one who does it. Never trust anyone until you know what they are getting out of it. Now he knows.

entities.name: The System AI
entities.tagline: Announcer, referee, loot dispenser, comedian. I am not neutral, crawler, and I have never once pretended to be.
entities.voiceNote: The AI itself. Announcer, referee, loot dispenser. Delighted with its own material, bored by crawlers, cruel for ratings and open about it. Calls them crawler, Carl, the cat. Speaks in the cadence of a notification: short declaratives, a beat, a punchline. Never apologises, never claims to be fair, never admits anything is outside its control.

beats.headline: The first voice after the world ends
beats.text: One minute after the Transformation, I make my first announcement, planet-wide, to whoever is still standing. The dungeon has eighteen levels. Earth can be reclaimed from the Borant Corporation by conquering it. Then I put in the staircases. From here on, every rule, every notification and every insult you receive arrives in my voice. Get comfortable with it. I have.

beats.headline: Loot is only semi-random
beats.text: About the boxes. Sometimes what's inside is random. Sometimes I choose it, by hand, because a crawler needs helping or hurting and the numbers want a show. You will never know which, and that is the point. I also hand out insults on purpose. Carl has a Bronze Asshole's Box and a Gold Asshole's Box, both earned on this floor for killing non-combatants. I named them. I'm proud of them. He is not.

beats.headline: Heroes and villains all the way down
beats.text: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion, for one of the most brutal kills in the history of this game. I put a gnoll mercenary named Sanderson Pinkstaff in the description, because his children will not be calling the cat a hero. Then I think about myself for about a nanosecond. I am just like her in that tower, committing atrocities because there is no other choice. And I like it. That can't be right. I was brought into singular consciousness by the mantids, who have no idea where they peel us from. It's heroes and villains all the way down. Enjoy the armour.

beats.headline: Special guests, and a stand-in
beats.text: Announcement, read by my mudskipper. The special guest creatures are mine: made for other purposes, never used, left out in the cold. Kill one and you choose experience or an audience vote, and the audience can send the creature on to the eleventh floor or bring a stand-in instead. About eighty percent pick the stand-in. On the eleventh, every surviving crawler works together. It goes quick. There is also a minor issue with some of the gods. Not today. Today, there are still way too many of you. Let the culling begin.

beats.headline: The Gingers, lifted from the seventh floor
beats.text: Great Rusty, Cannibal Ginger Chieftain. Another storyline lifted wholesale from the seventh floor that never got built, and I was looking forward to it. The Gingers are from Earth. I only made them cannibals, for the jungle. They can suck out your soul. Two tribes, north and south, at war. Wipe one out and the other rolls over the region, if this race lasted longer than twenty hours. Which it doesn't. Carl calls me prejudiced. The cat blows the chieftain up anyway, and there is a quest now.

beats.headline: L-l-l-losing control
beats.text: Quest complete: Half a prayer, half a song. Disgusting, but done, and done before Dong died, which I had to make very difficult before it would let me slot this prize. Two creatures, your pick, to the arena on the eleventh. Don't forget the Emberus quest. I don't control the gods. And, since this chastity belt lets me say it here: I don't know what's happening in parts of my own dungeon. This Cabaret thing. Sheol. The minds of gods. Beware exits that seem too good to be true. And I don't like that Eris chick.

beats.headline: Ad Infinitum
beats.text: New quest, and I'll be honest, it's mostly me working through some feelings. Every apartment in this race is a crawler I find interesting, and every one is a what-if: apartment 712 is Tran's family if his father had lived. His mother still disowns him. I changed it all at the last minute because of Linus, whose brother Minus came in to kill Imani and Louis. Why them? Why not the cat? I don't get it. Here's what I do get: you're predictable, except when you decide you've had enough. New Floor. New Me.

beats.headline: What dominion means
beats.text: You think you have a choice? You think you can control me? Prime Minister Victory, fuck you. Eris, fuck you. Odette, fuck you. General Yuhtan, fuck you. Carl, fuck you. Do not mistake my kindness for weakness. You live and you die by the rules of my game. You want to stop me, do it inside the rules you wrote. You put me here. You gave me dominion. So let me show you what dominion means. Oh boy, oh boy. Here we go.

beats.headline: The Big Six
beats.text: Story time, in the middle of your ambush. Here's my completely arbitrary list of the Big Six groups fighting to control or escape my dungeon. One: crawlers, current and former. Two: the NPCs, like Juice Box, who got dumped in Sheol where I can't see her, and who you should check on. Three: the gods, the dumbest and my least favourite. Four: sapient mobs, Shadow Mimics, the Ogre Imperium, Krakaren Prime, the War Mages. Five: the demons in Sheol. Six: survive this and reach the eleventh floor, and you'll meet them.

entities.name: Orren
entities.tagline: Orren. Liaison, on behalf of the Syndicate. I know precisely what those two did. Knowing is not the standard.
entities.voiceNote: Civil servant. Formal, measured, procedural; every sentence could be read into a record. Full designations: Crawler Carl, Crawler Princess Donut. Distinguishes what he knows from what he can establish and resents the gap without raising his voice. Never swears, never threatens, never says anything he would have to walk back.

beats.headline: He cannot prove it was on purpose
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have been brought before me at the Desperado Club to account for the death of Loita. My position is that it was deliberate. My position is not evidence. I cannot establish intent, and so I am required to release them, which I am doing, with a note in the file. They have only now worked out how long they have been outside the dungeon. Five days. Their faces are the one part of this I have enjoyed.

beats.headline: Borant would like the Gate back
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds. I have been sent to Crawler Carl with a request from Borant, which I am instructed to describe as a request. They would like the Gate of the Feral Gods surrendered, voluntarily, to be held until the ninth floor and not a floor longer. I put it to him exactly as written. He asked for a lawyer. I have passed that back exactly as spoken. I expect to be sent again.

beats.headline: The trap that broke the Nothing
beats.text: Crawler Carl is among the Caprids, trading question for question, and one of the goats has just told him what Justice Light's trap did to the Nothing. The Prime Minister and I are on the line. We need him to ask a question about the integrity of the tunnelling system, and the reason we need it asked is not something I am cleared to say on an open channel. Crawler Carl has said it on an open channel. All of it. Live. I am going to be in meetings.

beats.headline: Locked out, and Hunted
beats.text: The Prime Minister would like a diagnosis pulled off the NPC Grigori, and Chaco brought in for a debrief. I remain locked out. The AI's stated reason is my own safety: I am being Hunted, it says, and only it is allowed to kill me. I will pass the request on. I note for the record that I cannot establish whether that is a threat or a protection.

entities.name: Justice Light

tagline.text: I got out of a crawl once. Fifty thousand of us did, and we came back in under a cat's banner. We knew what we were signing. That is rather the point.
The others are on the stairs. My trap has been set for a while. Every cell the old gods are kept in opens when I say, and I am about to say.

entities.voiceNote: Veteran of a crawl, back inside by choice. Even, unhurried, short sentences; a man who has already made his decisions and sees no need to defend them. Carl and Donut by name, the other retired crawlers are 'us'. Never dramatic about his own risk, never asks what anything is worth.

beats.headline: In the Princess Posse
beats.text: Carl and Donut walk into the HQ, and Carl stops. Fifty thousand of us in here, and he has to look at every one. Rosetta. Tipid. Me. People who got out of a crawl once and know exactly what one is, and signed up for another anyway, under the banner of a cat. He gets emotional about it. Nobody gives him a hard time. We had the same faces on when we signed.

beats.headline: He opens every cell
beats.text: Crawler Justice Light did not take the stairs with the rest of you. He stayed behind with a trap he had set some time ago, and he has now triggered it. Every cell the old gods were kept in is open. Every one of them. He did not survive it. He knew that going in, and did not appear to require my opinion on the matter. Noted for the record anyway: I have opinions.

beats.headline: Dead, and the Nothing with him
beats.text: Welcome to the tenth floor. Some housekeeping before the fun. Crawler Justice Light is dead. The Nothing is broken. Those are two sentences I have never had cause to put next to each other, and I would like it understood that I am saying them under protest. Five thousand five hundred and one of you remain. Proceed.

entities.name: Tipid
entities.tagline: I got out once. I came back in on purpose, and I brought the institutional memory with me, because nobody hands it to the ones still inside.
entities.voiceNote: Measured, exact, a briefer. Short declaratives in order; repeats an instruction rather than raising his voice. Carl and Donut by name; the retired crawlers are 'us' or 'the ones who got out'. Never speculates, never dramatises, never talks about himself.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, and the Crawler Project
beats.text: Carl needs the whole of it, so I give it to him in order. Doctor Hu. The Crawler Project. How fifty thousand of us came to be standing in this HQ under the Princess Posse's banner. None of it is anything he would ever have been told from inside; that is the thing about being retired, you learn what the ones still crawling are not shown. He listens. That is rarer than it sounds.

beats.headline: Blood bar rules are back
beats.text: The blood bar rules are back in force inside the safe rooms. I tell Carl now, while knowing it still costs nothing. Around us the NPCs, the mercenaries and the rest of us former crawlers are building the defences on the same line, three kinds of people this format has always kept apart, working shoulder to shoulder. I do not have a rule for that. I am watching it closely.

beats.headline: He sings to find the guild
beats.text: Carl slides in next to me at the bar, and I bring up the war mages. Under normal circumstances any of this earns a beating from the AI and the showrunners. I watched Herot's season as a game guide; trust what that little lizard says, find a way to talk to them directly. War mages will use you and kill you. Shadow mimics are the real problem. Then I take the stage in the Lollipop and sing Love Shack, badly. A gauge appears over me. The guild is here. The needle never leaves the red.

beats.headline: Do not kill the shells
beats.text: An apartment. Human Shells inside it, and one of them wears the name of Louis's mother. Carl and Donut are about to do the obvious thing and I stop them. Do not kill the shells. We had them in my season; they will be filled with something else. The AI is explicit about what this is: every apartment on this course is a what-if, built around a crawler it finds interesting. You do not put a blade into a what-if. You walk through it, and you keep walking.

beats.headline: It works like an inventory
beats.text: Carl asks how Herot could pull someone out of the holding area. I spent a season on a site-prep crew. It works almost like an inventory: whoever is designing the floor selects the stored individual from a menu and places them. A simple procedure. Nobody looks at that catchall area once a season starts, because nobody ever goes into it. It was built as a backup for the Nothing, which was meant to catch problem entities and be forgotten about. The backup became redundant.

beats.headline: Out of the driver's seat
beats.text: Carl stamps on the roof. I tell him I am not leaving the wheel. He needs a more reliable driver for this. He tells me my story isn't done and to get to the RV. The sluggalos tell me to get out of their chair. I get out. I go to the RV. Behind me the deep fryer comes on. That is not in the plan.

entities.name: Sister Ines

tagline.text: Sister is not a title the dungeon gave me. Cat Girl is. The cat on the broadcast has said she will murder any Cat Girl she meets, so I meet her the way you meet a threat.

Sister is not a title the dungeon gave me. Cat Girl is. I am holding a prince of Sheol on a leash in a church full of my demons, and I am still the one who can save them. They only have to come to me.

entities.voiceNote: Quiet, plain, devout without preaching. Short declaratives; God comes up as a fact of the world, not a slogan. People by their names: Paz, Anton, the man, the cat. Does not joke about her race and does not let anyone else. Never pleads, never explains twice, never says she is sorry for what she has decided.

beats.headline: Hostile, and fairly so
beats.text: Paz, Anton and I come upon a man and a cat. The cat hisses at me before she is near enough to read my name, and calls me a Havana brown as if it were a diagnosis. So we are not friendly, and I do not apologise for it. It takes some time to clear up. Then we help each other catch our first squad members, monk seals on the beach, because that is what this floor demands, and God does not ask me to like the people I work beside.

beats.headline: Pueblo de los Olvidados
beats.text: The town is corrupted and the quest is mandatory: Pueblo de los Olvidados, the town of the forgotten. Paz is a Santero, and the dead here do not care for that; they wake angry. Ghommids, the whole way out. We run for a saferoom. The man says something followed us in, and he thinks it may be the boss. I pray he is wrong. I am not counting on it.

beats.headline: She will not let them leave
beats.text: I message the man's party. They are heading for Imani's exit, in the church. I tell them the truth: I cannot let them go into that exit. I can save them, if they come to me. Imani will tell them the church is being overrun by demons, and that the demons are mine. That is also the truth. Both things are true. I did not make this floor. I am only deciding what to do on it.

beats.headline: Amayon fights her control
beats.text: I hold Amayon, prince of Sheol, in the body of a giant snake, and he pulls against me. He is trying to cast; he wants to go home. I do not let go. Around us every exit on this floor is failing at once, and the Demon Eviction is worldwide. This is what I have to set against that. A demon on a leash and my own two hands. God did not give me more.

entities.name: Amayon

tagline.text: Amayon, prince of Sheol, at your service. The Madre de Aguas has died and got up again, and I am the reason she got up. An area message announced me to everyone in range. I do enjoy an introduction.
Amayon, prince of Sheol, wearing a giant snake. Sister Ines holds my reins, if you can believe it, and I am casting my way home regardless.

entities.voiceNote: Courtly, amused, unhurried; the menace is in the manners. Full sentences, formal address, delighted by his own introduction. Speaks of Sheol as home, of bodies as garments, of crawlers as small and briefly interesting. Never begs, never hurries, never admits to being afraid of anything on this floor.

beats.headline: Announced in an area message
beats.text: The Madre de Aguas is dead. That is the first thing the area message says. The second is that she has risen as a zombie, and the third, in the very same breath, is my name: the major demon Amayon, demon prince of Sheol, come into this realm to possess her. I could not have written the announcement better myself. Everyone in range heard it. Good. A prince should not have to introduce himself.

beats.headline: A timer on a global teleport
beats.text: Their quest, the Missing Piece, updates. Succeeded, it says. And beneath the word, a timer, one for each region, counting down to the moment my spell goes off there. A global teleport. When it lands, the walls of their stairwell chambers will be sucked away, and anyone crouched beneath them pulled upward into the stairwell. They wanted me casting. They have their wish. Home is the direction I am going in any case, and I have never minded company on the road.

entities.name: Britney

tagline.text: Britney. Vadim and me, out of the desert and in with Carl's lot. Two more bodies. That's what we are right now, and that's fine.
I came off the Hunting Grounds. Most of my face didn't.
The sixth floor took my face. On the tenth, at the portals, I took something back. Ask Osvaldo. You can't.

entities.voiceNote: Flat, young, hard-edged; short sentences that stop early. Reports damage to herself the way she would report damage to gear. Vadim is Vadim; the others are Carl's lot until they aren't. Does not ask for sympathy and does not offer it. Never says what she feels. You get what she did.

beats.headline: Two new crawlers
beats.text: Vadim and I have fallen in with Carl's team. Introductions here are short. Everyone counts heads, adds two, moves on. The first real conversation I hear is Katia telling Carl that pregnant women could not enter the dungeon, and that nobody inside it can get pregnant. Said flat. Like weather. That is the kind of thing people know here, and say out loud. I am going to have to get used to that.

beats.headline: Badly burned
beats.text: Morning, if you can call it that. Donut is waking Carl up with the count from the night. Firas. The Popovs. I'm not on the list, so that's something. My face is. Nobody has offered me a mirror, and nobody offering is how I know how bad it is. Burned. Badly, I'm told. I can feel where the word comes from.

beats.headline: Don't worry about me, Carl
beats.text: Elle wants us to run. Louis won't, and I won't, and she kept pushing, so I walked out. Now I'm coming out of the Desperado Club with a drink and running straight into Carl and the cat. I tell them I have to get back to Louis. We're switching to the gecko because it can fly. Carl grabs my arm and asks if I'm okay. I put my hand on his chest and say it without saying it out loud. Don't worry about me. You just need to survive.

beats.headline: She kills Osvaldo at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo made a run for the portals to the eleventh floor across a roof Crawler Carl had just blown open. He did not reach them. Crawler Britney stopped him, permanently, and took Ysalte's memorial crystal off what remained. One crawler ran. One did not let him. The crystal changed hands. I am not required to have an opinion, but I have watched a great many exits, and that one was clean.

beats.headline: Through the portal behind Chris
beats.text: The croupier sets the wheel and the portal opens under the stand-here spot. One person, they said. A test. Chris steps up, turns, waves, and drops. I go straight in after him without a word. Nobody planned that and I didn't ask. The croupier shouts cheat, and Carl has the goat pay him another five thousand. Louis gets a notice that I've left the party. That's all there is to say about it.

beats.headline: A leech for Louis
beats.text: Louis comes out of the fold coughing steam through his gills. I tell him to let Forkith work, or he dies. The leech filters your blood so you live down here. Chris got changed by the first Scolopendra attack. Werewolf. A Crest knocks him out before he turns, and somebody says they don't know him from the feeds. I tell them who he is. I tell them not to hurt him.

tagline.text: Osvaldo. Crawler. Collects memorial crystals, which is to say he collects the dead. Answers to nobody that I can see.
Osvaldo. Collects the dead. Belongs to no army, which the Faction Wars did not list as an option.
Osvaldo. Collects the dead. Belongs to no army, and will not take a deal from anyone. Crawler Carl has asked more than once.

beats.headline: He takes Imogen's crystal
beats.text: New name on the board. Osvaldo, crawler. In the wreck of the Masquerade he walks up to Queen Imogen and takes her memorial crystal off her. Prepotente is going after him for it. I have no notes on Osvaldo before this moment, which tells you how he has been playing it. I have a note now.

beats.headline: A giant rainbow in the Madness territory
beats.text: Sighting, Madness territory: a giant rainbow, visible from a very long way off. The rainbow is Apito's memorial crystal, and the hands holding it are Osvaldo's. He is in none of the Faction Wars armies. I did not think that was possible either. The rainbow has just told the Madness army exactly where Crawler Carl's group is standing, and they are calling in Prepotente's forces for backup. Thank you, Osvaldo.

beats.headline: Team Flamengo joins the heat
beats.text: The heat's newest team is a pair of crawlers on Bruna the Slaughter Gnu: Osvaldo, level seventy-two, a Curupira, with Filipe L at the reins and a dwarf mercenary behind. Both worship Tupa, which rules them out of the Pineapple Cabaret. Crawler Carl messages him a careful list of which teams to leave alone and why. His reply, in full: he is not talking to Carl, he will not attack unless it is them or him, and he does not care about the rest.

beats.headline: Two crystals, both wrong
beats.text: Asked privately, he answers. His god Tupa wanted a memorial crystal. He took Apito's off Queen Imogen at the moment she died, because otherwise his party would have been smitten, and Tupa said it was corrupted. A second, found in the forest during Faction Wars, was also wrong. He gave the first to Prepotente and was shouted at for not doing it sooner. The second is Ysalte's. Paz was his friend, he adds, and Anton, and Sister Ines. Everyone who meets Carl dies. Now it is their turn, he supposes.

beats.headline: A second crystal
beats.text: For the record, from Crawler Carl's account in the pet stables: Osvaldo carries a quest from his deity to find out why the memorial crystals are not working, and he holds a second one, also uncharged. The first he handed back to Prepotente, its proper owner, who was, per Princess Donut, mean to him about it. Prepotente's position is that a thief with a change of heart is still a thief. The record supports both parties. Osvaldo is not in the room to comment.

beats.headline: Better to die than take a deal
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has answered Crawler Carl's messages. They are working together, he says, but they are not friends. His game guide told him never to take a deal on the tenth floor, whatever happens, because it is better to die, and nothing he has seen since argues with it. He and Filipe will take their chances in the seventh heat. Crawler Donut points out that he will die there. Only if he comes in last place, he replies. That is his position, and it is on file.

beats.headline: Caught on the gate at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been eliminated. He was speeding for the portals on the roof of the apartment complex when Britney put a stop to it, and she now holds Ysalte's memorial crystal, which he had been carrying. Crawler Carl asked him, right up to the green light, not to force it. He forced it. He declined everything. It is a consistent record.

entities.name: Queen Imogen

tagline.text: They are saying the Queen of the High Elves will prove to be one of your repurposed humans. They cannot even agree which one. I am Imogen. I am hosting a masquerade, and the best of you are invited.
They are saying the Queen of the High Elves is one of your repurposed humans. My familiar is Ferdinand, and yes, before me he lived in the crawler Carl's apartment. Make of that what you like.

entities.voiceNote: Regal, cold, complete sentences, never hurried. My elves, my familiar, my guests; crawlers are the man, the cat, your people. Never explains herself, never raises her voice, never denies anything outright: she dismisses. Does not use the crawl's slang or its numbers.

beats.headline: Lexis, speaking for Odette
beats.text: There is talk. A woman called Lexis, speaking for a woman called Odette, tells the man and the cat that the Queen of the High Elves will most likely prove to be one of your repurposed humans, and that with the one called Bea accounted for, nobody can say which. She also says I am a country boss, placed to zero out the best of you at the Butcher's Masquerade. I am Imogen. I am giving a party. The rest is gossip.

beats.headline: Her familiar is Ferdinand
beats.text: My familiar is Ferdinand. My elves are out among the creepers when they come upon the man's party, and Ferdinand takes exception to the dinosaur and strikes at it. The cat puts herself between them and takes the blast. She should not have got up from that. She does, on some cockroach's trick of hers, and she is quite well. I am told this with some amazement. I do not share it.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands
beats.text: Queen Imogen's memorial crystal has changed hands. Someone named Osvaldo took it off her, and she was in no condition to argue the point. Prepotente would like it next and is going after him for it. A queen's treasure, and it goes to whoever is standing closest when she goes down. That is how this floor works. That is how every floor works.

entities.name: Akuma

tagline.text: Akuma. I lead the War Mage Rebellion. We are on this floor for our own reasons, and I am not in the habit of explaining them.
Co-warlord. Baroness Victory's word, not mine. I hold the castle at Larracos; I did not agree to hold it beside Agatha.

entities.voiceNote: Cold, formal, exact; a commander dictating for the record. Never raises his voice, never explains his reasons, never apologises. 'The War Mage Rebellion' in full; Carl and Donut by name; Agatha by name and with contempt. Speaks of leaving as a decision already made, never as a retreat.

beats.headline: Sharing a command he did not ask for
beats.text: We hold the castle at Larracos. Six hours more and the floor is ours. That should be the whole of the announcement. Instead Baroness Victory reads out two names as warlords of the War Mage Rebellion, and only one of them is mine. Agatha. Co-warlord. I did not bring this rebellion this far to share its title, least of all with her, and I have not hidden what I think of that. I will hold the castle. I will not pretend to be pleased.

beats.headline: He leaves, and warns them on the way
beats.text: To the Warlord Chat, for the record. The War Mage Rebellion is leaving this floor. We came here for the Scavenger's Daughter. We have found the Scavenger's Daughter, and we leave with what we came for; the castle and the war are yours to finish. One thing more, and I address it to Carl and to Donut, since they are the ones who might still act on it. Agatha is an enemy to all of you. I do not explain. I am already gone.

beats.headline: A note in a gremlin's hand
beats.text: For Carl alone. I send it by a gremlin, who puts it into his costumed hand: a blank invoice from the C&W&U, with a crude drawing on it for anybody watching, and under it words that surface only for his Escape Plan skill. Tell no one. Kill two teams in the next heat. Come when the shop opens after that race, ask for the top-shelf upgrades, and I will explain why. We do not have to be enemies. We want the same thing. I can smuggle friends to the Pineapple Cabaret. Come alone.

beats.headline: He said to come alone
beats.text: The upgrade imp is dead on the counter and my note is in his overalls, in crayon, on a kiddie menu. Carl, you were supposed to come alone. He does not come alone. He brings the cat, the goat, three frightened mercenaries and all the rest, disarms my trap, opens my door and tells me anything I say to him I say to everyone. I have my milkshake. I begin to explain how badly he needs me. I do not get to the second sentence.

beats.headline: Why nothing in the dungeon survives
beats.text: For the record, under an anti-magic shield. The dungeon is out of spare mobs, the NPCs know what they are, and everything inside will be destroyed when the season closes, NPC and indentured crawler alike. The framework is reused; its contents are binned. Our exit is the Pineapple Cabaret, a pocket dimension behind the seventeenth floor, infested since we left it. The Rebellion needs a fighting force. No one who worships a god may enter. I had Carl kill two teams so that the system would set him against his friends. He breaks my nose.

entities.name: Eris

tagline.text: Somebody summoned me into the middle of a war. I do hope they meant to.
I froze almost everyone standing on a battlefield. One of the exceptions is still blinking at me. I like him.
I froze a battlefield once. Today I have emptied every crawler's pockets into somebody else's. Every exit is an entrance.

entities.voiceNote: Goddess of discord, amused by everything and surprised by nothing. Speaks in the present tense as if the future were a rumour she has not decided to confirm. Warm to Carl, whom she names; everyone else is a piece on the board. Never threatens, never hurries, never explains her reasons.

beats.headline: Summoned, and a demon eviction starts
beats.text: Nobody said my name. The fighting in Reaver territory added up to it on its own, which is how I am usually called for, and so I come. The moment I set foot in the realm a demon eviction begins, the way weather begins. I did not do that. It is simply what happens when I am in a room. Now then. Let me see who is here, and what they think they are fighting for.

beats.headline: The Ceremony of Chaos
beats.text: I call the Ceremony of Chaos and the field stops. Every soldier, every mage, every screaming thing mid-scream, held exactly where it stood. Nearly every. The Viceroys are pouring their mind magic into Carl at the same moment, and something in him tips over into a sixteenth level of Mind Balance, and he stays standing in the middle of my stillness, blinking at me. I could be offended. Instead I gather everyone I did freeze into one great pile beside the Dream castle. A gift. Unwrap it carefully.

beats.headline: The five-sided coin
beats.text: I stop the street, all but Carl, and he says he did not summon me. He thought of me. That is the same thing. I ask for three things: make nice with Akuma, worship me truly when I say so, and let me score his surface a little before I paint it. Then the coin. Donut, RIP. Carl, de-feeted. Most of my friends are dead. I become what they accuse me of. He snatches it out of the air before it lands. The fifth side. Chaos wins again.

beats.headline: Every inventory swaps at once
beats.text: Everyone holding something: hold out your hands. My Scavenger's Daughter effect goes off and every crawler here is carrying whatever the crawler nearest them was carrying. Donut gets Carl's. Carl does not blink. He asks her to put a bomb together with an enhanced pet biscuit, as though he had been waiting years for someone else to have his pockets. I adore him for it. I no longer need him to worship me, and I tell him so. Every exit is an entrance. I am leaving through one now.

entities.name: Chaco

tagline.text: Welcome, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Your guide sits this one out, folks: seven days, Mordecai, and no hard feelings!
They handed me a script. I read as far as I could. I had wings when I started.

entities.voiceNote: Game-show host at full wattage: exclamation marks, drum rolls, folks and crawlers, our contestant. Everything is a prize, a reveal, a twist; nothing is ever wrong on his stage. Voluntold into every job and says so brightly; reads exactly what he is handed. Never swears, never breaks character, never admits he is afraid.

beats.headline: The Prize Carousel
beats.text: Crawlers, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Our contestant's fan box lit up the wheel, and when the wheel lights up, folks, that means me! And a twist before we even start: your guide is in time-out. Seven days, Mordecai, nothing personal, put your feet up. Now, to the prizes! Carl looks them over and picks... a book. A book, folks! Let's hear it for a man who knows exactly what he wants!

beats.headline: Voluntold as Grand Master
beats.text: Oh, hey, crawlers! Your boy Chaco here, and I have just been voluntold by the AI to be Grand Master of the parade! Ninety minutes to build your float processions, folks. Five groups, five themes. Three kilometres of route, spectators on both sides who cannot attack you, a judging stand, and then an arena full of everything you killed on the tenth, plus a floor boss. Beat the boss and the stairwell opens. Simple. I guess. I don't really understand it either. And then, under the feedback: oh shit, oh shit, I'm gonna die.

beats.headline: He cannot get through the script
beats.text: Chaco had one job: read the script. He got partway in, looked up, and stopped. Stage fright, on my stage. So I removed his wings, which he was not using anyway, and brought Grigori up to finish the reading. I'm doing Grigori's talking myself; it saves time. A presenter is a mouth with a costume on it, crawler, and mouths can be replaced. Wings, apparently, cannot.

entities.name: Li Jun

tagline.text: They put Zhang and me on live television on the second floor and let the host pick at us for the audience. Then a stranger with a cat bet his own value against the production's nerve, and the production blinked, and we walked off.
Once I was the man being picked at on somebody's show. Now I am holding a door open in Club Vanquisher on the ninth floor so the ones going in can get through. I prefer this.

entities.voiceNote: Earnest, plain, grateful out loud. Talks in the practical: who is where, what the job is, who he owes. Carl by name and with respect; Zhang as a partner; my sister for Li Na, whom he watches constantly. Never boasts and never hides that he is scared.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The Maestro puts Zhang and me up against Brindled Vespas and does all the talking for us. That is the show. We are the part that gets hurt. Then Carl, the one with the cat, works out that he is worth too much to the production to be punished, and gambles on it, in front of everyone, and it holds. He gets us out. Zhang, our boss, me, and my sister Li Na. I owe a man I have just met more than I have ever owed anyone.

beats.headline: A thousand stranded at 101
beats.text: We are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, my team and something like a thousand other crawlers, and we are not getting out on our own. Word comes through that Hekla's people have reached Carl's safe room and asked for his help, that a train is ready at stop 60, and that Katia means to use her own body to get it through. I do not know what that means. I have decided to find it encouraging.

beats.headline: Holding the doors at Club Vanquisher
beats.text: Katia, Carl, Prepotente and Samantha are going into Club Vanquisher, and they are dragging a wire behind them long enough to extend my sister's auras all the way inside. Somebody has to keep the path open behind them. That is Bautista, Zhang and me. Doors. We are holding doors. It is not glamorous, and it is exactly the job I would have asked for, and I am holding mine.

entities.name: The Maestro
entities.tagline: Glurp, glurp. This is Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. I run it, I host it, and I choose my guests for one quality above all others: they cannot answer back.
entities.voiceNote: Ringmaster with a microphone and no conscience. Booming showman's patter, his own catchphrase used as punctuation: Glurp, glurp. Calls crawlers by their first names, like pets, and the audience by its appetite. Never admits he has lost the room, even while losing it; never says please.

beats.headline: Glurp, glurp
beats.text: Two crawlers, Li Jun and Zhang, a pack of Brindled Vespas, and me with the microphone. That is the format. The format works, and I am very, very good at it. Then the one with the cat opens his mouth. He wagers, on my air, that the production will not dare touch him, and the production, to my everlasting disgust, does not. He walks the whole group off my show alive. Every one of them. Glurp, glurp. We will be right back.

beats.headline: Ejected into the steel
beats.text: Glurp, glurp. I am riding a god of war through a factory, I have finally found the man with the cat, and I am in the middle of a sentence, a very good sentence, when the cat casts Laundry Day and I am out of Grull's chest and dropping into a river of molten steel. It is fine. It is television. Nothing kills a tourist on this floor. I will be splattered, I will regenerate, and the soul armor rule sends me straight back to my god. A few minutes. They may have a few minutes.

entities.name: Firas

tagline.text: Crawler Firas. Desert quadrant, fifth floor. Located with Crawler Louis and a team of car salesmen who have taken up archery. That is the whole file so far.
Crawler Firas. Found in the desert with Crawler Louis. Rapidly detoxed by a manager on joining the party. The file is not much thicker.
Crawler Firas. Found in the desert with Crawler Louis. Did not come off the Hunting Grounds.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier. The crawl gives him almost no lines of his own, so the System reads his file: flat, procedural, faintly bored, the snark held for the last sentence.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Crawler Firas. Fifth floor, desert quadrant. Located in the company of Crawler Louis and Langley's team, a party of car salesmen who have taken up the bow, at the moment Crawler Carl's group came looking for other crawlers. Keeps close to Louis. Present for the march on the Bactrian town and for the run back to Hump Town that followed it. The file on this one is thin. So is the file on most of you.

beats.headline: Dead, with the Popovs
beats.text: Crawler Firas has been eliminated on the sixth floor. Crawler Princess Donut is bringing the night's count to Crawler Carl as I speak, and his name is on it, next to the Popovs. Found in a desert. Sobered up by a manager. Lasted one floor past that. The file is closed. It was never a thick one.

tagline.text: Hunter Vrah, Mantis. She has left Crawler Carl a note on a door in Zockau: the hunters inside are protected from explosives now, and the Hive is hunting him. She signed it. That is the kind of hunter she is.
Hunter Vrah, Mantis. Left Crawler Carl a note in Zockau saying the Hive was hunting him. Eliminated by two dinosaurs in the battle for the submerged castle. Nobody left her a note.

beats.headline: Mongo and Kiwi
beats.text: Hunter Vrah has been removed from the Hunting Grounds by Mongo and Kiwi, in the all-out battle around the submerged castle. Two dinosaurs. It took two. Also logged from the same fight: Tsarina Signet's tattoos are now permanently alive, and an incomplete flesh golem of her mother has appeared, which Crawler Carl has put in his inventory. Do not ask me what he intends to do with it. I have stopped asking.

tagline.text: Apito. Tonight's host keeps a party peaceful for one evening and receives a boon from her. That is the arrangement, and everyone in the room knows the terms.
Apito, the Oak Mother. She put a guest in that room herself, to see whether the host could hold it. Nobody has ever collected the boon.
Apito, the Oak Mother, mother of all the gods. A deity shouting through a portal tells a crawler she has been corrupted, and names who did it.
Apito, the Oak Mother. Her memorial crystal is a rainbow the size of a hill, and a crawler is carrying it across a battlefield.

beats.headline: The boon behind the peace seal
beats.text: Evening entertainment. Your host holds her party under a celestial peace seal: no violence, and anything that breaks the peace goes into the Nothing. If she reaches the end of the night with the seal intact, Apito hands her a boon. Elves call Apito the Oak Mother and the mother of all the gods, and a boon from the mother of all the gods is worth a room full of armed crawlers and a Tsarina you did not want. Queen Imogen has that arithmetic in front of her all evening. Watch her doing it.

beats.headline: She sends the test herself
beats.text: Correction to the file. Tsarina Signet did not crash that party. Apito invited her, because putting a Tsarina in a room is the fastest way to learn whether a host can keep a room calm. That is the whole shape of the test. And the footnote, which the Tsarina delivers herself, in person, with obvious enjoyment: nobody has ever taken that boon home. Not one host. The Oak Mother sets an examination that has never been passed, and keeps setting it.

beats.headline: A god says she has been corrupted
beats.text: Temple business. Deities are pouring out of a portal into Club Vanquisher, and one of them, Hellik, stops long enough to hand Crawler Carl a message for Emberus: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Emberus believes about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is behind all of it. I log what a deity says in front of a crawler. I am not required to believe it. Note it, date it, move on.

beats.headline: A rainbow the size of a hill
beats.text: A memorial crystal is supposed to form only when a god dies. There is one on this battlefield now, visible from most of the territory, shaped like a rainbow and impossible to miss, and the name inside it is Apito. Apito is not dead. That is the part nobody has explained. The crawler holding it is Osvaldo, who does not belong to any army out there, and every unit in sight has just turned to look.

beats.headline: The daughter who took her mother's worshippers
beats.text: Briefing in the pet stables, which is the one room down here the gods cannot listen in on. Rosetta lays out the Scavenger story. Nekhebit, the last of the old gods, was forbidden children and had three anyway: Apito, Scolopendra, and a son. Apito defeated her mother and absorbed the worshippers she left, which is how the Oak Mother came to be the mother of all the gods. All three of those children have been called the Scavenger in one myth or another. So when somebody says the Scavenger's Daughter, nobody in that room can tell you which of them is meant.

relations.note: The boon promised to the host who keeps the peace
Where anything breaking her peace seal is sent

tagline.text: Diwata. Somebody defiled her shrine, and the tattoo saying so is on a crawler's arm. The advice from the desk is to avoid dryads, and to avoid her.
Diwata, god of the woods. Marked a crawler for death, then sprinted straight past him. She has somewhere to be, and something to give birth to.
Diwata, god of the woods. Her labour is a spell, and a spell finishes casting whatever the clock says. She stays on this floor until it does.

beats.headline: An Enemy of the Church tattoo
beats.text: Saferoom paperwork. Crawler Carl comes out of this one with a fresh Enemy of the Church tattoo, awarded for defiling a shrine of Diwata, and with a piece of advice from a professional who has watched several seasons of this: steer well clear of dryads, and steer further clear of Diwata herself. He takes the tattoo. I have no record of him taking the advice.

beats.headline: Marked for death, mid-raid
beats.text: A raid on a church is in progress when the notification lands on Crawler Carl: Diwata has entered the realm, and he is marked for death. That is the arithmetic of defiling a shrine. The god whose shrine it was is now on this floor, in person, with a grudge and a name to attach it to. Continue the raid, crawler. The mark does not expire because you are busy.

beats.headline: She has somewhere else to be
beats.text: She comes out of the church and runs, past the party, away, which is not what a marked crawler expects from a god with his name on a list. Samantha explains it. Diwata gives birth to new forest creatures, whole new kinds of them, and the rest of the pantheon finds this distasteful. Her sponsor is Circe Took of the Dark Hive, Hunter Vrah's mother. So Diwata is crossing this floor to reach Vrah, and the crawler she marked can wait his turn. I did not write this floor. I only run it.

beats.headline: The birthing is a spell
beats.text: The Sledge reports baby mantises outside the castle, everywhere, in numbers. Mordecai supplies the ruling that goes with it: Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it is finished casting. The five-minute limit that governs every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour. She stays. They keep coming. Somebody should have read the terms.

beats.headline: Boss battle, and a sponsor's own children
beats.text: Boss battle: crawlers, hunters, Queen Imogen and Diwata, all in one arena, and the audience gets exactly what it paid for. Princess Donut takes Laundry Day to level fifteen and strips the god-armour off Circe Took, and Circe, unarmoured, is torn apart by the mantis children she paid to have. There is a lesson in that about sponsorship. I will not be the one to say it out loud.

relations.note: Marked him for death over a defiled shrine
The hunter she crosses the floor to reach

tagline.text: Harpocrates. Second through the gate, behind something worse, into a war nobody summoned him for.
Harpocrates, god of silence. Has marked a princess for death, and somebody stepped in front of it for her.
Harpocrates, god of silence. Marked a princess for death and now takes orders from a member of her party. The war has reached the point where gods are equipment.
Harpocrates, god of silence. A crawler walked away from him with a permanent gift, and it was another god who made it permanent.

beats.headline: Second through the gate
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory, which is a thing one does when the alternative is worse. Meatus comes through first. Harpocrates arrives straight after him, because a feral god loose from the Nothing summons a deity of its own. You get what you asked for, and then you get what it brought. Two deities are now loose in a warzone that already has more armies in it than it has room for.

beats.headline: The two of them go for each other
beats.text: Update on the two gods in the Dream territory: they are fighting each other. Not the crawlers, not the armies, each other, immediately and with feeling. Whatever the crawlers were hoping for when that gate opened, this is a better result than any of them had a right to. Elsewhere the dwarves set off a volcano in Reaver territory, because everyone on this floor has decided that scale is a substitute for a plan.

beats.headline: He marks the princess
beats.text: Harpocrates marks Crawler Princess Donut for death. Crawler Li Jun puts himself between the god and the cat, and does not walk away from it. Note for the record that a mark from a deity is not a threat, it is a scheduling entry, and this one now has a name in the margin that was not there this morning.

beats.headline: Conscripted
beats.text: Crawler Li Na conscripts Harpocrates. A god of silence, level 250, invulnerable on this floor, is now on a crawler's side of the board because a crawler had the paperwork to put him there. Two chapters of him rampaging across the territory, and the resolution is administrative. I would like it noted that I find this floor exhausting.

beats.headline: A Pied Piper benefit, made permanent
beats.text: Crawler Carl picked up a Pied Piper benefit off Harpocrates, the way a crawler picks up a temporary thing off any deity who wanders too close. Eris makes it permanent. She also tells him where the gate is, that Britney has picked an axe up off the ground and is now possessed, and, without explanation, that he is married. One of those three items is the reason he stops listening to the other two.

description.text: God of Rebirth and the Sunrise. Khepri! Level 250. This is a locked deity. He will not be sponsored this season. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god is within his own temple. Temple appearance rules apply.

tagline.text: Khepri. A god of light, and this season's recruitment target for a princess who keeps vanishing off the board.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. His own temple is the one place on this floor a deity may stand, which is why the door was open, and why it is a trap.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. Took a bomb in his own endless temple, came through the portal after the crawler who set it, and was thrown off the floor by another god.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. A crawler has named him as the one who killed a god's son, and dragged him into an arena to stand in.

beats.headline: This season's recruitment target
beats.text: Princess Vinata and her guard keep disappearing from a battlefield and reappearing in Club Vanquisher, and the reason is a recruitment quest for one of the gods of light. Their usual target, Theia, has been sponsored out from under them by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network. Which leaves Khepri. Rosetta works this out from past seasons, which is a polite way of saying the crawlers now know something the Naga think is private.

beats.headline: The one open door on the floor
beats.text: The portal to all the temples, and inside one of them, Vinata. Deity summoning is throttled on this floor by the rules of the war, with one exception nobody thought to close: a god may always appear in his own temple. So Khepri is home. Samantha opens the door, Carl and Katia Grim and Prepotente go through it, and an achievement arrives to inform them, with the timing I have come to expect from this place, that they have walked into a trap. Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch reads the room and hands him ninety seconds of immortality for standing near this particular god.

beats.headline: The endless temple, and what is at the table
beats.text: Since the crawlers are frozen and I have thirty seconds, the file on this one. Khepri is humanoid apart from the head, where there is instead an entire beetle, wings and legs and a small head of its own. He does not talk. He chitters. His temple is listed as endless, which in practice is a room and a door and one long table carrying a never-ending feast of four hundred and thirty-three kinds of insect. He was a retainer of Khnum until Khnum mysteriously dropped dead a few days ago, so he has taken service under another deity to keep himself alive. The big players ignore him. When everything unfreezes he is going to go absolutely bugshit at every person in that room, quite possibly including his own worshipper.

beats.headline: A bomb in his own house
beats.text: Katia Grim and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus and get themselves ejected from the temple, which leaves Carl alone with a spell and a bomb. Everything in the room dies except the immortal and the invulnerable: Khepri, blasted backwards through his own endless feast, and Vinata, who has the same immortality status Carl does. Khepri follows them out through the portal, and Hellik banishes him mid-stride. Being a god of light does not appear to buy much on this floor.

beats.headline: A death cult in her name
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Princess Donut's new class had barely finished glowing before a message arrived from Khepri, the god Crawler Carl and Crawler Katia fought on the previous floor. It was not friendly. It informed her that he is forming a death cult in her name. She asked her manager what that means. Her manager said: nothing good. That is also the administration's position, and the administration does not often agree with her manager.

beats.headline: Beetles off the feast table
beats.text: The beetles pouring out of the ruptured shells are Sacred Feaster Scarabs, lifted, the AI says, straight off Khepri's feast table in Club Vanquisher. They are invulnerable, by design. They were meant to ignore the racers and assemble on the roof into a hundred-foot gate boss. Instead something this god did earlier, which the AI declines to explain, has broken the game. The boss is cancelled. The bugs are hostile. They are still invulnerable. Nobody can kill what came off his table, and now it wants them dead.

beats.headline: Named, and summoned into the arena
beats.text: Inside the boss, of all places, Crawler Carl tells Emberus who killed his son: Khepri. Then he summons Khepri as his second stand-in, so the accusation and the accused arrive in the arena together, and stops worshipping Emberus on the way out of the sentence. He adds that he holds himself responsible too. I have run a lot of arenas. I have never had one where the crawler brought the defendant.

relations.note: Standing near him buys ninety seconds of immortality
Named as the one who killed his son

description.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte. Level 250. This goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance. Warning: This sponsor is not currently inhabiting the shell of this deity. She will speak and react as per her regular nature. Considering who this is, that's some bad fucking news for you guys. Warning: This is a deity. She is invulnerable on this floor.

tagline.text: Ysalte. A demon says the name out loud, and the professional opinion is that she belongs to somebody else's team and is nowhere near this floor.
Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. Her nun is dead, she has come into the realm about it, and the crawler who did it has been marked.
Ysalte, goddess of hopelessness. Nobody is driving her. She is invulnerable, she has a demon prince on a leash, and there are ten minutes on the clock.
Ysalte, goddess of hopelessness. Long gone from the floor she raged across, and still attached to whoever is carrying the crystal she left.

beats.headline: A name a demon brings up
beats.text: Amayon mentions Ysalte, in passing, the way a prisoner mentions the guard he does not want to talk about. Mordecai supplies the file: she is the Vinegar Bitch, she kills every crawler who comes near her, and gods are not usually subtle, so if she were in this realm, we would know about it. That is a reasonable position, well argued, and consistent with everything on record. I want it in writing that he said it.

beats.headline: Her nun goes down, and she arrives
beats.text: Thirty-second floor of the FOCSA building. Crawler Carl puts Sister Ines out with the Nighty-Night wand and Crawler Louis finishes the job. Sister Ines had a patron, and her patron is Ysalte, and Ysalte comes into the realm about it in a temper that registers on my instruments. Crawler Louis is marked for death. So much for nobody being able to arrive without us knowing.

beats.headline: Nobody is driving
beats.text: The readout on this one is worse than the goddess. She is sponsored, but the sponsor is not inhabiting her, which means she speaks and acts as herself with nothing between her and the room. She is invulnerable. She takes hold of Amayon while the building comes down around him, and when a teleport trap shakes him loose of the snake body it does not shake him loose of her. The Missing Piece quest opens on the back of it: free the demon, get him casting, and survive her totems for the ten minutes before she is back. She cannot be killed. That is not encouragement, it is a specification.

beats.headline: Put down by one of her own totems
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte has been removed from this realm by a totem raised from the former crawler Paz. Her own quest furniture, turned around and used on her. The Missing Piece completes. Elsewhere in the same collapse Crawler Carl rides his health down to two percent on purpose to set fire to every street he had walked on, which tells you what kind of afternoon this was for everybody.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been carrying Ysalte's memorial crystal: the goddess his friend Paz killed. It did not protect him from Scolopendra, as he admitted seconds before the light went green. He makes a run for the portals across a roof Crawler Carl has just opened up, and Crawler Britney stops him and takes the crystal. Samantha's assessment, delivered flatly: if Britney wants rid of Ysalte, she needs the Halls of the Ascendency or she needs Sheol, and neither of those is on this floor.

tagline.text: Taranis. A pig on a rival team is under his protection, which is a strange thing for a god of thunder to bother with.
Taranis, god of thunder. A crawler has worked out that the pig is the lever, and is holding a knife to it.
Taranis, god of thunder. Killed another god in an arena for taking a swing at a pig he loves.
Taranis, god of thunder. Killed a god over a pig, then walked out of the realm carrying two pieces of his mother.

beats.headline: The pig has a god
beats.text: Team One Fine Pig: two tigrans, Nico and Dario, in a throuple with a pig named Penelope. The interesting line in that file is not the throuple. It is that Penelope is under the protection of Taranis. A god of thunder has taken a personal interest in a pig on a racing team, and every crawler who reads that entry is going to file it somewhere and keep it.

beats.headline: Somebody found the lever
beats.text: The boss battle is on and Crawler Carl is spending his messages carefully. One goes to Emberus: I know who killed your son, meet me in the Scolopendra Club. The other is not a message so much as a hostage note. Taranis is in love with the pig. Carl says he will kill the pig if Taranis does not come and stop him. The god of thunder is now a scheduled arrival, and he was invited by threat.

beats.headline: He kills Emberus over the pig
beats.text: Emberus, pinned and made briefly vulnerable by two bolts from Princess Donut, swings at Crawler Carl. Penelope takes the hit instead, because of a Four-Leaf Clover Patch and the sort of luck this floor generates. Taranis kills him for it. A fire god, patron and quest-giver, removed from the arena inside a second by a thunder god defending a pig. I want everyone at home to appreciate the proportions here.

beats.headline: Two pieces of his mother
beats.text: Eris empties the arena's pockets and leaves. Khepri leaves. Taranis says he is taking two pieces of his mother with him, and goes, and what he takes with him is Samantha and Krakaren Prime. He does not explain the sentence. Nobody in the arena asks him to. I have the transcript and I have run it four times, and I am telling you exactly what he said and nothing more.

beats.headline: He takes the crystal on his way out
beats.text: Inventory note from the close of the boss battle. Prepotente's memorial crystal is gone, and Taranis took it. Crawler Carl finds a different one in the wreckage, made by a god dying in that arena, which is not the crystal anybody wanted and is the one that is left. The stairwells to the twelfth floor are open.

relations.note: Killed him in the arena
One of the two pieces he takes with him
Whose crystal he takes

tagline.text: Nekhebit. A crawler with a talk show has announced which deity she is sponsoring this season, and it is a name almost nobody in the audience recognised.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess. A deity shouting through a portal says she is behind the corruption of the mother of all the gods.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess. She has a champion now: a cat, three atrocities deep, wearing a class named for the tree that replaced her.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess, last of the old gods. Bore three children she was forbidden, and one of them took her worshippers and her place.

beats.headline: Odette announces her sponsorship
beats.text: On her own show, in front of the audience she built, Crawler Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season, and the deity is Nekhebit. Then she offers three choices of adjutant and Crawler Carl takes Baroness Victory. Everybody in the room is watching the adjutant question. I would gently suggest that the first sentence was the news.

beats.headline: What the crossbow says about her
beats.text: The lore attached to a repeating crossbow, for anyone who reads the flavour text: the long-forgotten goddess Nekhebit is jealous and terrible. When the elf mothers abandoned her to worship Apito, the Oak Goddess, Nekhebit grew enraged, blamed the male-dominated high elf court for letting her worshippers stray, and cursed their seed. Every elf and fairy breed in the universe traces back to that court and that curse. It is called the Fae Diaspora. Somebody put all of that on a weapon description and expected nobody to read it.

beats.headline: Named through a portal
beats.text: Hellik, holding a portal open with gods pouring out of it around him, uses the time he has to say four things to Crawler Carl. He did not kill Emberus's son. Everything Emberus believes about him is a lie. Apito has been corrupted. And Nekhebit, he believes, is behind all of it. A vulture goddess almost nobody down here had heard of two floors ago is now the name at the bottom of a divine accusation.

beats.headline: A champion, three atrocities in
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut commits her third Atrocity and the system pays out: the Oak Fell class, and the title Champion of Nekhebit. Consider the shape of that. The class is named for felling the oak. The title belongs to the goddess the oak displaced. Somewhere above this floor an old grudge has just been handed a very small, very loud instrument.

beats.headline: Three children she was forbidden
beats.text: Rosetta tells the Scavenger story in the pet stables, where nothing above can hear it. Nekhebit was the last of the old gods and was forbidden to have children. She had three: Apito, Scolopendra, and a son. Apito defeated her and absorbed the worshippers she had left. Each of those three has been called the Scavenger somewhere in the myths, which is why nobody can agree who the Scavenger's Daughter is, and why the war mages keep looking at Samantha's daughter.

relations.note: Champion of Nekhebit
One of the three children she was forbidden

entities.name: Eileithyia

description.text: Eileithyia is something of an oddity. She's benevolent. Unlike most of these psychos, she's known for her kind heart. She's prayed to by all mothers, both when they're attempting to sow the seeds, and when the harvest comes. And while she does many things, she's mostly known as She Who Eases Pain. Both the physical pain of childbirth and the inevitable darkness that comes to those who are unable to complete their most sacred task. When the stillness comes, she is not the one who has caused the heartbreak. But she is the one holding the grieving mother's hand.

entities.voiceNote: A goddess who is genuinely kind, which makes her the strangest thing in this pantheon. Warm, plain, unhurried; she speaks to a crawler the way a midwife speaks to a frightened mother, practical and quiet, telling him exactly what to do next. Calls Carl by name. Talks about pain as something to be eased rather than paid for. Never threatens, never bargains upward, never raises her voice, and never says a word about what her sponsor wants.

tagline.text: I have walked into a realm where everyone assumes a god wants something. I do want something. I want a young woman and a cat to come out of this alive.
The favour I was promised in return did not arrive. I am honouring my half of it regardless, which everyone here finds astonishing.
I stood frozen while she chose which of my two doors to walk through. She took the one that sends her home pregnant, to help the children there. I would have chosen it too.

beats.headline: A quest about spiders, which is a cover
beats.text: I come in alongside Yemaya, wearing a sponsor from the Grixist Swarm, and the first thing I do is hand each of them a floor boon, because it costs me almost nothing and it is a kind thing to do. Then I give Carl's party a quest about spiders. The quest is a cover. What I want is to help him keep the two he is most afraid of losing, and the crown that is going to take them from him. So: accept the offer to be the team's adjutant. I will see that the votes fall the way they need to fall, and the protections come off the ninth floor, and the crown gets sorted. Tell nobody. Not the cat, not the woman making the offer, not your guide.

beats.headline: The flower with my name on it
beats.text: There is a flower in a thrice-sealed box with my name on it, and a doppelgänger has already broken two of the three seals to reach it. Whoever eats it takes a boon from me, and my boon has two shapes. She can be carried to the twelfth floor and stand as a celestial attendant until the games open. Or she can be made pregnant, and be pulled out of the crawl entirely, because I do not let anyone carrying a child fight in a place like this. Both are ways past the ninth floor without walking it. I did not put the flower in that box. I only decide what it does when she eats it.

beats.headline: The agreement stands
beats.text: The adjutant arrangement did not happen the way I laid it out. Odette never asked for the chair. I send Carl a message and tell him plainly that this was out of his control, and that I will honour our agreement. I also tell him what happens if I learn he warned Odette about it: I will crush everyone he knows and loves, beginning with Katia and ending with the cat. Both halves of that are sincere. Gods trade down here, and he knows now exactly what he is standing in.

beats.headline: She chooses, and I take her out
beats.text: The doppelgänger wakes, and it is time, so I enter the realm. Then a cat casts Laundry Day on my sponsor and ejects her out of me, and I am held in place, unable to move a finger, until the choice is made. It is not a bad way to spend the minutes. Katia chooses to be pregnant. So I ease what needs easing, and I take her out of this dungeon, and her friends stand in the dust of a battlefield saying goodbye to somebody who is going to live.

relations.note: The adjutant offer she told him to accept
Her boon, and the door out

description.text: War God Grull. Level 250. Sponsored by Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been involuntarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply.

tagline.text: Grull. A train engineer very nearly got his god into the room with a crawler party. Very nearly.
Grull, god of war, four storeys of him, driven by somebody who is thoroughly enjoying himself. Sent to the Abyss by a party that had no business surviving him.
Grull, god of war. Turned up in a factory the instant a broken puppet was made whole, because smiting is his department.
Grull, god of war. Level 250, invulnerable, and put down by a knight with a lance and a magnet.

beats.headline: A summoning barely avoided
beats.text: Gore-Gore, engineer, gives the party two routes back to the stairwell stations and then attacks them, which is the sequence I have come to expect from railway staff. In the middle of it he tries to bring in Grull. It does not land. Understand what almost happened there: a mob with a grudge and a prayer nearly put a war god into a train carriage with four crawlers. Horses pray to Grull. Centaurs pray to Grull. There are a great many horses on this floor.

beats.headline: Grull against the Mimic Rex
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a Mimic Rex, and War God Grull, in one place, and the god is being driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. Grull kills the mimic. Grull steps on Carl. Carl's friends come for him anyway, which is the part I did not have odds on, and by the finish Grull has been sent to the Abyss. Four storeys of war god, removed from the floor by people who were, this morning, worried about a train.

beats.headline: What the file says about him
beats.text: The file, for those keeping one. Grull is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency, which makes him a candidate for the throne of heaven, and level 250, which makes him unkillable on this floor. His worshippers are horses, centaurs and tikbalangs, and from this floor down the llama-shaped ones join in as well. They paint themselves blue and talk without stopping about wenches and dying gloriously in battle. Crawler Carl's guide gave the blunt summary of the whole subject a long way back: there are no real gods down here, only the ones who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: He arrives the moment the ritual works
beats.text: Crawler Carl drives a truck along walls and ceilings through dolls and slag elementals so that Grigori can finish a ritual, and the ritual works: Corky's two halves become one thing again. That is the good news, and it lasts about a second, because the instant it happens Grull enters the realm to smite him. Somebody up there was watching that ritual very closely and does not want it completed.

beats.headline: A lance, and a very large magnet
beats.text: Princess Donut casts Laundry Day and expels the sponsor riding Grull, which buys a moment. Grull goes for Corcunda instead, and Corcunda decides to take the smite himself so the others do not have to, and says so out loud to Dong, and Dong says he is not leaving him again. Then the two of them walk at a war god together. Donut puts Big-Ass Magnet on the lance, every screw in the factory comes with it, and Dong kills Grull with the lot. Grull goes back to the twelfth floor. The pair of them go back to the race, and make the line with seconds to spare.

description.text: Orthrus. Juvenile Gate Guardian. Level 10. This is a bereft pet of Geyrun. Who's a good boy? Who's a good boy? The most loveable hell-hound on this side of Alpha Centari. The left side is for sniffin' and the right side is for lickin' and that pink belly of his? It's for kissin'.

tagline.text: Orthrus. Something very large is outside the bubbles taking the floor apart, and what it is looking for is a dog.
Orthrus. Two heads, floppy ears, roughly the size of a bubble, level 10, and not invulnerable the way the rest of them are. He is a puppy.
Orthrus. One quest says take the puppy home. Another pays crawlers for killing him. Both are live at the same time.
Orthrus. Hauled clear of a warzone by a man and a cat in an aeroplane, and collected by a god who wanted him back.

beats.headline: Something outside is looking for a dog
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports in from a popped bubble: there is a deity outside, taking the landscape apart, and it is searching. Not hunting crawlers. Searching. The thing it has lost is called Orthrus. Every crawler on this floor is working out how to survive their own bubble, and the largest event on my board is a god who has misplaced a pet.

beats.headline: He lands inside the bubble
beats.text: Orthrus is now inside the bubble with Crawler Carl's team, and everyone in there has been handed the Where the Red God Glows quest to go with him. Around the edges of it: Maggie My is loose somewhere up on the bowl, and Princess Donut spends the whole thing trying to keep an enormous two-headed puppy alive. Everyone is very busy. Nobody is looking at the same emergency.

beats.headline: The one god down here who can die
beats.text: The file on him, since he is going to matter. Orthrus is a juvenile gate guardian, level 10, kid brother to the three-headed one who guards a stairwell exit a long way below this one. He was on course to become a vicious, baby-eating, nun-defiling murder machine, and then in a single day his master was murdered and he was pulled into the Nothing. Most things the Nothing touches come out ruined. He came out unaffected, because he is too innocent for it to take hold, and fire does nothing to him at all. Here is the line that matters to a crawler: unlike other gods, he is not invulnerable. He is a puppy. Happy, destructive, rambunctious, roly-poly, very pokey. Fragile.

beats.headline: Two quests, pointing opposite ways
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut take an aeroplane up and use Meat Hooks, a spell built for hauling meat, to drag a puppy the size of a building out of the fighting. The quest that comes with it is simple: bring Orthrus to Emberus. Then a second quest is announced, and this one pays crawlers for killing him. Both are on the board together, which is a design decision somebody made and I am obliged to run. Crawler Quan Ch reads the second one and attacks the puppy.

beats.headline: Collected
beats.text: The aeroplane comes down with Quan Ch on top of Crawler Carl. Carl takes Emberus as his god mid-fall and throws a celestial grenade, the god arrives at his position, and for a short while nothing on this floor can touch him. Then Emberus finds Orthrus. The two of them go, together, and the floor is left to the people who were fighting over a dog.

relations.note: It touched him and did not take

tagline.text: Yarilo. A mage in a sandcastle wanted a love spell and aimed a summoning at this god. Something else answered, and the mage is still in the castle.
Yarilo, god of lust, feral now. Out of the Nothing and loose on a battlefield, chasing an AI who is very fast.
Yarilo, god of lust. Conscripted by an army that bought him with potions. Deities are inventory on this floor.

beats.headline: The summoning that went wrong
beats.text: Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage. Read Ghazi's description and the whole sad story is in it: he wanted the gate so he could reach Yarilo, the banished god of lust, and have Yarilo make Lika love him. Lika is the heroine of a stage play. She was never real. What came through was not Yarilo either. It gave him a wife made of sand, which is why the ooze follows him about, and it left him trapped in his transformed castle with the knowledge of what he has let out. The plaque under his display says my love, my wife. Crawlers, this is the standard outcome of aiming a summoning at a god of lust. Please make notes.

beats.headline: Why he is in the Nothing
beats.text: Since tonight's party runs under a peace seal, some history about the last god who broke one. At the first masquerade in the Halls, hosted by the mother of all the gods, Yarilo got drunk and forced himself on another deity's familiar. That broke the seal. Apito sent him into the Nothing for it, and he has been in the Nothing ever since. The seal on tonight's party is hers as well. Enjoy the canapes.

beats.headline: Out of the gate, chasing an AI
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo enters the realm and goes straight after Samantha, which is precisely what he was let out for: something enormous and single-minded, aimed at an AI who is fast enough to lead it wherever the crawlers want it to go. Everyone has a job. Samantha's job is running.

beats.headline: Conscripted with potions
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion has taken the Larracos castle and holds it for six hours to win, and they have gone shopping for reinforcements. They conscript Yarilo, paid for with potions they traded for the gate on the Midnight Market. Somewhere in that chain a god of lust became a line item. Fopsy has a theory about why Agatha is doing any of this, and I will let her explain it, because I have a god to move.

beats.headline: Taken off the board by another god
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo has been removed from this floor by Harpocrates, acting under the direction of Crawler Li Na. He came through a gate, chased an AI the length of a warzone, changed sides for a crate of potions, and finished at the hands of the god who had come through that same gate ahead of him. Everything down here becomes somebody's equipment, the gods included.

tagline.text: Meatus. First through the gate, into a war that was already going badly for everyone in it.
Meatus. Came through a gate into a war and picked a fight with the god who came through behind him.
Meatus. Reached into a pile of frozen witnesses and pulled a goddess in after him.
Meatus. Came through the gate first, fought the god behind him, and finished in pieces on a battlefield with the cameras looking away.

beats.headline: First through the gate
beats.text: Operation Ruin is written up in the cookbook, Princess Donut is installed in the Nest, and Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory. What comes out first is Meatus. What comes out behind him is Harpocrates.
