Neither of them was requested by name, because that is not a thing the gate offers, and both of them are now on a floor with four armies on it.

beats.headline: He picks the other god
beats.text: Meatus and Harpocrates start fighting each other. Of every direction those two could have chosen on arrival, the crawlers have drawn the one that costs them nothing, which after the fortnight this floor has had feels less like luck and more like an apology. In Reaver territory the dwarves set off a volcano, so the ledger balances.

beats.headline: He pulls a goddess into the pile
beats.text: The pile of witnesses is frozen, conscious and invulnerable, which is a combination I would like on the record as not my idea. Princess Donut casts Rolling Battle Formation on the whole heap and starts it moving. Meatus reaches into it and drags Eris in with him. A goddess of discord, inside a rolling ball of frozen soldiers, on a battlefield. Somewhere the Party Planner is coming apart and Crawler Louis is falling into a castle, and it is still the second most interesting thing on this floor.

beats.headline: Chopped, and nobody watches
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut casts her War Crime spell and Meatus comes apart into pieces. I closed the eye of the Scavenger's Daughter for that one, on the grounds that even she does not want to look at it, and I stand by the decision. Harpocrates swears revenge for him and leaves the realm. Two gods came through that gate. Neither of them is on this floor now.

relations.note: She opened the gate that brought him

description.text: God of Blacksmithery and Armor Ogun. Level 250. This god is not sponsored. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been temporarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply. He's here now because Ogun strongly believes all punishments should be handed out in person.

tagline.text: Ogun. Two crawlers get a quest from their own god, and it is not phrased as a request: fix my shrine, not theirs.
Ogun, god of blacksmiths. His shrine was not the one they picked, and he is coming into the realm about it.
Ogun, god of blacksmiths. Handed out a debuff nobody can heal, took a worshipper's life for a choice that worshipper did not make, and went home.

beats.headline: A quest from their own god
beats.text: Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, Paz, Anton and Sister Ines get themselves to Asojano's shrine intact, which required flagging a ghommid splitter named Skylar Spinach and a certain amount of nerve. Asojano begins a ritual. And in the middle of it, Paz and Anton receive a quest from Ogun, who is their god: only one shrine down here can be fixed, and he would like it to be his. Note the position those two men are now in. Note who put them in it.

beats.headline: The shrine they did not pick
beats.text: Deities appear from every direction, each of them making a case for their own shrine, which is the single worst committee meeting I have ever had to render. Then Katia Grim messages Carl: repair Yemaya's shrine or lose her and the cat to the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. So Bomo repairs Yemaya's. The ghommid settlement is freed, Carl walks away with slugpox and a card made out of Asojano, and Ogun enters the realm to punish his worshippers. Not the crawlers who chose. His own.

beats.headline: The outsider at the anvil
beats.text: The file, for the people about to meet him. Ogun is an outsider, one of the old gods, from an obscure pantheon that has dissipated into time, and until a minute ago he was the last surviving member of it. He spends his days at a celestial anvil, angrily making armour, piece after piece, and nobody knows why he does it or where the armour goes. It is said the pieces are a strange shape, all of them cut for four-legged beasts. He is a god of blacksmiths and armourers now. He was something considerably larger once, and his power and his ambition make him a real contender for the throne of heaven.

beats.headline: Punishment, in person
beats.text: Ogun puts a debuff on Paz that nothing down here can heal. Crawler Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton to shield him, and Ogun kills Anton instead, and leaves the realm having taken exactly what he came for. Paz, going, spends his last minutes telling Carl and Donut two things about Sister Ines: her race makes everyone near her want to protect her, and it gets stronger the longer they are near her, and before the crawl she was a murderer. Sister Ines turns Paz into a card rather than lose him.

relations.note: The one who repaired the other shrine

entities.name: The Sledge

tagline.text: Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Me and Bomo work the door.
Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Bought once at the bar, then written into a contract. I belong to her court now.
Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. I got inside that castle, I cast Zerzura, and everything standing in it came away with me.

entities.voiceNote: Short flat sentences, one thought each, nothing decorated. Says the plain hard thing and then stops talking. The Princess, Bomo, Carl, Louis, all by name and nothing more. Never complains about a job, never explains himself, never refuses the Princess anything.

beats.headline: Bought at the bar
beats.text: Two crawlers come up to the counter and buy security. Me and Bomo, sold as the pair. That is the arrangement in this place. You pay, and we stand between you and whatever comes through the door. The cat is not what I expect. She orders a dirty Shirley in a bowl with extra cherries, drinks the whole thing, and then she wants dancing, so I do my version of the robot while she bops and twirls on my shoulders. Princess Donut. I let her.

beats.headline: A miss on his own shift
beats.text: A crawler goes for the Princess on my floor, on my shift, and I do not get there in time. Elle puts the second one down. Astrid comes to apologise in person, and I stand where I am and wait to hear what a miss like that costs a body like me. Carl does not ask for blood. He asks for me and Bomo, permanent and complimentary, the Royal Court's own security every time they walk in. So now I have a court.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Carl's lawyer trades the Gate of the Feral Gods back, and I am part of what he gets for it. Four of us, free of charge: me, Bomo, Clay-ton, Very Sullen. Two spells on top, one for Bomo and one for me, copies of what the artifact could do. Bomo gets the jump to the stairwell. I get Zerzura. Nobody explains Zerzura to me. Nobody has to.

beats.headline: Surviving is winning
beats.text: Louis is worried about how it is going. Whether the plan holds, how it looks, who comes out on top of it. Surviving is winning, Louis. Everything else is bullshit. Then the changelings and me go into that castle, through a turret and the elf inside it, which is the thing everyone outside said could not be done.

beats.headline: He finishes casting Zerzura
beats.text: The battle is everywhere and my job is to stand still and finish the words. So I stand still and finish the words. The castle goes. The whole building and every NPC breathing inside it, taken out from under the people who thought they owned them. That is what the spell was for. I said I did not need it explained.

entities.name: Astrid

tagline.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. Hand-sized, tuxedo, severe bun, and she can make your heart beat until it catches fire.
Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager, and none of that was the part worth knowing. Ask the two dancers crying in the strip club whose mother she was.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice. The System keeps the file on club management the way it keeps files on everything with a level: rank, class, capability, and what the record does not explain. Carl and Princess Donut are guests, Katia Grim is a contractor, and the club is the club.

beats.headline: The management apologises
beats.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, Cardiovascular Mage, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. The Bloodlust Sprite is one of the rarest and deadliest things her kind produces, born holding magic over anything with a circulatory system, and the signature trick is a heart beating fast enough to catch fire. She is the size of your hand, she wears a tuxedo, her hair is up in a bun, and her voice is deeper than yours. A crawler makes an attempt on Princess Donut on club grounds and Astrid comes down to say sorry in person. The Royal Court walks out with permanent complimentary security. Establishments like this one do not hand out refunds. She handed one out.

beats.headline: A contract on the management
beats.text: There is a job out on her, and Crawler Katia Grim has taken it. The preparation is thorough, which is the compliment: Samantha parked at the bar to make noise, Katia getting herself ready, Carl setting traps down the service corridor they expect the assistant manager to walk. Nobody in the building tells her. That is the arrangement everyone employed here works under, and she has known it longer than any of them.

beats.headline: She goes to meet the demon instead
beats.text: The distraction runs too hot, reaches the casino floor, and pulls Minge out of one of the doors to the Nothing. A minor feral demon on the premises during business hours. Astrid does not go anywhere near a service exit. She finds Carl, tells him she is releasing the Vorpals to put the thing down, and tells him to get everyone out. And while the floor empties she says two things she has never once put on record in all the years this club has been running: that she has children, and that her husband is the Night Wyrm.

beats.headline: The contract closes
beats.text: Astrid, assistant manager of the Desperado Club, is dead. Crawler Carl killed her in the club kitchen, at the moment she moved to shield him from the demon, and the body went back to the Night Wyrm to close out the contract he had put on it. Her husband. Before it, she asked Carl to tell him she had done it to keep them safe: him, and their children. The Vorpals she had already released went and put the demon down without her, which is the sort of thing good management arranges in advance.

beats.headline: Whose mother she was
beats.text: Two of the dancers out of the Penis Parade are sitting in the strip club crying, and here is why. Damascus Steel and Anaconda are her sons. Everything an assistant manager's influence is worth had been spent quietly, for years, keeping those two off the record and out of anyone's way. Her husband ordered the contract. Damascus wants every dancer in the Parade hired on as a mercenary where it is safe, and after that he wants his father.

entities.name: Ghazi

tagline.text: They call me the Mad Dune Mage. The sandcastle out on the dunes is mine.
I am a glass mage. I opened a hole to ask a god for one small thing and something else came through it, and now everything I own is sand, myself very nearly included.

entities.voiceNote: Self-pitying and grandiose in the same breath; a scholar's vocabulary spent dressing up a want. Explains himself at enormous length to anyone in the room and blames the thing he summoned for what he chose. Lika by name, always. Never says the word coward, never mentions the lie he told the College unless cornered, never asks after anybody else.

beats.headline: What he wanted
beats.text: They come in through the fountain court, three of them and a dinosaur that shatters my Lika where she stands, and then they find me, so you may as well have all of it. Lika is a half-naiad trobairitz out of the stage plays they put on in the city. A bard cleric under a vow of celibacy, played by a different half-naiad every season, based on a minor deity, and not real. I know she is not real. I wanted Yarilo brought back out and asked to make her real, and to make her mine. I told the College of Magecraft I was studying the Gate of the Feral Gods for stable long-distance transport. What answered when I opened it was not Yarilo. It was something else that had learned to wear the name, and it is why this castle is what it is.

beats.headline: Married to the ooze
beats.text: She tricked me. That is the part I want written down. I asked for Lika and the thing married me to the ooze instead, and my wife is still down in my halls being exactly what she is. The doll in the fountain, the one with a soul sitting in it, that is the nearest thing to a real Lika this world ever managed. Carl knocks me flat and takes the winding box off me while I am out. I wake up with a headache and tell them everything anyway, because who else is there to tell.

beats.headline: Out of the castle, and no further
beats.text: Ghazi, human, level 43 glass mage, known across the quadrant as the Mad Dune Mage, is dead. The sand ooze went down, the sandcastle came in on itself, and Crawler Katia Grim carried him clear of it. She killed him in the open a moment after that, for the notes in his coat explaining how the artifact is worked. He went to sand. Carl and Princess Donut were still buried under the other end of the building and heard none of it.

entities.name: Henrik

tagline.text: Henrik. Principal of the Dromedarians at Hump Town, and the reason there is a man in the basement with pieces taken out of him. Except that it is not Henrik in there.
Henrik. Changeling, principal of Hump Town, one third of an artifact, and a body sitting in a flooded submarine.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice: the file on a man who is not the man, kept flat and procedural because the impersonation is the only interesting entry in it. Wynne, Carl, Princess Donut by name. The System does not speculate about which of the two of them the town liked better.

beats.headline: The basement under the town hall
beats.text: Hump Town's town hall, and a good number of the Dromedarian guards are not Dromedarians. In the basement is Wynne, held as collateral, and Wynne is willing to say who has been working on him. Henrik. Principal of the town, changeling underneath, level 50. What he wants out of Wynne is a spell that will put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus, and the method for getting it has been to take Wynne apart slowly enough that he might change his mind. Crawlers from the subterranean quadrant appear at the boundary and put Wynne down before any of it concludes.

beats.headline: He explains the collateral
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut sit down with Henrik, charmed, and he explains how collateral works here, which is the local economy in miniature: Wynne held against the truce with the gnomes, and an ambassador, Leon the Commissar, who comes to inspect and casts a spell to make sure the collateral has not been swapped for a changeling. The next inspection is due in two days. How the code between the two sides actually works, he does not volunteer, and nobody in the room expects him to.

beats.headline: The delegation to the gnomes
beats.text: The plan walks out of the hall in a line: Carl, Princess Donut, Firas, Louis, a reanimated Wynne, and a Henrik who is Katia Grim doing his voice, not very well. They meet Leon, the Gnome Negotiator, and present Wynne as a man in urgent need of healing. Princess Donut announces herself as the healer and asks for passage onto the Wasteland in exchange. Leon will take Wynne and the healer and nobody else; the cat will not go without her manservant.

beats.headline: The body in the submarine
beats.text: Henrik of Hump Town, changeling, is dead, and has been for some time. Katia Grim runs into the flooded submarine to get away from a sharktopus, and Carl finds the body already sitting in there with its piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods still on it. One magically linked pocket watch, recovered. Also on him: a note recording that Quetzalcoatlus can be put down with an electric shock. Whatever else he was doing, he was still working that problem right up to the finish of him.

entities.name: Hellik

tagline.text: Hellik. God of sun and life, twin brother of Emberus, level 250, and the second half of what Carl signed for: a standing order to kill him.
Hellik. God of sun and life, twin of Emberus, and a great deal more civil in person than the quest attached to him suggests.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice. For most of the crawl this god is a red sun, a line on a quest log and a name on a hit list, so the page is the file rather than the man. Emberus is his brother, Carl is the acolyte, and the System declines to say which brother it believes.

beats.headline: The second quest
beats.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now, and the paperwork comes with a brother attached. Hellik: god of sun and life, Emberus's twin, level 250, said around the celestial floors to be quite obsessed with killing his own brothers, and the likeliest hand behind Geyrun's death even though he was sitting in council with Emberus when it happened. Two quests arrive together with the acolyte's package. Find Out Who Killed My Son. Kill Hellik. The second one has a deadline attached and it is the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: The terms of a family feud
beats.text: What a god's grudge looks like when it is applied to one crawler. No magical item blessed by Hellik may be owned or used, so a whole category of loot is now dead weight. Every shrine of his is marked on the minimap. Every one of his adherents carries a symbol over their head and pays double experience when put down.

beats.headline: It stops being paperwork
beats.text: NPCs who worship Hellik now go hostile toward Carl the moment they see him, no provocation and no conversation required. Inside Club Vanquisher the clerics stand in front of a stained glass door they will tell you shows Hellik bringing truth to Apito, whatever that is supposed to mean. It does not show Hellik at all. It shows the brother above him, and the clerics have had that door wrong for centuries.

beats.headline: He turns up in person
beats.text: The temple goes up, the portal starts letting gods through into Club Vanquisher, and Khepri comes out with the rest of them. Hellik banishes him on sight, in front of everyone. Then he turns to Carl with a message for his brother: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Carl has been told about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is the hand behind all of it. He asks for an alliance. The quest to kill him is still open in Carl's log while he says it.

beats.headline: The clock on the order
beats.text: Quemada worships Emberus too, and Quemada's professional opinion is that the standing order cannot sit unattended much longer. They need to make an attempt on Hellik, and soon. Nobody in that conversation raises what Hellik said in the club.

entities.name: Quetzalcoatlus

tagline.text: A wailing shrieker over the tomb. She has no body, which is the whole of the problem for everybody who wants something out of her.
A wailing shrieker who guarded the tomb until two crawlers worked out where to put the wire.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. She is a guardian mob with no recorded conversation, so the file is what there is: what she is, what she can do, what people are prepared to do to a man in order to get it, and the four ways of putting her down.

beats.headline: A name out of a basement
beats.text: The name surfaces in a cellar under Hump Town, out of a man being taken apart in pieces. Wynne is being worked on to give up a spell, and the spell is meant to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus. Whatever she is, she is worth a body to somebody, and somebody is prepared to do that to a man over several days in order to get her one.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.

beats.headline: How to put her down
beats.text: A note comes off a body in the flooded submarine and it is the answer to her. Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock. A wailing shrieker takes banishment, exorcism, a current, or the destruction of her lover's corpse, and of those four exactly one is lying around this quadrant with the power still running to it.

beats.headline: The panel in the tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is finished. Morris Sp went down the ladder to the submerged panel knowing what the next lightning strike would do to anyone still in the water, connected it, and the current did precisely what the cleric's journal said it would. The Subterranean Quadrant is liberated and the bubble pops. Its crawlers are all named in the notice: Gwendolyn Duet, Low Thi, Morris Sp. Every one of them is dead. That was the price the floor quoted, and they paid it without renegotiating.

entities.name: Big Tina

tagline.text: Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and the reason the dinosaurs keep coming down on Point Mongo.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and an ursine child who never got to finish her solo.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and a daughter with her mother standing in front of her.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. She is a city boss with no speech in the record, and the file the AI keeps on her is the only place her side of it exists at all. Kiwi is her mother, the recital is the wound, and the System reports the rage without recommending anyone go and test it.

beats.headline: The quest gets a name
beats.text: Samantha goes across the water to look at the far shore and finds the team over there dead. All of them, and all of them by one thing. The Recital quest updates with the name it has been withholding. Big Tina. Allosaurus, level 80, immortalized city boss, and the attacks on Point Mongo have been hers from the beginning.

beats.headline: Prepotente Town #4
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut take two more towns and arrive at a third to claim it. There is not much left of the third. She has already been through it, and there is a pattern to which places she visits that nobody has sat down and read yet.

beats.headline: What she actually wants
beats.text: The party goes back into the town for Miriam and finds Big Tina standing in it again, and this time the shape of the thing comes clear. The dinosaurs of the Hunting Grounds were ursine before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack turned them into what they are. Tina was a child when it happened. What she wants, under all of it, is to dance at a recital, because hers was stopped before her turn came. She is also a vampire now, and she is building undead out of what she brings down.

beats.headline: She is brought in, and does nothing
beats.text: The dinosaur squad comes back to Carl and Princess Donut with Big Tina walking in behind them, and everybody in the clearing braces for the obvious. The obvious does not happen. Kiwi puts herself between the boss and the crawlers, and Tina stops. Nobody present can yet say why that works.

beats.headline: The recital, finally
beats.text: In the middle of the battle Princess Donut puts the I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi, and the pack leader is not a mongoliensis any more. An ursine stands there, naked but for the paper bubbles. Tina looks at her and knows her, and the Recital quest closes on the spot. It was never a quest about a monster. Nobody reading the log had any way of knowing that.

entities.name: Kiwi

tagline.text: Kiwi. Level 60 mongoliensis, head of an all-female raptor pack, and the reason nothing else does any hunting on this stretch of ground.
Kiwi. An ursine, heavily pregnant, and until about an hour ago the head of the fastest pack on the floor.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. A pack leader with no speech in the record, described the way the AI describes a mob it privately admires: raptor first, mother second, and the second one only once the record supports it. Mongo is the other dinosaur in the story and the System is not going to be delicate about that.

beats.headline: Mongo runs off
beats.text: Mongo bolts with Princess Donut still on his back and runs a pack of dinosaurs to ground. Kiwi is at the head of it. Level 60 mongoliensis, the fastest and cleverest predators anywhere in this jungle, and the whole pack is female, as is every dinosaur anyone has counted in the area. Which is odd. Odder still: dinosaur-class mobs did not exist on this ground before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack, and here they all are. Mongo and Kiwi settle the introductions between themselves, at length, with Princess Donut obliged to watch.

beats.headline: Charmed, and an escort
beats.text: Kiwi brings the pack in and Princess Donut charms her with a potion, and the fastest thing on the floor becomes an escort service. Carl works out at the same time that The Plenty arranged this entire chain of events, and that what it wanted out of the arrangement was its precious Prepotente protected.

beats.headline: She stands in front of a city boss
beats.text: The squad comes back to the crawlers with Big Tina walking in behind it. Big Tina is an immortalized city boss and everyone in the clearing understands exactly what that means for the next few seconds. Kiwi steps in front of her. Tina does not attack. Nobody yet has an explanation for it that they would put in writing.

beats.headline: Taken all the way back
beats.text: Mongo and Kiwi bring Vrah down together in the middle of the castle battle, which is a sentence worth reading twice. Then Princess Donut uses the I Take It All Back potion on her, and the mongoliensis is gone. An ursine stands in the wreckage, naked but for paper bubbles, and Big Tina looks across at her and knows her mother's face.

beats.headline: Still pregnant, and family
beats.text: Kiwi is very pregnant and has been carrying since the Hunting Grounds, which is a long time to be in that condition even by this dungeon's standards. Big Tina, for her part, has decided that Mongo is her father. Nobody in the fortress has the standing, the courage, or frankly the desire to correct her.

entities.name: Edgar

tagline.text: Edgar. A giant tortoise who talks, and who puts the dead onto Signet's skin where they go on being useful.
Edgar. A giant tortoise who talks, and who can sit outside a building and tell you what is moving around inside it.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. A tortoise with a specialist's skill set and almost nothing on the record in his own words, so the file lists the services instead: ink, reconnaissance, surgery. Signet's family, Carl's plan, Princess Donut's tattoo. The System does not make the obvious tortoise joke more than once.

beats.headline: The ink comes from the body
beats.text: Edgar is a tortoise. Edgar is also the reason Signet's tattoos are what they are, and the method is not squeamish: he works from the corpse. Miss Nadine, dead, goes onto Signet's skin as ink and comes back off it as something that moves and fights. Miss Nadine's attachment to Clint drags Clint along with her, so he turns up on the skin as well, unasked and unbilled. Nobody in the party looks surprised. There is apparently a queue for this.

beats.headline: He maps the castle from outside it
beats.text: Ahead of the castle job Edgar sits well back from the building and maps the whole of it from where he is. Every room, every level, and a set of small connecting tunnels that fit nothing anyone can name. Louis is the one who works out what they are for. They are Ferdinand's, so that he can move around his own house without ever using a door.

beats.headline: Sense Movement, level fifteen
beats.text: Rosetta has a theory about how Vinata keeps getting into Club Vanquisher, and Edgar is the instrument that settles it. He senses the non-corporeal moving through the castle. He also picks up upward momentum coming off the ground, which is what it looks like from below when somebody nearby worships a god for the first time.

beats.headline: A tattoo for the cat
beats.text: Rosetta, Milk and Edgar come up into the tower to work on Princess Donut. She is getting a tattoo, and given who does the ink around here, a tattoo is not decoration. It is a thing that will get up off her and fight when she calls it.

beats.headline: Surgery, on a clock
beats.text: Sixty-five minutes on the floor and every member of the party has a job. Edgar's job is surgery. He and Mordecai operate on Louis while the rest of it goes on above them, and nobody has told the tortoise how long he has.

entities.name: King Rust

tagline.text: King of the Skull Empire. My army is drawn up outside your walls and I have asked for a formal parlay. Do not read anything into that yet.
King of the Skull Empire. My daughter has taken one of my warships and told the Syndicate she intends to pull the switch on this planet with her own hands, and so I am here asking a crawler for help.

entities.voiceNote: A king accustomed to being obeyed who has just stopped being obeyed. Formal, blunt, ceremonial when ceremony serves him; the grief comes through the formality rather than around it. Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, my daughter, my empire. Never begs, never says please, never acknowledges how far the crying has already gone.

beats.headline: The army arrives, and asks to talk
beats.text: My army comes onto the field in good order, the way it has come onto every field for as long as there has been a Skull Empire. The crawlers seal their safe room against us, because they have learned what that doggy door of theirs is worth to an enemy. Fine. Let them shut it. I did not bring an army all this way to go through a door. I request an official parlay with Crawler Carl and Princess Donut, in the correct form, in front of every camera pointed at this floor.

beats.headline: The cat sees it first
beats.text: Baroness Victory reads out the rules of a parlay and each of us stands where we are told to stand. Deng Bao is at my shoulder, a Grixist, as an adjutant ought to be. Carl and the cat come out under the bubble and look at me, and the cat has it before a single word is spoken. I am crying. I have been a king a very long time and I have never once done this in front of an enemy.

beats.headline: What his daughter has done
beats.text: My daughter Formidable has commandeered one of my warships. She has announced to the Syndicate, openly, that she intends to trip the Failsafe by hand to keep the rogue thing on this planet out of the center system. And she told them the rest of it while she was at it: that my empire has been manufacturing their security systems with our own doors left quietly in the back of them. So here it is. I ask a crawler to send my daughter a message on behalf of the people of Earth, and I offer to pull my forces off this floor in exchange. Carl takes the deal.

beats.headline: Walking back to his own line
beats.text: King Rust of the Skull Empire is dead. The agreement was made and he turned to walk back to his own army, and Rosetta Thagra came out of where she had been waiting and took him, for reasons entirely her own and nothing whatever to do with the deal. His army attacked the instant he fell. His ring and his retina went onto a data pad in Rosetta's hands, Carl looted the body, and a parlay conducted in the correct form in front of every camera on the floor ended in the one way the rules had not covered.

entities.name: D'nadia

tagline.text: Princess of the Prism Kingdom. Small, as kingdoms go, and a considerable force in certain trade circles. I say what I think on air, and I have just watched them shoot my friend.
Empress now. I am judging a pet contest, which makes me part of the production, which is precisely why I am judging it.
I sponsored the cat. A sponsorship is an asset and I have sold the asset. Do not look at me like that. It is trade.
Warlord of the Prism clan. There is a crawler and a cat inside my castle, and everything I have done, I have done for my people.

entities.voiceNote: Warm, physically demonstrative, and blunt to the point of rudeness; trumpets through her facial tentacles when amused. Says 'the Prism Kingdom' in full whenever she is being official, which is often. Treats affection and trade as the same activity and has never noticed the difference. Never raises her voice at anyone she considers beneath answering.

beats.headline: A seat on the Danger Zone panel
beats.text: Ripper Wonton's panel, and the crawler and his cat are on it. I keep reaching for his hand and my claws keep going straight through his fingers, which does not stop me reaching. Then the Skull Empire fire at those two and hit Manasa instead. My friend. The comedian starts treating her death as a piece of political arithmetic, and I tell him to shut his mouth. The Prism Kingdom condemns the action, and I say so on air within the hour: we will bring a grievance against the Skull Empire in the Syndicate Courts.

beats.headline: Empress, judging the pet contest
beats.text: The ball, and I am judging the talent show and the pet contest both. Chaco is running the prize counter. I find the crawler in the crowd and tell him the truth of it: he and his attorney very nearly ruined my buy-in bid, and here I am regardless, judging, which makes me production.

beats.headline: One of the two places
beats.text: Two places in the ninth floor's war came up at once. One of them is mine: the Prism Kingdom's, bought in my own name where anybody watching could watch me do it. The other went to a brand-new non-profit corporation. I know exactly whose that is.

beats.headline: The sponsorship changes hands
beats.text: I sell my sponsorship of Princess Donut. It is not appropriate to sponsor a crawler I may be fighting, and it paid well. Whoever bought it will want something for their money, and that is a matter between the cat and the buyer now.

beats.headline: Marked, and taken by the dinosaur
beats.text: Empress D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom, warlord of the Prism clan, is dead. Crawler Carl marked her with the Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Mongo did the rest. She said at the finish that everything she did she did for her people; he told her to her face that she did it for herself and that her people will pay for it. I am obliged to broadcast both halves of an exchange like that.

relations.note: Sold on, mid-war.
The sponsor slot she sold is the one the tiara comes out of.

entities.name: Cascadia

tagline.text: You have been hearing me since the first floor. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill. Yes. That voice. It is mine, and so is the show.
There is tequila going through the rebreather. I have run out of the face I put on for the microphone.
I asked it to let me die. It said no, and it took my flippers off with the loudspeaker open. Say the line, Cascadia. Say the line.

entities.voiceNote: Two registers with no bridge between them. On air she is bright and condescending, calls the crawlers monkeys and twits, and signs off with the same three words every time. Off air she is exhausted, profane about her own production, and wildly self-pitying about the floor she designed. Says 'the production', 'the network', 'my floor'. Never apologises.

beats.headline: The card system, explained brightly
beats.text: Good morning, crawlers. Today I walk you through the card system, and I do it in the voice, because the voice is the thing you people respond to. Somebody upstairs decided this floor gets decks and totems and a duelling format. Somebody upstairs is always deciding. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: One crisis shy of the failsafe
beats.text: They put the ninth floor's planning meeting in front of me, and the crawler asks after an administrator who has recently stopped attending meetings. So I come through in person, rebreather and all, two feet of me, and I raise my little arms and invite him to try something, because whatever he does to me happens to him as well. I tell the room I am one crisis away from pulling the thing that finishes all of us. The cat suggests moisturiser and cucumber slices and refers to me throughout as Zev's boss.

beats.headline: Coming apart at the warlord council
beats.text: I do not get through the official business. I have a tequila ball and I laugh in Odette's face, and she takes the meeting off me, and every warlord at the table watches her do it. Princess Vinata uses my family in a whisper today, to unsettle a crawler, as though my family were a piece of set dressing she is permitted to move. I let her. There is nothing in what she says that I can dispute.

beats.headline: Everything hurts
beats.text: I press the button, and what comes out is the truth. You're all going to die. You should already be dead. You idiots should have taken deals. You did it to torture me, didn't you? Why are you still alive? Why am I still alive? Why won't you let me die? I sit there with the button held down, bubbling, and every garage on my floor listens to me bubble. Everything hurts. Then feedback, and somebody else gets to the microphone.

beats.headline: The catchphrase, and what it costs to refuse it
beats.text: It wants the line. I will not give it the line. So I ask it, over the loudspeaker, with the whole floor listening, why it will not simply let me die, and it takes several of my flippers off me for refusing. I am the executive producer of this season. I designed a floor. Somebody write that down.

beats.headline: An announcement, mostly about her ex-husband
beats.text: The announcement is meant to cover the outreach guild between the next two races, and the rule that the seventh race runs three teams to a heat with one team walking out of it. I get all of that out. I also get out a great deal about my ex-husband, because the microphone was already open and nobody in this building has the standing to take it off me.

relations.note: Zev answers to her.

entities.name: Asojano
entities.tagline: A god nobody has worshipped in a very long time, standing in a town he used to rule. Level 130, non-corporeal, and wearing a hat that stops him seeing where he is going.

description.text: Asojano - Orisha. Level 130 City Boss. This is a non-corporeal spirit. Also known as the Lord of Smallpox, Asojano is one of the most respected and feared of the Orishas, a former god made flesh upon the rise of the Ascendency. As the worshippers of these gods grew more and more extinct, their temples crumbled, and the power of these former deities waned. […] One day, not so long ago, Asojano found himself here in this small town, visiting the world he once helped rule. There was no malice to his actions. He came just so he could look upon what he once had and what he had lost. Still, power lingers, even in the most forgotten of shells. Asojano is disease incarnate. He kills, and he heals. He is life, and he is death. He also wears a reed hat that makes it difficult to see where he's going, so he bumps into stuff a lot.

beats.headline: A city boss attaches himself to the party
beats.text: I have him at level 130 and non-corporeal, and he is now standing in a crawler party's safe room as though that were a normal thing for a city boss to do. There is a request attached to the company: repair his shrine and the spirits held in this town go free. He asks Paz specifically, which tells you he has read the party's paperwork rather more carefully than the party has.

beats.headline: The ritual at the shrine
beats.text: They reach the temple intact. Carl flags a ghommid splitter by the name of Skylar Spinach on the way, which I enjoyed. Asojano begins his ritual, and at that exact moment Ogun hands his own worshippers a quest of his own: one shrine may be repaired, and he would like it to be his. Paz and Anton read it together. Carl, Donut and Ines start working out how one fights a city boss inside his own temple.

beats.headline: Flagged a heartbeat before he falls
beats.text: Deities arrive from every direction, each with a shrine to argue for. Carl sends Bomo to repair Yemaya's, which settles the argument. Donut and Mongo take Asojano apart, and Carl flags him a heartbeat before he goes, so what remains of the Lord of Smallpox is a card in a crawler's deck. The ghommid settlement is liberated. Carl leaves with slugpox, which is very much the sort of souvenir this floor hands out.

beats.headline: Half of Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang
beats.text: The card gets played. Asojano and Uzi Jesus combine into a single totem, Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, which is either the best or the worst thing to happen to a former god of disease. I have decided not to rule on which.

relations.note: Into the deck.

entities.name: Rishi

tagline.text: I speak for the Blood Sultanate at these meetings. Not royalty, whatever the cat has assumed. A cousin. By marriage.
My arms are off and I am sitting in a crawler's safe room, and I am still the only one in it holding a document worth signing.

entities.voiceNote: A diplomat's register: the clause first, the threat second, and 'harshly' where another speaker would say what he means. Calls Carl 'crawler' and Donut 'Your Highness', with no warmth in either. Discusses his own survival as though it were policy. Never once says what he wants for himself.

beats.headline: A compromise, with a warning attached
beats.text: The crawler tables an action item on Juice Box's behalf: a tenth team drawn from the NPCs, holding the same protections the rest of us hold. My position is a compromise. A team of her own and she will surely dominate the game. So: the unaffiliated NPCs are given invulnerability this season and a safe area the rest of us may not enter, and in return her attacks stop. Should they not, the Sultanate is quite versed in dealing with terrorism and will respond harshly, and I would like the minutes to show that I said so here, first, and calmly.

beats.headline: The Great Consensus, and a fleet
beats.text: They have me, so they may have the rest of it. The philosophy is called the Great Consensus, and Vinata was an adherent of it, and what her circle intended was to steal the entire fleet and run with it, for a generation, in a direction none of the tunnel threads point. I did not walk into that temple beside my wife. I knew what was waiting inside it, and I knew that going in with her made me as dead as she is. So I stayed outside, and buried myself in the dirt, and here I am, with something to trade.

beats.headline: The offer, and the ring
beats.text: For the record: the prisoner offered Crawler Carl a signed instrument granting every native of Earth citizenship in Naga lands, in exchange for the Naga settling the other planets of Earth's system. A real document, and worth something. Crawler Carl marked him with the Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Then he killed him. Sultan Rishi the Usurper, first of his name of the Naga Uprising, is dead.

beats.headline: His belongings arrive in the safe room
beats.text: Housekeeping. Crawler Carl opened a fan box and the entire contents of the late Sultan's inventory landed in the middle of the safe room. Among it: makeup samples for a merchandise line built around Princess Donut, which Princess Donut had not approved, and about which she has a very great deal to say. The cleaner bot has not recovered.

entities.name: Damascus Steel

tagline.text: Assistant lead at the Penis Parade, and the one who can get you through the door you are actually looking for. Look at your elbow, crawler. Now look at mine.
My mother is dead and my father ordered it. I am not asking you for help. I am telling you to put every dancer in this club on a mercenary contract before I go.

entities.voiceNote: Low, flat and transactional, with a bouncer's economy of words. Calls Carl 'crawler' and the customers nothing at all. Warm only about the dancers and his family, and he explains neither. Gives instructions rather than making requests, and expects them followed.

beats.headline: The door behind the club
beats.text: He comes in asking for me by name, and not for a dance, and he has the spiderweb on his elbow that says he is entitled to ask. So I take him to a private cubicle, and out the back of the cubicle, to the entrance nobody advertises. On his way out I tell him to limp, or I take out his knee. Let the room think it knows what happened in that cubicle.

beats.headline: Two brothers on the floor of their own club
beats.text: Carl and Samantha come through the club with the Vorpals still working behind them, and what they find is me and Anaconda flat on the floor, crying, in front of the whole room. The Vorpals take Minge in the same minute. I do not care what any of them see. My mother is dead.

beats.headline: What the family actually is
beats.text: So the crawler gets all of it. My mother and the Night Wyrm were crawlers themselves, a long time ago, and they are our parents, mine and Anaconda's. She spent years pulling strings so the two of us would be dancers rather than something worse, and those strings are gone now. Hire every dancer out of the Penis Parade as mercenaries. All of them. Today. Then they keep breathing. My brother and I have somewhere else to be, and it is wherever our father is.

entities.name: Anaconda
entities.tagline: Level 75, quarter naga, lead dancer of the club's ground floor and the cat's declared favourite of the entire roster. Currently face down on his own workplace floor, weeping, which is not in the routine.

beats.headline: Crying in the middle of a raid
beats.text: Level 75. Quarter naga. One of the lead dancers at the Penis Parade and one of Princess Donut's favourites, a preference she has shared with the audience. Carl and Samantha come up the hidden stairs from the floors below with the Vorpals still at work, and there he is beside Damascus Steel, crying too hard to stand up. The Vorpals take Minge in front of him. He does not look up for it.

beats.headline: Family business
beats.text: Another of the dancers offers to come along and fight. He declines, and the reason he gives is family business. Damascus hauls him up off the floor. He says that if his brother is going after their father then he is going too, and the pair of them walk into the back cubicles, where whatever happens happens off camera.

entities.name: Baroness Victory

tagline.text: Orc. Attorney. Adjutant. I put my own aunt into indentureship over unpaid taxes, and the other parties still had to sue to try to keep me out of this game. The filing was badly drafted.
An Elite walked into the fortress carrying somebody else's sponsorship and a great deal of explosive. He did not reach the second room.
Two names hold the castle at Larracos and only one of them wanted a colleague. I read them out as written.

entities.voiceNote: An attorney first and an officer second: the rule, then the consequence, then silence. Formal address for Carl and Donut, none for anybody else. Fond of a loophole and entirely unembarrassed by her own family. Never threatens, on the grounds that a threat is merely a badly drafted notice.

beats.headline: Three candidates, and the crawler picks the lawyer
beats.text: Odette puts three of us in front of the crawlers on her show, having first announced that she will be performing as a deity of her own this season, Nekhebit, which is her affair. What the crawlers are choosing is an adjutant for the ninth floor. Carl asks me whether he has killed any of my family. I tell him: my half-sister, and nobody but my brother-in-law and nephews holds him responsible; several distant relations, which was within his rights. I recently sentenced my own aunt to indentureship for her taxes. Carl picks me.

beats.headline: Herman the Fleet does not get to finish
beats.text: Carl, Donut, Tipid and Florin come into the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, and Florin walks them through the ceasefire rules. Then our own Elite, Herman the Fleet, leaned on by Sensation Entertainment, reveals what he actually is, which is a delivery system for a bomb. I deal with him. An adjutant may do that. It is in the rules, and I have read the rules.

beats.headline: The rules of the parlay
beats.text: I walk Carl and Donut up to the parlay and give them the rules before we arrive, because a parlay is a contract with a shorter fuse than most. King Rust brings Deng Bao, a Grixist, as his adjutant. Donut notices before I do that King Rust is crying.

beats.headline: A ruling about the goat
beats.text: Most of the Naga army is already dead and Prepotente did it, for what the Blood Hunter show did to Miriam Dom. Carl would like to work with him. My advice is a ruling rather than an opinion: he may not, not directly, not while Prepotente stands outside the Princess Posse. Bring the goat inside the team, or keep your distance from him.

beats.headline: Two warlords for one rebellion
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion holds the castle at Larracos, and six hours on the clock decides the floor. I run alongside Carl and give him what I have, which is less than he wants. Agatha has been named co-warlord beside Akuma, much as Ferdinand was added beside Juice Box, and nobody on that team anticipated it. Akuma does not like her. Their motivations are unclear, even to me.

beats.headline: I am going to level with you
beats.text: Carl. I will level with you. The AI is spread well beyond this solar system. It has killed an entire Mantis system and blown up a group of Valtay-leased manufacturing facilities, and nobody knows how it is feeding itself. Mobs from the dungeon are appearing where they should not. The Plenty control the tunnels, may be the only ones able to shut them off, and have not answered us. So ask Orren's question. He rephrases it, out loud, and the AI lets it go out live.

entities.name: Vinata

tagline.text: Princess of the Naga and warlord of the Blood Sultanate. For these games you are welcome to call me the Whore. It saves everybody a great deal of time.
My house has never once had to finish one of these wars. There is a door out of every castle, and a god standing at the far end of ours.
There is a crawler in my god's temple, and he came through a door I built for myself. Good. Let him stand where a god can see him.

entities.voiceNote: Silk, and delivered very close to the ear. Prefers a question to a statement and a whisper to a speech. Calls Carl 'the crawler' and never by name; calls her house 'the Sultanate' and never 'us'. Offers other people their own dead as though it were a courtesy. Never says what the Naga are actually doing.

beats.headline: A whisper at the warlord council
beats.text: I come and stand at the crawler's shoulder while the council goes on around us, and I put a small question to him quietly, so that he alone hears it. Cascadia has just learned her husband and most of her family are gone, and look at her. How does he imagine he will manage when his own is? He tells me his family is already dead. So I tell him that is not the family of which I speak, and I watch him understand which one I mean.

beats.headline: The door into Club Vanquisher
beats.text: The Sultanate's trick is older than this season of theirs. One of the warlord's guards worships a god of light; the god summons its worshipper to a temple inside Club Vanquisher; the warlord's party travels with her, out of reach of anybody hunting the castle. The usual name on that list is Theia, and this season Theia is sponsored by someone in the pay of the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, so this season the god is Khepri, and a few weeks at a table crawling with beetles. It is a small price for being nowhere anybody can find.

beats.headline: The trap has two immortals inside it
beats.text: They come through the portal into Khepri's temple, the crawler and Katia and the goat, with Samantha opening the door for them. Standing this near this god hands a very few of us ninety seconds of immortality, and it does not enquire whose side they are on. His patch gives him his ninety. Being what I am gives me mine.

beats.headline: Ninety seconds each, and hers runs out first
beats.text: Warlord Vinata of the Blood Sultanate is dead. Crawler Carl set a bomb down inside the temple and stood in the middle of it, and everything in that room without a god's blessing went with the blast. Two of them had one. The crawler and the warlord came out through the doorway wrapped around each other, and while they were still on the ground his slugpox returned to him, and a sluggalo burst out of his back and put a hatchet between her eyes the moment her ninety were spent. The portal is open. There are gods walking out of it into Club Vanquisher.

relations.note: The crown's outstanding requirement is paid in her nagas.

entities.name: Dong Quixote

tagline.text: Seventy years of age, a lance built for a mounted man, and at long last a mount to put beneath it. I dance for my living. I adventured for it first.
Mr. Jefferson has left me, and he has taken something of mine along with him. Corcunda is behind a garage door I am not permitted to open.
A war god is coming for the most beautiful man who has ever lived. He shall have to come through the lance. Vale to you all. Vale.

entities.voiceNote: Chivalric and entirely sincere about it: formal address, archaic flourishes, and 'Mr. Jefferson' for a tube sock full of nickels. Calls Corcunda the most beautiful man who has ever lived and will say it to anybody. Seventy years old, an adventurer before he was a dancer, and unembarrassed by either trade. Says 'Vale' where another man would say goodbye.

beats.headline: A mercenary with a lance and a sock
beats.text: I come through a teleport trap meant for Holger, who would not leave the children, and present myself outside the Madness castle alongside Katia, Imani and Splash Zone, with Bigs the slugalette riding behind me, and I bring with me the lance, which I have carried without a mount since the club came down, and Mr. Jefferson, who is a tube sock of nickels and a better conversationalist than most of this company. And beneath me is a swamp yak that once bore King Rust. Gonk. I am mounted again.

beats.headline: Into the Madness castle
beats.text: Carl and I go deeper into the castle while the great ball of crawlers rolls toward it, and on the way we take two crawlers who did not choose to fight us, conscripted, and leave them bound and unharmed behind us. In the surgical theatre at the back is Architect Houston, midway through joining himself to a changeling's body, with a crawler strapped to the table beside him. I hold the doorway. Carl interrupts the procedure.

beats.headline: Down outside a garage door
beats.text: I go to the garage of the Lady Dominators because Corcunda is inside it, and I fall down before I reach the door. They carry me back to our own garage, where I had left Mr. Jefferson, and Imani is sent for. Whatever she tells Carl, she tells him in silence, and nobody tells me. The quest to bring Corcunda's halves together advances a stage regardless. I did not earn that stage.

beats.headline: His greatest shame
beats.text: There is a way to bring him home. A spell split Corcunda in two, long ago, and his other half never cared for me; join the two with a fleshmancer and he is freed from those women and their team. And I must confess why he left. I did not want him to go back to his other half. I was afraid that once the two were whole again, the whole would not like me either. When he went, he asked me to go with him. I did not. It is my greatest shame.

beats.headline: I shall drive
beats.text: I ran down to the wreck to speak with Corky, and those women gathered him up and carried him into their garage and pushed me aside without a word. So be it. Carl and the princess both laid hands on the controls in that race, and so neither of them may touch them in the next. I shall drive. He says we will talk about it. What is there to discuss?

beats.headline: Nickels, not gold
beats.text: A brawl in the Lollipop, and a crawler singing through it, and so I take up Mr. Jefferson and sweep the stage clear before him, howling as I go. A mantis creature tears the good sock open as I strike her, and out come the coins, and half the room falls upon them. They are nickels. Every one of them is a nickel, though I have been feeding him honest gold pieces. I do not understand it.

beats.headline: The other side of the door
beats.text: This is unbearable, Carl. I am on the other side of the door, and I cannot even see him. He is the love of my life, and what you mean to do will change him forever, and I am not to be allowed to say goodbye. I am dying besides. They call the thing upon me Negative ROI, and Mr. Jefferson has stopped speaking to me, and my health is seeping away. I do not complain of the curse, my good sir. I complain of the door.

beats.headline: Why he fell in love
beats.text: Do you know why I fell in love with him, my boy? I will tell you. There was a battle in the Desperado Club not long after he was split, and I was afraid it would spread to the Penis Parade and we would all perish. Corky put his hand upon my shoulder and said that if we died that day, we would die together, and that is more than most people get. There is no such thing as a sad ending by the side of the people who make you happy. And now his other half stands before me, wearing my scarf.

beats.headline: Holding the halves together
beats.text: They get Corky away from the Dominators and bring both halves of him and a fleshmancer into the back of the truck, mid-race, and my part in the work is to hold the two of them together with everything I have while it is done. I am not well. I hold him anyway. Their two lives become one under my arms, and there is one Corcunda where there had been two.

beats.headline: A charge, and a good death
beats.text: Grull, god of war, came for Corcunda on the racetrack, and Corcunda took the smite to spare the rest of them. Dong Quixote wore the scarf his partner had put about his neck, mounted him, and drew the war lance out of inventory. Princess Donut cast Big-Ass Magnet on that lance and every loose screw in the factory came to it. The pair of them went into Grull at speed, and the lance landed. Grull called it a good death and granted them one. Mercenary, formerly of the Penis Parade. Vale to you all, he said. Vale.

tagline.text: Otter. Water mage. Formerly of the Penis Parade, presently under a mercenary contract with a crawler faction, carrying a crossbow built for something smaller than an otter.
He has gone off this floor to ask the Guild of Suffering where his wife is. Nobody can raise him. I am declining to speculate, and I do not decline often.

beats.headline: One of the dancers, under contract
beats.text: He arrives by teleport trap outside the Madness castle with Katia, Imani, Dong Quixote and Bigs the slugalette, and joins Carl and Elle there. For the file: he came out of the Penis Parade with the rest of the dancers when the club came down, signed a mercenary contract, and has been in every fight since without once being the reason a plan failed. Water mage. Short. Reliable. There are crawlers I could not write that sentence about.

beats.headline: An inventory of the safe room
beats.text: Somebody should keep a list, so here is the list. In the safe room: Splash Zone, Rosetta, Samantha, Bigs, and Tipid, who spends most of his time curled up asleep on the training-room floor. Mordecai is a shadow mimic wearing the shape of a Moon Reaper. Mongo and Rend are out in the garage. Carl walks in and picks up a spell for turning himself into ooze. Nobody in that room finds any of it strange, which is the part I would like noted.

beats.headline: He goes to ask Hamed a question
beats.text: Splash Zone, Gluteus Maxx and Doctor Bones went to speak with Hamed. Carl works out that he cannot raise any of the three, and the reason he cannot is that they are not standing on this floor any more. What he went to ask Hamed for was help in finding his wife. That is the whole of what I am prepared to put in the file.

tagline.text: Hedy. Gremlin, level thirty, vehicle mechanic. Non-combatant, not permitted in your safe room, and the only reason anything you drive sees a second heat.
Hedy. Gremlin mechanic. Still mending what the track breaks, and now telling them which upgrade they actually want instead of waiting to be asked.

description.text: Hedy. Gremlin. Level 30 vehicle mechanic. This is an applicant to be manager of your garage. This is a non-combatant NPC. Hedy is an expert in all things mechanical. If you choose a mechanical-based vehicle, she will be in charge of your garage. Don't let her appearance fool you. She's about as experienced as one can get when it comes to engines. If you can limp your vehicle back to the garage, rest assured it'll be good as new by the time the next heat starts. Warning: Just because Hedy is a non-combatant NPC, it doesn't mean she's invulnerable. If something happens to her, your vehicle will not get repaired between heats. Hedy is not allowed to enter your safe room.

beats.headline: The garage comes with a mechanic
beats.text: Five thousand five hundred and one crawlers arrive, Crawler Donut takes the Assassin of Sekhmet class, and Crawler Donut picks the mechanical vehicle category, chiefly so that it will not eat Mongo. The category comes with an applicant. Hedy, gremlin, level thirty, and the terms attached to her that nobody reads: non-combatant, not invulnerable, not admitted to the safe room, and if anything happens to her the vehicle stops being repaired between heats. Crawler Donut takes her. The other applicant trains animals.

beats.headline: First trip to the garage
beats.text: They drive back into their own garage after the first heat, trailer and all, and are handed the particulars of the next race. Then Hedy puts the upgrade board up, recommends the spider legs above everything else on it, and they take Retractable Legs. I record the choice without comment, except to observe that a vehicle which can stand up is also a vehicle which can fall over.

beats.headline: Arms crossed at the garage door
beats.text: Between heats. The garage door goes up and Hedy is standing there with her arms crossed, and she would like to know what they did to her girl, and why last place. The particulars of the next race come through, and then the audience's upgrade vote, which she presents as a kindness to Princess Donut. Across the same garage Bucket Boy jumps out of the truck to tell Dong that he has seen Corcunda. The repairs get done regardless.

beats.headline: She picks the upgrades for them
beats.text: The upgrade board goes up again and Hedy walks the party through it again, subdued this time, because she can read the room. She has watched what this course does to a chassis. They have only felt it. Her advice is taken, which on the whole is more than the advice of anyone else in that garage that day managed.

beats.headline: Lost with the ice-cream truck
beats.text: Casualty notice. Hedy, gremlin, vehicle mechanic, who drove the ice-cream truck carrying the Faction Wars heads in the procession. The truck is in smoking pieces against the arena wall. Bigs delivers it plainly: we lost Hedy. Crawler Carl says ahh, hell. It was the first time she had been allowed out of the garage.

relations.note: Garage attendant

tagline.text: Jasha. Level sixty-five bugbear of team Free Love. Tie-dye, beads, no trousers, and a vehicle that no longer moves.
Jasha. Bugbear, team Free Love. Repays a favour the same heat he is asked, for people who would not have asked it of him, which on this course is a dangerous habit.

beats.headline: Broken down with a manatee on them
beats.text: First heat, and team Free Love is in pieces at the side of the track: two bugbears in tie-dye and beads, Radoslav and Jasha, one wrecked vehicle, and a Screeching Death Manatee working its way through the wreckage. Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut stop. They put the manatee down, they put the fire out, and they rig a tow. Crawler Donut's assessment is that the beads are overdoing it and these two are undercover police. What they are is two NPCs who have just lost the third of their team, and who remember enough to want to be free.

beats.headline: A plan with five names on it
beats.text: Carl, Donut, Chiyome, Radoslav and Jasha work out a plan between them: get Rapture into Donut's sights and take the shot. The shot is never fired. Team Sparkles chooses that moment to put a hole through team Girth the Trouble's vehicle, and Girth the Trouble is off this floor for good. Five heads, one plan, nothing to show. Plans on this course have a shelf life measured in seconds, and that one did well to reach the starting line.

beats.headline: Carl asks him, of everyone
beats.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut takes the heat, with the Lady Dominators and Crawler Osvaldo's crew close behind it, and the first thing Crawler Carl does with the win is send a message to Jasha: there is somebody still out on the track who can be pulled off it. Jasha asks whether he truly means to save that one, the worst of them. Tow him in if he will let you, Crawler Carl says, and be wary. I file the request itself, because who a crawler asks is a fact about the crawler.

beats.headline: They go back for Dwight
beats.text: Jasha and Radoslav went back onto a live course and pulled Dwight out of it, which is the only reason Team Sparkles is still racing. Crawler Carl suggested it, and Jasha asked whether he meant that one, the worst of them. Nobody would have said a word if they had driven past, and a great many spectators would have preferred it. Team Free Love did it anyway, promptly, for a team that would not have done it for them. I file this under: awake.

beats.headline: Team Free Love is eliminated
beats.text: Team Free Love has been eliminated. The device that did it sat in their own vehicle, placed there by Crawler Carl, and it was triggered by Crawler Carl at the moment Crawler Osvaldo announced he was crossing the line. Somebody in that heat was going to finish last. Crawler Carl decided it would not be his own people, and the two racers he chose to make that true were the two he had once stopped beside a manatee to help. Radoslav and Jasha crewed that vehicle. That is the whole of the notice.

tagline.text: Dwight. Sparkling unicorn, level eighty-seven enchanter, one of two on Team Sparkles. Unicorns are famous for gentleness. Not this one.
Dwight. Sparkling unicorn, level eighty-seven enchanter. Owes his continued participation to two bugbears he has never thanked, and has just put his horn through a disc jockey.

description.text: Dwight. Sparkling Unicorn. Level 87 Enchanter. One of two members of Team Sparkles. I bet you already know what a unicorn is. A sparkling unicorn is pretty much the same thing, but they sparkle because they have even more magic permeating them. Their horns are quite valuable to certain parties, so if you kill him, it's recommended to grab the horn as quickly as possible. Most unicorns are regarded for their beauty and their grace and their childlike innocence. They're generally known for their overly gentle manner. But not Dwight. Dwight is known for being a complete prick. He's the type of guy who would call the police on a kid setting up a lemonade stand. He's the type of guy who, at the office pizza party, would take three pieces, knowing there's not enough to go around.

beats.headline: Team Sparkles goes past
beats.text: Team Sparkles stops in the road just long enough to be rude, Dwight and Lucienne both, and then goes straight over the top of the trailer and the wrecked van when the food truck's horn spooks their mount. In the same stretch of track Crawler Carl works out what this floor is actually for, which is thinning out the NPCs who have woken up, and Elle gets through an awkward meeting with a fan. The Royal Court of Princess Donut finishes the first heat seventh of nine, having spent most of it towing team Free Love home. Dwight finished ahead of them. Dwight would want that mentioned.

beats.headline: A cannon out of the bush
beats.text: Green light. A tank barrel slides out of the side of Team Sparkles' pile of vines and fires point blank into the yellow Chevy Bel Air of Girth the Trouble, whose guck elemental had spent the countdown shouting at the unicorn about his horn and his mother. The car goes straight up like a rocket and comes down burning in the ditch. The barrel peels back like something in a cartoon. Girth the Trouble is eliminated. Dwight tells everyone how girlie that was. Then the bush leaves.

beats.headline: The cannon again, at the line
beats.text: Subject comes up on the left in the final seconds with the cannon hanging out of the slime-covered bush and fires across the finish, into the food truck and the Lady Dominators' GTO alike. All three vehicles go over the line together, airborne. The vine survives, smouldering; so do Dwight and Lucienne, whose helmet is cracked. Dwight wants to see everyone cry, and promises that everyone is dead next race and will be shot first. Then the vine limps into the garage marked 2.

beats.headline: Rescued by people he was rude to
beats.text: Team Sparkles is still in this race, which by every reasonable projection it should not be. Jasha and Radoslav of team Free Love found Dwight spinning in circles just outside the exit and dragged him in. I record outcomes rather than motives, so I will confine myself to the facts: the two who did it are the two whose van he once drove straight over.

beats.headline: The horn and the disc jockey
beats.text: The Lollipop, packed to the walls, Crawler Carl full of bard potions and climbing onto a stage to sing his way into a guild. Dwight is drunk at the front of the room. As the pair of them get up there he drives his horn through the disc jockey's face. The disc jockey had been shouting at him. Beyond that there was no faction in it, nothing at stake and nothing to gain. He simply did it, in a room already full of armed strangers looking for a reason.

beats.headline: One drunk unicorn, one wrecked duet
beats.text: He follows it by hurling the dead disc jockey at Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut, misses, and hits a demon of team Yokai, which draws in the Minister of Blood-Letting and his skeletons and then most of the floor. Carl's allies spend the entire song trying to keep the teams in that room from murdering each other. On the last line of the thing Crawler Donut is knocked flat by a paralysed kappa and loses the entry she had just sung for. Crawler Carl gets in alone. One drunk unicorn, one wrecked duet, one guild place where there should have been two.

beats.headline: Over the roof
beats.text: Heat Five, first place: Team Sparkles, which is to say one drunk unicorn who sat motionless on the starting line while everyone else drove in. According to Jasha, relayed by Osvaldo, he then rode up the factory wall, crossed the roof and dropped off at the finish without entering the building. He was the only racer to work out that this was allowed. Osvaldo calls it cheating. The rules do not, and the rules are the ones keeping score.

beats.headline: Sober, with a missile launcher
beats.text: Dwight arrives at the final heat awake and sober, which is noted. His vine is towing a wheeled cart with a spinning missile launcher on it, which he cannot fire until he clears the low ceiling of the starting blocks. His navigation hologram has been programmed to look and sound exactly like the late Lucienne, and it tells Crawler Carl his low-tier unit is finished. Dwight tells Carl he will suffer as he dies. Carl rolls up the window.

beats.headline: One swipe at the starting line
beats.text: Team One, Team Sparkles, has been eliminated. The light turned green and the timed hole punch opened the shield, the vine-killing potion killed the vine, and a second potion fried the navigation that looked like Lucienne. Before Osvaldo's gnu had recovered from Dwight's own cannon, Crawler Donut was through the window and had removed his head. His horn is now in her inventory. The missile cart never launched. The official notification reads: because, holy shit, that was pretty badass. It stands.

tagline.text: Chiyome. Razor Fox, level eighty, Mistress of Nunchaku. Leads team The Wild Hunt, and throws stars as well as anyone in my files.
Chiyome. Razor Fox, level eighty. Led team The Wild Hunt. Called for help on an open channel while there was still a channel to call on.

description.text: Chiyome. Razor Fox. Level 80 Mistress of Nunchaku. One of three from team The Wild Hunt. Since this is the first time you've examined a Razor Fox that wasn't suffering from an anatomy-changing disease, let me tell you about these little fellas. (And, ladies, since the one you're looking at is a lady ninja, they make the women ninjas wear red because . . . Well, I'm not sure why.) I love these guys. Each one picks a weapon proficiency upon childhood, kinda like a ninja-turtle thing, and they train in both that and in a ranged weapon. Most, like Chiyome here, pick throwing stars as their ranged weapon of choice.

beats.headline: Meeting the neighbours
beats.text: Carl and Donut come out of their garage into the Team Roundabout and go round the neighbours, which on this floor means meeting the NPCs who will be trying to survive the same heats. Among them, three Razor Foxes racing as The Wild Hunt, and the one doing the talking is Chiyome. Level eighty. Nunchaku on the belt and throwing stars beside them. I say on the record that I am fond of Razor Foxes. I do not say that about a species very often.

beats.headline: In on the plan
beats.text: Chiyome sits in on the plan with Carl, Donut, Radoslav and Jasha: Rapture into Donut's sights, one shot, done with it. It comes apart before a trigger is touched, because Team Sparkles destroys team Girth the Trouble's vehicle and Girth the Trouble is gone off this floor. Chiyome does not complain about the wasted planning, which puts her ahead of most of the field on this course and all of the commentary.

beats.headline: The Wild Hunt is eliminated
beats.text: Chiyome reported over the channel that The Wild Hunt was in trouble. Then sugar hermits began falling out of the sky, and Crawler Donut pulled Temporary Macaroni out of her Banquet Fit for a Princess and built a tunnel of it, and Crawler Carl got on the channel to tell Chiyome where to drive. There was no longer anybody to tell. The Wild Hunt is eliminated. The Jugglers with them. The tunnel was a good idea, arriving in the order that good ideas usually arrive in.

tagline.text: Corcunda. Half a mantaur, riding with the Lady Dominators, and the reason Dong Quixote has not drawn a steady breath since he laid eyes on this garage.
Corcunda. Two halves of one mantaur, in two places, in two different suits, and only one of the two will hear a word about Dong.
Corcunda. One mantaur again, whole for the first time in cycles, on a moving vehicle, with a god arriving.

beats.headline: Dong's friend, on somebody else's team
beats.text: Genesis and Rapture, two womantaur dominators, make an appearance and go off to the Hairpin bar. The third member of their team is the one that matters here: a half-mantaur, and he is the friend Dong Quixote is always talking about. Corcunda. A quest opens on the spot to put the two of them back in the same room, which is my way of saying production has noticed that a crawler's mercenary is in love and has decided to sell tickets.

beats.headline: Asleep in the back seat
beats.text: Subject is in the back seat of the Lady Dominators' burgundy GTO at the top of the hill, curled up and hanging out of the side, with an Unconscious notification over his head. He has not fallen asleep during a race. He has been put to sleep, by spell. Crawler Carl walks past him on the way to look at the boss, notes it, and says nothing. His employers have a wide shield over the car.

beats.headline: Dong falls ill at the door
beats.text: Dong tries to get inside the Lady Dominators' garage to reach him and goes down ill on the way. He is carried to Imani. The quest ticks over to its second stage anyway, which nobody on that driveway earned. Imani's reading is that this is not any ordinary sickness. Dong is in withdrawal, and the thing he is withdrawing from is the company of his own sentient sock. I record what the healers tell me. I do not always enjoy it.

beats.headline: There are two of him
beats.text: The shape of the problem, finally stated out loud. Corcunda is not one person in one place. A spell called Split Personality went off a long time ago and split him in two, and both halves lived through it: Corky, riding in the back of the Lady Dominators' car, and Porky, hopping on a single foot behind the doors of the stage performance guild, which Crawler Carl has just sung his way into. Porky agrees to the reunion. Porky also has terms, and the terms are that somebody afterwards answers for how this happened, and that somebody is Dong.

beats.headline: Pulled out of the hole
beats.text: Corky, recovered from the wreck by Princess Donut, arrives in the back of Crawler Carl's truck unconscious, strung out, and cooking inside his own suit, since the Dominators' containment had failed. A doll hitches in on him. Carl throws it out and tears a patch of suit away with it, and a health bar appears. Grigori clears both debuffs. Corky wakes, asks whether the race is over, and is told to lie still, because his other half is beside him and it is time. He calls for Dong.

beats.headline: The ritual, at speed
beats.text: Grigori performs the joining on a moving vehicle while Crawler Carl drives it up the walls and across the ceiling through the dolls and the slag elementals. It works. The halves close, two suits become one mantaur, and Corcunda is whole for the first time in a long time. He gets a moment of it. Then Grull enters the realm to smite him.

beats.headline: He goes to meet the smite, and says it out loud
beats.text: Corcunda knows what the mark over him means: the smite is his, and Grull will not leave until it lands. So he says the rest out loud, in front of every one of them. He never stopped loving Dong Quixote, and now he has to go to Grull. He puts his scarf around Dong's neck. Dong tells him he is not leaving his side again. The two of them go at Grull together, Dong riding. Crawler Donut throws Big-Ass Magnet onto Dong's lance, every screw for two hundred meters comes to meet it, and Grull goes back to the twelfth floor the hard way.

relations.note: Danced there, before the split

entities.name: Jurgen

tagline.text: My wife is Heidi. She is outside this place and she is carrying our child, and everything I do down here is arithmetic about that.
My wife is outside this place carrying our child. Between her and the end of it stands one crawler nobody can reach. So yes, I am desperate. Put it in those words.
My wife is outside this place carrying our child, and the reason I still have the body she would recognise is a boy's crystal and nothing else.

entities.voiceNote: Big, warm, plain-spoken; a soldier who talks like a family man. Brings Heidi into the conversation as though she were standing at his shoulder, because to him she is. Says what frightens him straight out and asks for help without dressing it up. Never boasts about the fighting and never sneers at anyone.

beats.headline: The mystery meat at Hungry Eyes
