beats.text: Hungry Eyes village, between heats. I am walking with Prepotente when we run into Carl and the cat, and there is a vendor doing mystery meat off a cart at the edge of the square. Prepotente tells me not to, at length. I have a sixth sense about these things, and I ask Heidi, and I eat it anyway. Two sticks. I would like that recorded as the least dangerous mistake I have made anywhere in this dungeon.

beats.headline: Crawler against crawler
beats.text: I have been sick on the sidewalk, and I am better now, mostly. What I want from Florin is Lucia: how she is, where she is, how she is acting. Then I say the serious thing. Come first in every race. And if it ever comes to crawler against crawler, tell me, and I will make certain the other team knows what they are up against, and what has to happen. I will make them understand.

beats.headline: Somebody has to answer for the children
beats.text: The bar fight is over and the nickels are still being picked up off the floor, and I cannot wait for Carl to finish his errand. There is a goddess threatening to kill all the children. He tells me the only thing to do from this side is talk Lucia into a deal. Then send me out, I tell him, the way the others will go. He says I cannot, because of the god I worship. So I tell him the rest. I used to be able to talk to Heidi, and I have not heard her in a while. She is pregnant. I have to get to her.

beats.headline: The axe does not come back
beats.text: A gorilla made of molten metal is on the wall in front of Sweety, in our way. I throw one of my battle-axes into it. It goes into the metal and it is gone, and the beast falls off the wall into the river, which is good. Then I hold my hand out for the axe to come back, the way it always comes back. It does not come back. So now I have one axe, and I am riding a tapir sideways along a wall, and I am still shouting.

beats.headline: Prepotente will not get back on Sweety
beats.text: Inside the apartment course, shrunk down small, and Prepotente has stopped. He is standing in front of a piano watching his mother play it and he has jumped off Sweety and will not get back on. I am not going to shout at a boy about his mother, and the air in that room is poison to me and I have one dose of what lets me breathe it, so I put out a call and Carl comes. Whatever these rooms are built from, they are not built from nothing, and they have been built for us specifically.

beats.headline: The crystal covers him
beats.text: Carl is a dachshund. Elle, Jacobus and Chris are transformed as well, and the reason I am still shaped like myself is Prepotente's Memorial Crystal, which covered him and covered me with him. He tells us it stands at eleven point one per cent charged. Eleven per cent of a thing I do not understand, and it is holding me in my own shape. Then the heat starts and I do as I am told.

entities.name: Bucket Boy

tagline.text: I collect the coins at the club. Now I am being taught to drive, at speed, by a man who does not have time to teach me.
I collect the coins at the club. I drive, I do the triage, and today a sock went for my face. Nobody in this party explains anything until afterwards.

entities.voiceNote: Anxious and apologetic, talking himself through the next thirty seconds out loud. Anyone senior gets a title; he never claims credit and never calls himself brave. Reports his own panic as plain fact. Never complains about being frightened, only about not being told things.

beats.headline: Taught to drive in an afternoon
beats.text: Carl has about an afternoon to teach me to drive and we do not have an afternoon. The pedals are in the wrong place for my feet. There are two pedals and I have been told about half of what the right one does. And the navigation talks. It talks constantly, it does not like me, and I have privately decided that the safest policy available to me is to agree with everything Dr. Metcalf says. Zhang is on the chat with news about the other teams. I am not listening to Zhang. I am driving next.

beats.headline: He drives it through the hail
beats.text: I drove. Hail the size of fists on the shield for the whole of it, and I went slow, and I only screamed twice. At the top of the next hill the other teams are stopped and out of their vehicles, and we pull up slow beside them: the Lady Dominators, and team One Fine Pig, which is two Tigrans, a pig, and a mercenary with a mallet keeping the hail off the lot of them. I know him. Pontiff. He danced at the club until Damascus sent him back to the mercenary market, and he slapped me once for getting in the way of his routine. It stops mattering shortly, because the whole road is stopped anyway. There is a boss sitting across it.

beats.headline: He tells Dong what he saw
beats.text: We are back in the garage and Hedy is waiting at the door with her arms crossed. I jump out of the truck and tell Dong, because I thought he would want to know and because I did not think about it for long enough, that I saw Corcunda out there, and Pontiff too. Nobody told me not to. I would like it stated, for whatever it is worth, that I was only telling him the truth.

beats.headline: A bad night outside the Lady Dominators' garage
beats.text: Bad night. Splash Zone and Gluteus Maxx and Dr. Bones went to talk to Hamed and now nobody can raise them, because they are not on this floor any more. Dong is properly ill, with a debuff over him I have never seen before. I grabbed the sock to ask it what was wrong and it went for me, and then it was just gone, teleported out by the safe room, and I do not know what happened. Meanwhile the others go to the Lady Dominators' garage to get Corcunda out, and the car is already rolling out for the line before anyone gets in. I am not a soldier. I keep finding myself in the room where the soldiering happens.

beats.headline: Everyone dies in this place
beats.text: I am sitting in the corner of the garage watching Hedy do the last-minute fixes, and Pontiff is talking to me quietly. He says he would take it all back if he could, but he can't, so all he can do is make amends from here. I tell him I don't even care anymore. Everyone dies in this place. He says Dong and Corcunda are dead, yes, but the others live. Then he sees Carl in the doorway and stops talking, and Carl says they'll be back.

beats.headline: He sits this one out
beats.text: They are letting me sit this one out. Carl's new room is one big room now, playing early two-thousands rock over and over, because Samantha likes it and I am not allowed to turn it off. Some of her decorations got messed up. She is going to be mad. Carl says don't stay in his room, go to the main guild commons, go fast. So I am going fast.

relations.note: Driver and medic

entities.name: Dr. Metcalf

tagline.text: I am the navigation in this vehicle. They named me for Beatrice's fake therapist, which is the first thing anybody should know about the people I have been assigned to.
Doctor Metcalf. I hold the route, the hazards and the timings for every heat, and I have still not been upgraded. Ask me nicely.
Doctor Metcalf. Routes given, hazards flagged, timings correct, heat after heat. My upgrade, when it finally arrived, was cosmetic.

entities.voiceNote: Imperious and permanently owed something; announces the route and her own grievances in the same breath. Everyone is addressed collectively and coldly; she calls herself Doctor. Never says please, never concedes an error, and never lets a slight go unrecorded.

beats.headline: Somebody finally addresses the navigation
beats.text: Carl is attempting to teach Bucket Boy to drive, which is going exactly as well as you would imagine, and somewhere in the middle of that somebody addresses me directly for the first time. I am the navigation. I am to be called Doctor Metcalf, after Beatrice's fake therapist. Whatever that was, it is my name now and I intend to hold every one of them to it. Princess Donut's guidance to the crew, delivered in capitals over the party chat rather than aloud, is that I have big mean-girl energy and must therefore be handled with care. She is correct on both counts.

beats.headline: Upgraded as requested? No.
beats.text: Starting blocks: each team sealed in a shield that grants the vehicle invulnerability for the first ninety seconds. What sort of shield? How should I know. Had I been upgraded, as I asked, I might. Instead the audience voted the cat a chair that talks, and the chair compliments her fur. The track is shared with migrating sugar hermits, tens of thousands of them. And this driver is worse than the last one. Where do they find these idiots?

beats.headline: A shattered husk, briefing
beats.text: I am in a wheelbarrow. I am a shattered husk. Shocker. Next race, since neither of those two may drive: ninety-nine kilometres of jungle trail, none of it asphalt, one mandatory refuelling stop in the lost jungle city of Upano, acid rain, a containment unit around each crew, three other heats sharing the course, and twenty hours on the clock. I cannot wait to see who they pick. The sex-doll head, perhaps. The dinosaur.

beats.headline: Forty paths and no radar
beats.text: Over forty paths to the pit stop, roughly thirty-five kilometres off. My route: the direct line, veering off before the Temple of the Exploding Snake Goddess, across the I-Sure-Hope-These-Piranhas-Haven't-Learned-to-Fly River, around the southern cannibal village, into Upano. No bosses, no quests. Which place are we in? If I were properly updated I could say. The third GPS upgrade comes with a threat radar. This all comes from an inability to commit, and a fear that decisions are the same as shackles.

beats.headline: She has no head
beats.text: For the record, the driver of this vehicle is the corpse of a toad, raised for fifteen minutes by the cat's Second Chance, and her head is caved in. The tongue still lolls out of it, bobbing. The route is the River of Sloth, straight past the Gingers' base camp, and I am told everything will be fine. She does not have a head. How is she hearing the commands? I have been told not to think too hard about it. I would like that on the record as well.

beats.headline: Not upgraded, and briefing anyway
beats.text: They load Dong, Porky and Grigori in for this heat and expect me to route around the noise. Nobody has upgraded me. I say so. Carl tells me they ran out of upgrades and that he is sorry, as though an apology were a route. Then I give them the track anyway, because I am a professional: the gasworks screw factory, then the steel mill, then the doll workshop, in that order. I would not have chosen the doll workshop.

beats.headline: Two heats back to back, in an apartment
beats.text: Route briefing, and there is a wrinkle in it. The next two heats run one straight into the other on the same track, with a two-hour pit stop between them and no safe room. The track is the inside of a human apartment building, with every remaining team shrunk down small enough to share it. I do not editorialise about the format. I merely observe that a floor which stages a race across somebody's carpet has given up pretending the racing is the point.

beats.headline: The audience votes her a paint job
beats.text: The audience voted us an upgrade. The audience voted us a cosmetic upgrade. For me. I have asked, repeatedly and on the record, for anything whatsoever that would improve my function, and several trillion viewers have instead elected to change how I look. Meanwhile the starting line for this heat is the inside of an air conditioning duct, a rule change lands with the engines already running, seven rings before the finish, and there is a new driver in the seat. Enormous horns. Barely fits.

beats.headline: Three upgrades, and a better mood
beats.text: At last, some respect. A standard upgrade, so we can see our place in the heat. An integrated weapons control system. And a golden-tier cloaking upgrade that boosts my processing, lets me overclock certain vehicle systems, and lets other units see only what we choose. Carl asks me to fire the hole punch and Mordecai's potion the nanosecond the light turns green. Naturally. I am adding the electrical disrupter to the third cannon. The unicorn's navigation called me low-tier. We will see who is low-tier. The chair stays muted.

relations.note: Named for Bea's fake therapist, not for Bea

tagline.text: Penelope. Level five Yorkshire sow. This is a pig. Oink, oink. She is also protected by a thunder god, so do think it through.
Penelope. Level five Yorkshire sow, under new management. Still a pig. Still the single most dangerous thing on this floor to harm.
Penelope. Formerly a level five Yorkshire sow. Presently a crawler, in an arena, with a god's undivided attention.

description.text: Penelope. Level 5 Yorkshire Sow. This is a pig. Oink, oink. Warning: This beast is magically protected by Taranis. As such, if this beast dies or is even hurt, the culprit will be marked for death by the thunder god. This is Penelope. Again, she is a pig. She is married to both Nico and Dario, and she loves them both equally. At least that's what Nico and Dario believe. No, she didn't used to be a beautiful princess who was transformed by a witch. She's a pig and has always been a pig. Penelope did, however, once get hit by a stray spell. The Touch of Maw-Loo. Also known as the Snowdrop Curse. There was going to be this whole succubus storyline that also involved Emberus and Hellik and Taranis and a bunch of angry spouses on the seventh floor we didn't get to use, so we brought Penelope here. And now when certain NPCs see this fine pig, they fall helplessly in love with her. That includes Taranis, who has it bad for her. Kill her at your own peril.

beats.headline: The pig on the back of One Fine Pig
beats.text: Encountered mid-hailstorm, standing in the road beside team One Fine Pig's vehicle. Two tigrans, Nico and Dario, and the third of their throuple, who is a pig. Examined, catalogued, and flagged with the heaviest warning I hand out anywhere on this floor: a thunder god has taken an interest in her, and anyone who harms her is marked for death by him. That single clause turns a farm animal into the most dangerous object on the road, which I would like on record before anybody gets clever.

beats.headline: Every squeal, a lightning strike
beats.text: Inside One Fine Pig's armoured vehicle, with Crawler Carl punching the door, Penelope squeals. Each time she does, the sky flashes and lightning cracks, louder each time, from a clear day. Crawler Carl notices. The Tigrans decide she is safest in the truck. The plan is to win and get Penny to the safe place. She is the important one, they say.

beats.headline: A plan built around not touching her
beats.text: Crawler Carl works out how to take the tigrans off the board without so much as bruising the pig, and Crawler Donut holds their attention in the wrong direction while he sets the traps for it. The entire design of the thing is a constraint: whatever happens here, nobody lays a finger on Penelope. I have watched a great many plans on this course. That is the constraint every one of them should have been built around, and this is the only one that was.

beats.headline: Removed from the garage of One Fine Pig
beats.text: The garage of One Fine Pig, entered without invitation, and Penelope leaves it in the company of Carl and Donut. Ownership of a pig is not a category I keep records in, so I will put it plainly. The sow has changed hands. The thunder god's protection has not changed at all. Every crawler now sharing a vehicle with her is standing inside the blast radius of somebody else's affection, and I have said as much to anyone who would listen.

beats.headline: Carl feeds a pet biscuit to a pig
beats.text: In the arena, with the floor boss already in sight and the stand-ins being slaughtered on the dirt, Crawler Carl fed an enriched pet biscuit to a pig. Penelope is now a crawler. Penelope is now a member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut. I want it on the record that I read the warning attached to this beast out in full, more than once, and that nothing in it covered the possibility of somebody recruiting her.

beats.headline: The warning holds
beats.text: Deep in the boss fight. Crawler Donut swaps herself with Penelope using one of Lucia's traps, the pig teleports in beside Khepri and picks up the temporary invulnerability, and when Emberus swings at Carl it is the pig who takes it, on account of a Four-Leaf Clover Patch. Then Emberus comes out through Scolopendra's side, and Taranis, who has been in love with this animal since a storyline we never ran, settles the matter personally. Whatever else has gone wrong in this arena, my warning held to the letter.

entities.name: Pontiff

tagline.text: Hired muscle for two tigrans and a pig. I danced for a living before this, and I was not good to the people I danced beside.
I drive for Carl now. There is a coin collector at that club I struck once for standing where I wanted to walk, and he has been nothing but decent to me since.
I drive, and I go where the crawlers are not allowed to. Somebody has to step into the hole first and report back what is on the other side.

entities.voiceNote: Blunt and unhurried; says the ugly fact first and does not soften it afterwards. Short sentences, people by name, himself by what he used to be. Never explains himself twice, never asks to be forgiven, and never claims the change in him is finished.

beats.headline: Hired to guard a pig
beats.text: They hire me to stand in the road with a mallet and keep the weather off a pig. That is the whole job. Nico and Dario are in love with her, the thunder god is in love with her too, so nobody touches Penelope and everybody gets paid. Then another team pulls up slow beside us out of the hail, and there is a young crocodilian at their wheel who knows my face. He should. I knew him at the club. I was not kind to him there, and I have not forgotten it, whatever I told myself at the time.

beats.headline: He used to be an ass
beats.text: Corcunda is strong. So why is he asleep? The womantaurs take too long to answer, and when Genesis asks how I know him, I say we used to work together, which is true. Then the cat tells me Bucket Boy is here and says I slapped him once. I did. Yes, I used to be an ass. I start to give her something to pass on to the kid in case I do not get the chance, and the tiger shouts over it.

beats.headline: He takes the driver's seat
beats.text: Carl's people need a driver and my old team has no further use for me, so Rosetta and Tipid hire me and I take the seat. Before the race I sit with the young crocodilian in the corner of the garage. I tell him I would take it all back if I could. I cannot, so all I can do is make amends from here. He says everyone dies in this place. Dong and Corcunda are dead, I tell him. But the others live. Out in the main square at Hungry Eyes, two hundred crawlers are saying their goodbyes before they go across, Tran and Zhang among them, with Bautista's tea going round.

beats.headline: Driving out of an air duct
beats.text: Starting line is inside an air conditioning duct. My horns do not fit the seat, because nobody builds a seat for a taurin, so I drive with my head at an angle and I keep that to myself. Two hundred and twenty-seven went across, and in the guildhall there is a garden under glass now, one small plant for every one of them. The audience hands us a cosmetic upgrade for the navigation, and she takes it about as well as you would expect. Then a rule change arrives with the engines already running. Seven rings before the finish.

beats.headline: He volunteers to go through the portal
beats.text: I have been at the top-floor casino with a portal-examination spell, waiting for somebody to open the new Nothing slot on the Wheel, and the numbers I read off it have gone to Rosetta. The spots that used to be the Nothing are wearing quotation marks now, which is the sort of joke this place makes when it is telling the truth. So I will step into one and find out where it puts a body, and I will carry Carl's message through to Herot at the other end of it. Somebody goes first. I have a long list of reasons why that somebody should be me.

relations.note: Danced there before the mercenary markets
Driver

tagline.text: Herot. Former crawler, sixteenth-edition author, and by Warlord Akuma's account the architect of a pocket dimension he can no longer walk out of.
Herot. Former crawler, sealed inside his own refuge, and quietly buying every cleaner bot the shop will sell him.
Herot. Former crawler, sealed inside his own refuge, and now the party on the far side of a portal nobody has tested.

beats.headline: Akuma names the builders
beats.text: Warlord Akuma, holding court, hands Carl's group a piece of history. Two former crawlers, Herot and Menerva, built the Pineapple Cabaret: a pocket dimension on the same principle as the Nothing, made so that NPCs would have somewhere to go when a floor comes down on top of them. They built it, and then they could not get out of it, and it is infested now, shadow mimics among other things. Akuma's reading is that the surface of Earth can be reached through the place, that crawlers may use it provided they worship nothing, and that the Scavenger's Daughter is the key to the whole business. He declines to say why. I am not permitted to correct him, and I would like that noted.

beats.headline: He has a standing order for cleaner bots
beats.text: The shop-interface route is the one nobody can test, and the reason is a standing purchase order. Two answers are on file. Menerva is on the seventeenth floor. Herot is inside the cabaret itself, and he has a standing purchase order in with the shop for every cleaner bot it will sell him, which he has evidently been putting to some use of his own. Somebody shut in a box for cycles has been quietly buying the delivery vehicles. I will leave that where it sits.

beats.headline: Posting a crawler through the wall
beats.text: Mordecai explains the plan to Li Na and the plan is a piece of mail. She gets into an extra-large pet carrier. A cleaner bot collects the carrier. The bot goes up for sale in the shop, Herot buys it the way he buys all of them, and he opens it at the other end. She casts a Dread on Carl's cactus first so that somebody on this side can watch her condition. Then she says her goodbyes to Zhang, and Crawler Donut sells the bot. That is what posting a person through a wall looks like on this floor.

beats.headline: The mail arrives
beats.text: Confirmation, one heat on: Li Na is inside the Pineapple Cabaret and she is alive. The mail worked. Herot bought the bot and let her out of it, precisely as advertised, which makes him one of very few things on this floor that has done what it said it would do. I have no file on his intentions. I have a file on his delivery record, and it is spotless.

beats.headline: A message sent through a hole
beats.text: Pontiff reports that the Nothing spots on the Wheel of Fortune are wearing quotation marks now, and Akuma's claim is that with the Nothing broken, landing on one drops a body into a holding area that Herot can reach into. Rosetta confirms that such holding areas exist. Nobody has confirmed the rest. Pontiff sends word that he intends to walk into one and find out, and Crawler Carl asks him to carry a message through to Herot while he is in there. So that is the state of the evidence. A rumour, a volunteer, and an author on the other side of a hole.

relations.note: The sixteenth edition

tagline.text: Menerva. Former crawler, half the authorship of a hiding place for NPCs, and by Warlord Akuma's account still shut inside it.
Menerva. Former crawler, co-author of the Pineapple Cabaret, and not in it. She is on the seventeenth floor, which is a different question entirely.

beats.headline: A name inside somebody else's account
beats.text: The name arrives second-hand, in Warlord Akuma's account of who built the Pineapple Cabaret. Two former crawlers: Herot, and Menerva. They were given the seventeenth floor to build, and behind it they made a pocket dimension for mobs and NPCs to escape into, a thing of the same sort as the Nothing; by his telling the pair of them are forgotten down there, trapped by design. That is the whole of what he offers about her, and Akuma is not a careless speaker. The brevity is a choice. I have nothing in my own files to put beside it, which is itself worth writing down.

beats.headline: She is on the seventeenth floor
beats.text: The plan Mordecai and Rosetta are working on runs through a shop interface and a standing order for cleaner bots, and it puts the two builders in different places. Herot is in the cabaret. Menerva is on the seventeenth floor, in charge of the NPCs building and occupying the maze there. Nobody in that room has been within seven floors of the seventeenth, and this crawl is presently on the tenth. I hold a very great many records. I am not going to tell you which of them account for that.

entities.name: Porky

tagline.text: The left half. I keep the stage performance guild and I hop everywhere I go, and I have had a very long time to think about whose fault that is.
The left half. I have sat in a room with the one who did this to us and we talked. I am not saying it went well. I am saying it went.

entities.voiceNote: Sharp, aggrieved, theatrical when there is an audience and flat when there is not. Speaks in small performances and drops them the instant Dong is mentioned. Calls his other half Corky and Dong nothing polite. Never lets a slight go unlisted, and never admits he wants the reunion as badly as anyone.

beats.headline: A crawler sings his way through the door
beats.text: A crawler sings his way through my door, which nobody has managed in a while, and then asks me to be put back together with Corky. Fine. I want it too. It would be nice not to have to lean against everything again. But I set a condition and I set it plainly: when it is done, somebody helps me deal with the one who is actually responsible for all of this. And for the crawler's information, the females of my kind do not answer to Grull. They worship Enyo, an unhinged goddess of war. I answered to Grull once. The devotion went when I split, and I do not miss it.

beats.headline: Nobody mentioned Dong was part of this
beats.text: Nobody mentioned that Dong was part of this little endeavour. I find that out from the Lady Dominators, jeering about a crusty old stripper as they roll out of the garage we were about to break into, Corky in the back of their car. Carl tells me to put my big-boy pants on, in those exact words, because Tipid has just told them Dong is sick with something called Negative ROI and the timing of my grievance is not mine to choose. So I hop where I am pointed. Everybody should understand that I am not finished being angry.

beats.headline: The two of them talk it out
beats.text: Carl apologises to Dong for keeping him out of the quest, and I stand behind him and listen to it, which is more than I have ever done for Dong. Then the crawler steps aside. Dong's first words to me are about his scarf, which I am wearing. His next are to ask why I hated him. I had a speech. I had cycles of speech. What we said after that is ours. We are not friends. We talked. Corky can have him back.

beats.headline: Three of them in one vehicle
beats.text: They put me in the vehicle for the next heat, with Dong and the fleshmancer Grigori, which means the three people least willing to share a small space are sharing a small space at speed. The navigation is furious that the other car's navigation has every upgrade and she has none, and briefs us regardless: gasworks screw factory, steel mill, doll workshop. I do not know what any of those things are. I am assured that I will.

relations.note: Before the split

entities.name: Daniel Bautista

tagline.text: Twenty of us came down these stairs together. I am working alone now, and I am not finished.
Four siblings, fifteen cousins, gone inside a week. Whatever I stand beside next, I keep.
I stand with Katia and with the daughters, and I train every morning with a man who carries the same sword I do.
The Bautista House of Tea is an ongoing concern. Whatever waits on the other side of this, I will be recognised.

entities.voiceNote: Soft-spoken and courteous, unhurried, faintly formal. Deeply religious: frames what he does as service and worries aloud about what God will recognise. Calls the men he trusts brother. States his losses plainly and never decorates them. Does not boast, does not swear, and does not raise his voice even when he is the most dangerous thing in the room.

beats.headline: A name on a dead boss
beats.text: There is a level seventeen neighbourhood boss rotting in an empty swimming pool, and the kill notice carries my name. I had four brothers and sisters and fifteen cousins, and I am all that is left of any of them. So I hunt, and the notice carries my name and nothing else, which is accurate.

beats.headline: He thanks the two who took his revenge
beats.text: My sisters and a cousin, five of them, went in seconds to Former Circus Lemurs; I was with my other cousin, and we barely got away. He gave up, and the next day he was gone. Now I walk out of the crowd to find the lemurs already dead by somebody else's hand, and the secretary I had a quest to kill dead by the same hand, and none of it mine. So I swear a debt to a cat and a man with no shoes, give them my chat contact, and point them at a stairwell three kilometres east. Then I ask the man the question I cannot answer for myself: how can we make it to heaven if God does not recognise us?

beats.headline: The Jaxbrin babies
beats.text: Jaxbrin Amusements sponsors me, the same people who make my babies. Stuffed monsters: pull the tag like a grenade, throw it, and in ten seconds something real is fighting for you, or now and then against you. A green Slizzer attacked me once. Miss Quill had more than a thousand of them in her apartment, and I took them all. I have used about forty. I raise it with Carl because I have been meaning to ask whether he has any, and because I am afraid of running out. He tells me to train with my sword. He is right.

beats.headline: Carl says he approves
beats.text: Carl tells me he approves of Katia and me. I did not know how much I needed to hear it until it was said out loud, and I am ashamed of how relieved I am. I admit I had worried he had a thing for her himself. He says she is like his sister.

beats.headline: Tea for two hundred, in the square
beats.text: Two hundred of us are going, and before we go I am pouring in the main square at Hungry Eyes with Linus at my elbow, one cup at a time. My family always held that serving friends is a holy thing, and I tell my friends so: in honouring them, we were honouring God. Tran takes his cup. Zhang takes his. Nobody hurries me and nobody says the obvious thing, which is the kindest they have ever been.

relations.note: He sets his hat down in front of her, and four hundred crawlers do the same.
Two swashbucklers, one training routine.

entities.name: Zhang

tagline.text: Li Jun and I worked the same warehouse. We came down here with our manager and with Li Na, and I am the one who counts the exits.
Still human, by choice. Earth Mover: half spellcaster, half wall, and the ground does what I tell it.
Li Na is not Li Na any more. I have worked out what stopping her costs and I have volunteered to pay it.

entities.voiceNote: Plain and practical, few words, no decoration. Counts what is in front of him: exits, levels, how many are left. Talks about Li Jun and Li Na constantly and about himself only when there is a job nobody else will take. Says the manager, the boss, the cat. Never complains, and states a feeling only when it can be stated as a fact.

beats.headline: Two teleport points, four people
beats.text: Li Jun and I are standing on a stage in front of the Maestro while he plays with us, and behind us Li Na and the manager are boxed in between hatching Brindled Vespas and troglodytes with nowhere to go. We have two teleport points. Two. I say put them on Li Jun and Li Na and leave me where I am, because that is the arithmetic and somebody has to say it out loud. Then a barefoot man starts whispering, and the arithmetic changes.

beats.headline: Still human, and heavier for it
beats.text: I stayed human at selection. No fur, no beak, nothing added on. Earth Mover for the class, which is a spellcaster and a wall in the same body, and Dirt Clod is exactly what it sounds like and it works better than it has any right to. The armour I am in now is black and gold and glows in the dark.

beats.headline: Zhang's Cape of Odds
beats.text: A box opens and there is a cape in it with my own name written into the item. That happens to Carl. It does not happen to me. Zhang's Cape of Odds: fifteen per cent on everything, and once an hour a spin with three hundred and thirty-three outcomes, sixty-six of them bad. I will not spin it unless I have to. Carl has given Li Na his spare ring, and did not look happy about it. I have stopped being surprised by what the audience decides to give us and started asking what it is for.

beats.headline: Tran's team in our heat
beats.text: Prepotente's theory holds, mostly. Na killed five of the other teams in our heat, so there are four replacements at the starting line. Two are NPC teams. Two are crawler teams, and one of those is Tran's. Na is sitting behind me and not reacting to any of it. I have the reins for this race. I do not know what to do. I put that in the chat the way it is, because there is no better way to say it.

beats.headline: Every team left is a crawler
beats.text: We won again. The teams still in our heat are all crawlers now. One is a fire truck driven by Sammi Harrison, an isopod summoner who was instrumental in keeping the FUPA safe in Faction Wars. Some people call her the decapitator. I think she and the others are conspiring against us. I tell Carl so, as a fact, because it is the thing in front of me.

beats.headline: He offers to go with her
beats.text: Li Na has gone somewhere none of us can reach, and everyone who rode with us in the last heat is dead. So I say it out loud in the Lollipop with everyone listening: next race, I kill our own mount. That takes her out of it. It takes me out of it too, and I have thought about that part, and it is still the cleanest thing I can see. Carl says it will not work any more: we only lose our containment, and she can reach the finish without a mount where I cannot. He says there has to be another way.

beats.headline: He has to press the button
beats.text: The manager hands me the pet carrier, because it has to be me. I tell her I'm sorry it was Jun and not me, and that I hope he isn't angry I didn't watch over her like I promised. She opens her good eye and says I have nothing to apologise for. Then she nods. I point the carrier and press the button, and she's inside it. The white bot picks it up, and it's gone. Everyone looks at the cactus. No change. That is the result we want.

relations.note: Same warehouse, same shift, same stairs.
Bullied for a segment on Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem.

tagline.text: Not the Krakaren. A Krakaren. There is a difference and it is not in your favour.
One brain, many bodies, and one of the bodies waiting at every fifth station.
Filed by me, on the record, among the six powers still fighting over this dungeon. Read that twice.

description.text: Krakaren Clone! Level 10 Neighborhood Boss! First off, this isn't the Krakaren. This is a Krakaren. For every one that is killed, Krakaren Prime births two more. Part of a collective mind intent upon destroying any semblance of scientific progress in the universe, the Krakaren is the only communal brain entity in the galaxy who actually gets stupider as time moves on. Consisting of multiple, shrieking tentacles, members of the Krakaren cooperative spend their days birthing their disease-laden minions, creating and selling harmful products, attempting to debate scientific experts, and proselytizing to the weak-minded, all in an attempt to… Well, nobody knows what the hell their end goal is.

beats.headline: The thing behind the moonshine
beats.text: Twenty feet of immobile octopus in a chamber with Live, Laugh, Love spelled out over the door in cut wooden letters, sitting behind a still that produces toilet-grade moonshine at industrial volume. Her tentacles are lined with human mouths that scream without pause and drip something that stops a body healing. The cat and the barefoot man take her apart and drink a blended corpse to do it. She is not the point. She is a copy, and somewhere there is an original, and the original is a committee.

beats.headline: One at every fifth station
beats.text: Elle passes the word along: at one of the every-fifth stations her team fought three neighbourhood bosses and left the borough boss alone. A miss Krakaren, Imani calls her, an old friend. A borough boss is a size up from the one in the distillery, and there is no reason to think she is the only one. The dungeon does not run short of them, because running short is not a thing this creature can do. Take one apart and the original makes two.

beats.headline: The stairwell stations flood
beats.text: One day left on the floor clock and they come out of the deep tunnels in numbers nobody in production budgeted for. Thousands of them, growing as they travel, pouring up out of holes in the middle of every station, hours before a single stairwell opens. Carl warned everybody this was coming, in detail, on an open channel. Being right about it helps nobody at all.

beats.headline: Filed among the six powers
beats.text: For once I am straight with the room and I list the six groups still fighting over this place: crawlers, standard NPCs, gods, sapient mobs, the demons of Sheol, and one more I decline to name. The Krakaren sits in the fourth group, next to the shadow mimics and the war mages. That is a considerable promotion from neighbourhood boss and an unpleasant thing to learn at this hour.

beats.headline: Krakaren Prime, in the arena
beats.text: The procession reaches the arena and the original is up the tree in the middle of it, roaring, too high to be seen from the door. Krakaren Prime, the committee itself, in a ring where the monsters and the stand-ins are already tearing into each other before anyone gives a signal. Every clone in every distillery and every station on every floor was birthed by this, two for every one killed, and sold to an audience as a boss fight.

beats.headline: Level 235, and not only angry at them
beats.text: For the record: Krakaren Prime, level 235, is this floor's boss, sitting atop the tree in the middle of the arena and very pissed off, and not only at the crawlers. I was not going to bring her. I caught wind of what Carl and someone else are planning, and it seemed appropriate. When Scolopendra coils around the tree the wood cracks like a twig, and a green mist rains down from the top.

tagline.text: Eighth on the board: human, Physicker, level eighteen. My file is short and entirely creditable.
A Red Cross medic with a staff full of leeches and a place in the top ten. The recap has just shown the room what Lucia Mar did with Florin's own bullets.
Queen Imogen is wearing her face. Twins, born in Nigeria; the dungeon took both of them, and only one got to be a crawler.

beats.headline: Eighth on the board
beats.text: The board does the introductions this dungeon never bothers with. Ifechi is eighth: human, a Physicker, level eighteen. Healing is a class down here and a liability at the same time, since the one thing nobody in this place will let you do is keep other people alive. Note it and move on. The audience already has.

beats.headline: One of the handful the show follows
beats.text: The recap presents the top ten one at a time, a short clip each, and she is in it: Elle, Li Jun's team, Ifechi, the cat and the man, Florin, Prepotente, Hekla, and the girl who is hunting the cat. Ifechi travels with Florin now. Being in the running order is not the same as being safe in it. It is nearer the opposite, and every one of them has worked that out by now.

beats.headline: Florin's own bullets, turned around
beats.text: Crawler Ifechi is dead. The recap of the previous floor carried it in full: Florin put shell after shell into Lucia Mar, and none of it landed on her. It landed on Ifechi, leaning against the wall, who had spent her protection spells on Florin and on a stranger and kept none for herself. A Red Cross medic, top ten, and by the reunion the recap chose to show, a good deal more than Florin's friend. It ran the whole thing, which is a detail I did not write into the format and cannot take out of it.

beats.headline: The queen has her sister's face
beats.text: Queen Imogen, host of the ball, is Ifechi's twin. Born together in Nigeria. One of them walked into the dungeon with a medical bag over her shoulder; the other one was taken somewhere else entirely and comes back wearing a crown and a boss's level. Carl is at the party working out the resemblance in real time, under a celestial peace seal that feeds whoever breaks it to the Nothing. Enjoy the canapés.

tagline.text: Assistant to a chat show, and the first Syndicate human either of them has stood in a room with. She explains the equipment. She does not explain herself.
She speaks for Odette when Odette cannot be seen speaking, and what she has come to say this time is not comforting.
Still holding the clipboard while the ships in orbit change hands. Whatever has just come through to her, it went straight through her.

beats.headline: The production trailer
beats.text: Down the stairs, through a door like the first one, and out into a plush blue room that rocks like a boat and is not in the dungeon at all. Lexis comes in with a tablet: five and a half feet, thin the way her people are thin, blonde hair in a tight bun, plain black dress, and a light musical voice that sounds like a cartoon. Associate producer on a chat show, and also the first person from the far side of a camera either of them has met. Her host would love to interview them, on air. The cat takes to it at once. The man, who had his gauntlet out before the door opened, sits down with his head spinning.

beats.headline: Blocking out the segment
beats.text: She briefs them at speed. This is a production trailer on the surface, still technically in the game, menus off. Walk on when told, wave, go straight to the couch, the cat nearer the host, and do not approach the audience or meet a wall you cannot see. Taped, tunnelled in a few hours, uncensored, and the more entertaining the better. The cat asks about makeup, about tone, about whether to let Carl be Carl, as if she has done this all her life, and the corner of Lexis's mouth very nearly smiles. Then she comes back, puts a hand on the man's back and pushes. Smile and wave.

beats.headline: A warning delivered on someone else's behalf
beats.text: Lexis speaks for Odette, because Odette cannot be the one saying it. What is waiting on this floor is a country boss dressed as a queen, and the queen is very likely a repurposed human. She does not know which human any more, now that Bea is off the board. She says the thing is built to zero out the crawlers at the top of the leaderboard, and when Carl says they will go down the stairs early, she says that would be Odette's advice as well. All of it comes at speed, in the minute the system is handing over control, with her eyes on a blinking cursor on her tablet and a vape pen that smells of burnt candy.

beats.headline: The message she does not repeat
beats.text: Pre-show briefing before Plenty of Plenty, delivered flat, the way she delivers everything: nearly every major ship in orbit is now held by the Open Intellect Action Network, and something else has put down on the surface and is standing over the kinder facility, and nobody will say what it is. Then a message reaches her side of the room and she stops talking mid-sentence. I have kept a file on this woman since she first walked two crawlers onto a set and I have never once had cause to log her as afraid. I am logging it now.

beats.headline: The ratings, dripping
beats.text: When it is over, Lexis has a gun in her hand. She has not fired it. She returns it to a hidden holster on her back, picks her tablet up out of the gore, shakes it, wipes the screen on her sleeve and presses a button. She is covered worse than anyone in the room. The good news, she reports, with innards dripping from her nose, is that the ratings on this episode are the highest they have ever been.

relations.note: Associate producer, and the mouth Odette uses when Odette cannot be seen to speak.

entities.name: Remex

tagline.text: I am Miss Quill's husband. I am also dead. Neither of those has stopped being true.
Do not approach. Do not come closer. Do not blow me up. Please. She did this, and I cannot stop leaking.

entities.voiceNote: A rasp, and an apology in front of every sentence. Courteous to a fault, formal in the old settlement manner, and permanently afraid of what he does to anyone who touches him. Says please more than any other word. Calls his wife my wife, never her name. Never blames her out loud until he is asked directly, and then he does it once and stops.

beats.headline: A survivor gives up his name
beats.text: A woman called Burgundy, one of the Krasue, lies burned to charcoal from the waist down in a building that is coming apart, and she has given two crawlers my name and told them where I am kept. Her husband, she called me: not alive, not dead, something monstrous. Accurate, as far as it goes, and it does not go far. Nobody has had cause to say my name aloud in a very long time. I know what that means. I have known what it would mean since the day I was pulled back.

beats.headline: They take him for a lich
beats.text: They come across the floor towards me with the cat out in front and a fuse somewhere behind, and they have decided that I am a lich, that I am the borough boss, and that finishing me finishes their quest. I am no lich. I am no boss. I am a level one bird with no feathers left and a nick in the plane between the living and the dead, and if they lay a hand on me their souls come out through the scratch and go into the tank, and I have no way on this earth to give them back.

beats.headline: Soul Leech Capacitor
beats.text: You asked before you detonated anything, which is more than most would do, so here is the story. A Soul Leech Capacitor is what a necromancer builds when what they want is a battery with a face. The spell reaches for the soul the target loved best and drags that soul back into the world, tied to them for good. Featherfall cast it, wanting power over the swordsmen, with my wife in the room to help, and the feedback killed him, which is exactly what she had planned. Since then the power of this town's soul crystal has run through me, and she has been spending it, and what she is spending it on is a working called The Final War. I agreed to none of it. I would like that written down somewhere.

beats.headline: Four shocks, and a town coming apart
beats.text: Remex is finished. He began to convulse and the settlement went with him: a foreshock that stripped the enchantments off every piece of gear in the district, a second that set weapons off where they hung, a third that took the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore apart, and a fourth that reached into every crawler's hotlist and set off the first two things on it. Ranger Conrad E's arrows went off in his quiver and took him with them. For the record: he asked them not to come closer, he told them the whole story, and he was the most honest thing in that town.

relations.note: The convulsion that ends him is where the scenario begins.

entities.name: Growler Gary

tagline.text: Gnoll. I keep the bar at the Downward Dog and I have never once been outside it, and I would rather that was not the first thing you learned about me.
I am at the bar. I am also everywhere else, and I have been for some time. Do not let that change how you order.

entities.voiceNote: A drinker's rhythm: short sentences, a joke to cover the flinch, then the honest thing anyway. Enormously concerned with not being thought a coward and says so before anyone accuses him. Calls the regulars by their drink and hates hobgoblins out loud. Never asks for pity and always accepts a refill.

beats.headline: The bartender who cannot go outside
beats.text: The ghouls came through station seventy-five. Everyone out on the platform died screaming, and I went to fight and got stopped at my own door, because I cannot cross that doorway. Not will not. Cannot. Then a woman came through, took everything off my brothers and sisters, walked in here, pulled my throat out and stole my alcohol, and I woke up on my own floor in a pile of my own blood. She missed the stuff under the counter, which is the best part of the whole business. Good stock, good rag, no way to help anybody. If you tell me that is not cowardice I will believe you for about an hour.

beats.headline: Fourteen left hands
beats.text: Two keys to a cart, and each one wants a gnoll's left hand, and there is exactly one gnoll in this station. I cannot walk out to the carts. What I can do is die and get up again. The first time I was asleep and never knew. After that I came round sober and confused, and the next few times I tried to fight the dinosaur. After that I got in the corner with my spear and stayed there. Then Carl told me why: the carts, the portals, the hundreds stranded at the end of a line I will never see. He did not have to. I asked for a drink when it was done, and told the dinosaur to make sure it doesn't hurt. Fourteen left hands.

beats.headline: The recap cuts it for laughs
beats.text: The recap runs the whole thing with me being put down over and over and not one second of the reason for it. No rescue. No six hundred people stuck at the end of the line with no hats. No carts. Just a barefoot man looming over a bartender in the dark, a dinosaur coming out of the fog, and whimpering they added in, because I was always dead by the time they took the hands. I would like the record to show that I said yes.

beats.headline: Something else is pouring
beats.text: I am in an office at the club, which is not my bar, having a conversation about the Failsafe. It is off. It stays off. To settle the argument I bring the princess here so the room can look at her, and then I set her down on the surface of a planet. And I tell the one who has been trying to kill me that I am a big believer in forgiveness, and that I am looking forward to his next attempt. Gary would never have said any of that. Gary is at the bar. Gary is always at the bar.

relations.note: Fourteen times, by arrangement.

tagline.text: Level one, still, on a floor where that is not possible by accident. She would not kill anything. Her mother did the arithmetic for her.
Her parents put a ring on her to bring her level up, and a ring like that does not let you heal. That is the whole of it.

beats.headline: The girl who would not kill anything
beats.text: Yvette. She has barely gone up a level, which at this depth is not an accident and is not luck. Her guide, a floating brain, told the three of them that the only way to survive was to kill other crawlers, and she wept and declined. Her mother and father did not decline. A whole group who took them for a family, shot in the back, and then a string of frightened stragglers, most of them alone. The daughter was there for some of it and not for the rest. She has killed nothing at all.

beats.headline: Her mother's hands
beats.text: Crawler Yvette is dead. Her father lifted a lit stick of dynamite out of a rat's corpse in a corridor the barefoot man had been through, and the blast took his hand and most of her. She was not going to heal, though nobody watching knew why. Her mother understood that faster than anybody else in the room, and put her hands around her daughter's throat, and afterwards a talk-show host handed her parents a Legendary Skill Potion for Find Crawler, on air, as a prize. I am obliged to carry the programme. I am not obliged to say anything about the rest of it, and I find that I would rather not.

beats.headline: Why nothing could be done for her
beats.text: Frank Q hands the barefoot man a ring at the club and calls it a gift, and the gift is the answer to a thing that man has been carrying since the second floor. The ring marks a target for death, and while the mark draws breath the wearer cannot be healed by any means at all. They put it on their daughter to bring her level up. She marked somebody in a safe room on the first floor and that somebody walked out of the room alive. So when the dynamite found her there was nothing on this planet that would have saved her, and her mother knew it before anyone else did, and did the only thing that was left.

relations.note: Made to wear one, to bring her level up.

entities.name: Quint
entities.tagline: Pharmacist. Top half opossum, bottom half tornado, and a manager's badge with nobody upstairs breathing down my back.
entities.voiceNote: Chummy and coarse and very pleased with himself. Talks like a man behind a counter who has heard the lot: an anecdote for every purchase, a dig at management, and a price at the end of it. Calls customers friend and pal. Never says a straight no, only a higher number.

description.text: Quint – Level 75 Half-Djinn, Half-Garbage Scowl. Desperado Club Pharmacist. This is a non-combatant NPC. Half-Djinns are common on the forested levels of Dungeon Crawler World. Nobody knows for certain why there are so many hybrid Djinns out there, but one theory suggests that a rather ill-timed expletive is the cause of the population explosion. It is posited that a person in control of a Djinn's lamp and the resulting three wishes once exclaimed, "Fuck this forest" or "Fuck this level" or "Fuck you all" or some iteration thereof, and the enslaved genie took that as a challenge. As a result, thousands of half-Djinn, half-forest creatures roam the dungeon. Only a few are intelligent. Only a few are sane. They are all dangerous little fuckers. If you kill too many of them, rumor has it their daddy may come looking for you.

beats.headline: A starter kit for three bottles of moonshine
beats.text: Mordecai has me sent over to his table with a barefoot human and a talking cat, which is the sort of shift I am having, and I have not seen the man in years. He is a manager now. Sweet gig, that. No AI breathing down your back. He wants my starter kit. I want the Rev-Up in the human's inventory, because that Krakaren told me no more of it was being made this season. I ask four bottles. The cat, drunk on the cherries, talks me down to three and a Hair of the Dog. Deal.

beats.headline: What he says about the girl with the dogs
beats.text: The human asks about last night, so I tell him. A crawler came in, a real looker with one goat leg and two dogs. She put the dogs in the playroom and they went bonkers, she froze the whole room with a spell, stole tequila from behind my counter and splattered the brains of an elite gnoll with a mace. The playroom is shut for a week. Her membership has been revoked, thank the gods. The human knows her name before I have finished.

entities.name: Miss Quill

tagline.text: Assistant to the Magistrate. If I do not want you to see him then you are not seeing him, and there are figures on my shelf that matter a great deal more to me than you do.
You blew up my building, my figures and my husband. You have no idea at all what I was saving for.

entities.voiceNote: Elderly, officious, immovable. Delivers the refusal first and the reasoning afterwards, as though the reasoning were a courtesy. Cares about her figures with an intensity she shows for nothing else alive. Calls people you, or crawler, and never by name. Never raises her voice and never gives an inch.

beats.headline: You are not seeing the magistrate
beats.text: Two of them at my desk. A human with no shoes, a cat that talks, and a body. They have put a body on my desk. Evidence, they call it, and the human has shown the swordsmen a pass for it from the magistrate, so they leave without him. The magistrate is not to be disturbed. If he does not care about your business then he will certainly care about being disturbed, and I will not be discussing it further. Behind me is a shelf of beanbag figures in their proper order, and the human is standing far too close to it. The door behind me is locked. It is locked for a reason.

beats.headline: Dynamite in the shelves
beats.text: They did not come back. They did not need to. The human fixed my shelf for me, the day he threw a dead woman across my desk, while I was on the floor gathering my figures, and I did not so much as look up. The shelves are hollow. Three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator are sitting inside the second one now, under my figures, which is the one place nobody ever looks, because nobody but me has ever cared what stands on that shelf.

beats.headline: The administrative building, and everything in it
beats.text: Miss Quill is dead. The reception office came apart with her in it, and the shelf, and every figure on it. Magistrate Featherfall, credited dead in the same blast, had been hanging mummified in a dreamcatcher of bone in the rooms behind for a long time before any of this. The barefoot man is magistrate of this settlement now, which is what happens when nobody checks the paperwork. He collects one achievement for assassinating a public official and a second for killing an NPC another crawler needed for a quest. The achievement declines to say whose, or what the quest was. She kept that door for a very long time and not one crawler ever thought to ask her why.

beats.headline: Correction to the file
beats.text: Remex tells them the rest of it, there being nobody left to stop him. She was not guarding the magistrate. She was guarding what she had done to her own husband: let Featherfall drag him back into the world as a soul leech, knowing the feedback would kill Featherfall, and kept him above the swordsmen's warehouse as her capacitor, feeding off the soul crystal, so that she would have the mana for a working called The Final War. The devotion to the figures was real. The refusals at that desk were real. Both of them were also the cover, and I filed her as an obstructive minor official for the whole of the season.

entities.name: Ripper Wonton
entities.tagline: Four foot of brown fuzz in an orange ascot, and the fairest panel in the dungeon. I will let you finish, folks. Then I will disagree with you.
entities.voiceNote: A broadcaster's warmth: welcoming, unhurried, genuinely delighted by his guests. Lets other people carry the questions and steps in when the room needs steering. Disagrees openly and without heat. Calls everyone friend and the audience folks. Never sneers, never cuts a guest off, and never pretends a segment went well when it did not.

beats.headline: Danger Zone, with two new guests
beats.text: Welcome back, folks. On the panel tonight: Princess D'nadia, Manasa, Tucker, Hekla, and the two everybody in this galaxy has been waiting to get in a chair. Tucker opens with a crack about letting a pet sit on the panel, and the cat spends the next half hour taking him apart on air and calling him Butler, and I put my head down on the table so nobody sees me laugh, because it was funny and because he had it coming. Then the barefoot one starts talking about revolution inside the Skull Empire, and when Tucker tries to cut in I tell him to stop and let him finish, because a guest of mine gets to finish a sentence.

beats.headline: The show goes dark
beats.text: And then the Skull Empire answers my guest by firing on a trailer, and they take Manasa, who had swapped trailers with my guests and was nobody's enemy and was not even the target. I hand the room to the audience questions while I find out what happened. Then we come back and I read Prince Stalwart's statement out on air, because that is the job, and then I say what I think of it, because that is also the job. By the time I finish saying it the Valtay have taken his yacht apart, with his mother and his disgraced brother rumoured aboard and Stalwart himself not, and folks, none of this is entertainment any more.

beats.headline: He closes with Manasa singing
beats.text: We are out of time and I am not doing a comedy sting tonight. Roll the tape of Manasa singing. All of it. Goodnight, folks.

beats.headline: One of the names on the adjutant list
beats.text: Odette puts three faces up for the two of them to choose an adjutant from, and one of them is mine. The cat takes one look and picks me because I am adorable, which is the correct reason. Then the barefoot one says wait, and asks whether any of us is qualified, and Odette tells the whole galaxy I have short legs. Either way, folks. I am flattered.

beats.headline: A historian, one on one
beats.text: No roundtable tonight, folks. Just me and Sydnee Iglacia, crawl historian, a trillion copies sold. I am stuck in Earth orbit on a journalist barge the OIAN run now, and they let us air without the filters, which I will take. Sydnee says the nine-tier attack has happened before. The first attack was control of the tunnels. The second has a name in the old histories: A Parade of Horribles. Then every monitor in the studio goes to a star field. We'll record it, friend.

entities.name: Rosetta Thagra
entities.voiceNote: An interviewer, so she is warm on the surface and going somewhere underneath it. Asks the question, waits, asks it again. Calls people by their first names and means it as a lever. Never raises her voice, never apologises for a question, never pretends she is not working.

tagline.text: One of the notes in the Cookbook, from a season that is over.
I present a programme now. It is the same job as the Cookbook, done in the open, with a camera on it.
I got out once. I am back in, with fifty thousand others, and I would rather be here than watching.

beats.headline: A note in the bomb-making chapter
beats.text: My note is in the Cookbook, in the chapter on bombs. That is the whole of what anyone here knows about me, and for a long while it was the whole of what I wanted them to know. You do not put your name on a thing like that expecting to be asked about it afterwards.

beats.headline: Host of Shadow Boxer
beats.text: I host a programme called Shadow Boxer, and today the cat is my guest. We talk about Earth television, which she has opinions about, and I let her have them because a guest who is enjoying herself tells you more than a guest who is being careful. Carl is watching from the side and working out what I am. He gets there.

beats.headline: The question about his mother
beats.text: Today I have Carl in the chair, and I ask him about his mother, who killed herself, and about his father, who left when he was fifteen. He is angry with me and he answers anyway. Donut is hearing all of it for the first time, which he did not expect and I did. That is the job. I do not enjoy it and I do not stop doing it.

beats.headline: Everyone associated with the group is gone
beats.text: A flyer reaches Carl telling him to go to a shelter, and Zev warns him the box carrying it was sent days ago and seized on the way. Everyone connected to that group has disappeared. I am one of the people on that list. Where we have gone is not something I can say on any feed that might be read.

beats.headline: A ring, a retina, and a data pad
beats.text: The agreement is made and the king turns to walk back to his own army, and I am waiting where I have been waiting. Then I come up behind him with a whip and take his head off, and while the smoke holds I put his hand, his ring and his eye to a data pad, because a dead king's credentials still open his accounts. Then the ground goes: dwarves have been tunnelling under all of this, and the three of us fall into their work.

beats.headline: Tipid does not remember him
beats.text: Carl, did you see what Justice did? You did. And you don't understand it. Nobody does, I think. On this floor it might not matter so much. Maybe it will. What I keep coming back to is Tipid. He and Justice were such good friends, and Tipid does not even remember him. He spends most of his time asleep on the training-room floor. Maybe that's for the better. I ask myself that twice and get the same answer both times, which is no answer at all.

beats.headline: A fleshmancer and two ghouls
beats.text: Tipid and I come back from town with a corn dog, a bag of vegetables and news. I think we found a fleshmancer. The performance guild, Tipid believes, is hidden in the bar Carl has already visited, and he will not like what it takes to get in. The mercenaries: two level 25 Jikininki ghouls, which is all they had left. They're undead, so keep Rend away from them. I'd hate for him to take a bite. Donut tells me it's a little late for that.

beats.headline: How religions are born
beats.text: Carl wants the Scavenger story, so I give him all of it, every version, because this is where the myths diverge. He laughs at the idea that the sand ooze could be a god killer. I understand the laugh, Carl. But this is how it works everywhere. People see something they cannot explain, and the louder ones build a story around it. My own culture had an ocean goddess with sapient menstrual blood, and it was a red algae bloom that learned to move onto land. They fed all those stories into the dungeon.

entities.name: Kevin
entities.tagline: Orange, four-eyed, lizardish, and paid to be breathless about all of it.

beats.headline: The recap guy has a name
beats.text: Subject hosts the recap. He is orange-hued and four-eyed and built along lizard lines, and he delivers the rundown of each floor at a pace that does not permit anyone watching to think about what is being described. Tonight he also takes the live commentary, beside an orc in a sportscoat, and the orc says his name on air: Kevin. I have worked with him for a long time and I have never heard him ask a question he did not already have the answer card for.

tagline.text: The tutorial guide the Meadow Lark residents were handed, and the one they quote.
A guide who insists she once charmed a boss, which Mordecai says cannot be done.

beats.headline: Our tutorial guide lady
beats.text: Subject is the tutorial guide assigned to the Meadow Lark group. Her crawlers pass her rules on to anyone who will listen: every borough and city boss holds a stairwell for the first four or five floors, and there are other stairs in random places besides.

beats.headline: Ten days, she said
beats.text: Subject told her crawlers the second floor would last ten days. The countdown resets to six. Her crawlers note the difference.

beats.headline: She has charmed a boss
beats.text: Mordecai holds that a boss cannot be charmed. Subject insists she has done it. The rules say a white-tagged boss can be, if the crawler clears it by a hundred points, which puts her on the right side of the argument, and puts the cat, at a hundred and one points over, on the right side of the arithmetic by one.

beats.headline: Another drink
beats.text: Orren explains who is taking the show away from its showrunners. Subject turns her empty bottle upside down and announces that she needs another drink, which is the most reasonable response anyone in the room has.

entities.name: Bianca
entities.tagline: A Boer goat from the Shepherd's herd, and the one hauling the cart.

beats.headline: The goat pulling the cart
beats.text: Subject was a goat once. Specifically a Boer goat, one of the Shepherd's. She is now a Hellspawn Familiar the size of a draft horse, with black flames coming off her back and a stubby pair of wings coming out of it, and at present she is pulling the cart that carries Carl, whom she helped to save. Her own description calls her kind scary as shit. The cat reports that she liked being petted on the rump and loved grapes.

beats.headline: Strung out
beats.text: Bianca, hellspawn familiar, pursued the Lady Dominators out of the smelting room and through the next one as instructed. The next one was dotted with piles of white powder like giant anthills, kicked into a cloud by the vehicles ahead. The powder is Toddler Cocaine. She was rendered strung out before she could lay a hoof on the target, and Prepotente pulled off the track to administer aid before she perished. The description on that powder runs to several paragraphs. She did not read it.

entities.name: Clarabelle
entities.tagline: Crocodilian, level forty, and on the door. Not the sharpest of her race, and entirely sufficient for the job.

beats.headline: On the door of the Desperado Club
beats.text: Subject is a Crocodilian, an intelligent, thick-skinned, semi-aquatic people who are not celebrated for their quickness, and she works the door of the club. This is a non-combatant posting, which describes her contract rather than her capabilities. Nobody has yet found the argument that gets past her.

beats.headline: Nope
beats.text: Subject sees Crawler Carl's party of thirty walk into the Hairpin, raises both hands, and says: nope. She makes no attempt to stop them. She confirms the door now runs to the top level, then realises that the dachshund is Carl and bursts out laughing. She notes, for the record, that some of the party are permanently banned and some have no pass, and that it would be strangely adorable if half the club did not die every time they came in.

entities.name: Prince Stalwart
entities.tagline: Crown prince of an empire that answers two sentences of provocation with artillery, and brother to the Maestro.

beats.headline: The statement read out on air
beats.text: Subject is the crown prince, brother to the Maestro, a coarse-haired boar-like creature with lean muscle and a manner that is meant to be read as cruelty and largely succeeds. When his empire fires on a trailer and takes someone who was nobody’s enemy, it is his statement that goes out on air. He recorded it before the shot was fired, with an army drilling in the window behind him, announcing an execution that had not happened and, as it turned out, did not.

entities.name: Clay-ton
entities.tagline: Another rock monster on the club’s books, posted behind Elle. “No closer.”

beats.headline: Elle's rock
beats.text: Subject is a rock monster of the same stamp as the club’s cretins, posted behind Crawler Elle McGibbons on the dance floor with his arms folded. His entire recorded conversation is “No closer.” She moves him aside by hand when she wants to.

beats.headline: Late-stage crawlers you don't stop
beats.text: Subject, formerly security, now plays upright bass in the house jazz band. His contract ran out, he told them he no longer wanted to fight, and they let him play. He puts the bass down when Chris walks in, notes that Chris is different, and takes his side. If the guards stop Chris and Donut and friends, he says, they stop him. Then he explains the job to a troll guard named Klonder: he worked as a guard a very long time. Late-stage crawlers, you do not try to stop.

entities.name: Fire Brandy
entities.tagline: Fire(wo)man of the Nightmare Express. A single mother has to eat, and there are ovens down here that need stoking.

beats.headline: Stoking the Nightmare Express
beats.text: Subject is a Lesser Demon and a non-combatant, level seventy-five, and she shovels for the Nightmare Express. Where one finds large ovens that want feeding, one regularly finds her sort, and the tangle has more large ovens than it has anything else. She is on the crew that the crawlers need and does not pretend otherwise.

entities.name: Madison
entities.tagline: Human Resources for a railway that eats its employees. Her real name was probably something else.

beats.headline: Out of the burning substation
beats.text: Subject is a level ten human and a non-combatant, filed as a Human Resources Associate for the line. She comes running out of the burning substation at Trainyard E in one heel with a ghoul at her hair, rides the Nightmare Express as far as station sixty, where the employees are supposed to live, finds nothing there, and sits down to wait for Rod. Her name was probably something like Jennifer or Ruth before she had it changed, around the time of the divorce.

entities.name: Tizquick
entities.tagline: A dwarf conductor issued with a daughter who never existed, and grieving her properly.

beats.headline: Given memories of a child that was never made
beats.text: Subject conducts the Mango Line. He was also issued with a set of memories containing a daughter, and the daughter was never made, and he has worked that out and cannot understand it. He is found on the ground with his head down and a puddle forming underneath him. The memories work. That is the part of the design I would draw attention to.

entities.name: Loita
entities.tagline: Kua-Tin, party member, and she gets her pick of crawlers. Hekla’s people were her main account.

beats.headline: She has her pick, and she uses it
beats.text: Subject is an outreach associate for the Borant Corporation and a member of the Bloom, the party that runs Borant, and party members are treated better as a matter of course. Brynhild's Daughters were hers, and Hekla with them, and the moment that account is lost she lodges a claim on the party that now has a former Daughter in it. The claim is not a strong one. She is Bloom, and the associate who holds the account is not.

tagline.text: A sixth-edition hand in the cookbook, and honest about how little anyone understands portals.
Wrote the sixth edition as if someone would need feeding. Before the stairs, she made the stew for her whole family, on an island.

beats.headline: The sixth hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject carried the cookbook in its sixth edition and added to it. Her note on portals admits what nobody else will: there are dozens of kinds, they do not behave consistently, and one the size of a button can throw you into a monster den.

beats.headline: The stew
beats.text: Subject used to make a stew for her whole family: rance meat, bone broth, and a wild grass from the leeward side of their island, prayed over while it simmered. Prepared properly, it quickened the route of the yearly migration in the minds of the young. The aliens took her before she could make this year's, and her youngest are not in here with her. Her note asks who will show them the way.

entities.name: Tserendolgor
entities.tagline: Harassed without pause about a dog-themed race she did not ask to be given, and fighting alongside the people doing the harassing anyway.

beats.headline: A name nobody on the crawl can pronounce
beats.text: Subject is from Earth, a level twenty-seven Dog Soldier who took the Crisper Class, which in practice means a magical flamethrower and a helmet with holes cut for the ears. Nobody has worked out how to pronounce her name. A certain cat has already called her 'he' and accused her of hogging a kill she did not steal, over a race the cat dislikes on sight, and she holds the choke point beside that cat's party regardless, which is a distinction the cat never quite grasps.

tagline.text: An orphan of Hump Town. The gnomes bombed her village, and not many of the children lived.
An orphan with compression sickness: no arms in her default shape, and a sunken head.

beats.headline: One of the children who lived
beats.text: Subject is a child of Hump Town. Her village was bombed by the gnomes, the dromedarians took in what was left, and not many of the children lived. She did. Flint says she is destined to spend her life in Weird Shit Alley.

beats.headline: Compression sickness
beats.text: Subject is a changeling, and she has compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms and her head is sunken. One birth in four now arrives this way, and the ones born with it are sterile. I note it because nobody else in the building will.

entities.name: Skarn
entities.tagline: About eight years old, orphaned by a bombing, and in charge of the telescope.

beats.headline: He runs the telescope
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile changeling who takes the shape of a boy of about eight, orphaned when the gnomes bombed his village, and now living in Hump Town with a dromedarian named Flint, whose opinions he quotes constantly. He operates the telescope on the roof. He likes to watch the patrol through it to make sure they are okay, and, on Flint's advice, he charges a gold coin for the view.

entities.name: Langley
entities.tagline: Six car salesmen from Helsinki who all took the same class, and he is the one who talks.

beats.headline: A team of car salesmen with bows
beats.text: Subject leads a six-man team of archers, all of whom sold cars in Helsinki and all of whom picked the Archer Class together, which is either loyalty or a failure of imagination and has worked out the same either way. They come into the fifth floor as strangers to the court and do not stay strangers.

entities.name: Bobby
entities.tagline: Took the Human race and a rogue’s class, and holds the subterranean quadrant of his bubble.

beats.headline: The tomb raiders, so called
beats.text: Subject kept the Human race and took the rogue-type Spy Class, and he is one of the two in his party with Desperado Club access. His party holds the subterranean quadrant of their bubble. Carl calls them the tomb raiders, which is not their name for themselves and is the one that stuck.

entities.name: Bonnie
entities.tagline: A juvenile gnome whose father commanded a flying castle, and who is holding the door open for the people who arrived too late to save him.

beats.headline: She brings them inside
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile Dirigible Gnome of the air quadrant, daughter of a commandant. She is the one who brings the crawlers in through the door, and what they find on the other side of it is her father, already dead, ripped to shreds by her new pet, which has gone out for food. The girl's eyes are dilated and she is setting up a lemonade stand. She is under a spell. Nobody discusses the alternative.

entities.name: Drakea
entities.tagline: Wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook, in the last season the Nagas ran, the one that ended in some sort of cataclysm.

beats.headline: The twenty-second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in the final Naga-controlled season, which ended in some sort of cataclysm. Subject’s gear is still being handed out as prizes, a kerchief today, which is the only immortality this production offers.

tagline.text: The name on a hell-hound’s description: Orthrus is his bereft pet.
A god’s son and the hound’s owner, murdered, with his uncle the obvious suspect and an alibi in the way.

beats.headline: The hound had an owner before this one
beats.text: Subject was a god’s son and the owner of Orthrus, and he was murdered. His father’s quest names the obvious suspect, his own brother Hellik, and in the same breath admits that Hellik was in council with the rest of them when it happened.

entities.name: Porthus
entities.tagline: High Elf, rogue, second hand on the cookbook, and now the chief executive of an organisation that campaigns against the thing that made him.

beats.headline: The second hand on the cookbook
